title: [agoge-forger] GH#63 — Migrate SFTTrainer to TRL 1.4 SFTConfig
description:
## Context

**P0 — train path is broken on the locked stack.** `uv.lock` pins `trl==1.4.0` (and `transformers==5.12.1`), but `src/agoge_forger/train/trainer.py` still builds `SFTTrainer` with the pre–TRL 1.x kwargs. Every real `agoge train-qlora` / `train-lora` run dies at trainer construction; unit tests stay green because nothing instantiates `SFTTrainer`.

Verified in local `.venv` (`trl==1.4.0`):

```text
TypeError: SFTTrainer.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'dataset_text_field'
```

Broken call site (`_build_sft_trainer`):

```python
SFTTrainer(
    model=model,
    train_dataset=dataset,
    dataset_text_field=config.dataset_text_field,  # removed from SFTTrainer.__init__
    max_seq_length=config.training.max_seq_length,  # removed; now SFTConfig.max_length
    tokenizer=tokenizer,  # renamed → processing_class
    args=training_args,  # currently transformers.TrainingArguments
)
```

`_build_training_args` still imports and constructs bare `transformers.TrainingArguments`. Installed TRL expects SFT-specific fields on `trl.SFTConfig` (subclass of `TrainingArguments`). Inspected surface:

| Concern | Pre-1.x (current code) | TRL 1.4.0 (installed) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Sequence length | `SFTTrainer(max_seq_length=…)` | `SFTConfig(max_length=…)` |
| Text column | `SFTTrainer(dataset_text_field=…)` | `SFTConfig(dataset_text_field=…)` |
| Tokenizer | `tokenizer=` | `processing_class=` |
| Args type | `TrainingArguments` | Prefer `SFTConfig` |

`SFTTrainer.__init__` params of interest: `model`, `args`, `train_dataset`, `processing_class`, `peft_config`, `formatting_func` (no `dataset_text_field` / `max_seq_length` / `tokenizer`).

YAML / pydantic surface stays stable — do **not** rename experiment keys:

* `dataset_text_field` on `ExperimentConfig` (`src/agoge_forger/config.py`)
* `max_seq_length` on `TrainingConfig` (same module; also used by `preflight.py` VRAM risk)
* Example configs: `configs/smoke_test.yaml`, `configs/local_rtx5080_16gb.yaml`, etc.

Entry points: `train/qlora.py` and `train/lora.py` both call `run_training(config)` only.

## Repo / surfaces

| Path | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/trainer.py` | `_build_training_args`, `_build_sft_trainer`, `run_training` — **primary fix** |
| `src/agoge_forger/config.py` | `ExperimentConfig` / `TrainingConfig` YAML mapping (`dataset_text_field`, `max_seq_length`) — keep keys |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/qlora.py`, `lora.py` | Thin wrappers → `run_training` |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/preflight.py` | Reads `config.training.max_seq_length` for OOM risk (no TRL API) |
| `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` | `trl>=0.8.0` declared; lock resolves **1.4.0** |
| `tests/` | **No** trainer construction coverage today (gap tracked by [rmems/agoge-forger#66](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-212/agoge-forger-gh66-regression-test-trainer-construction-vs-installed) / GH#66) |
| `.github/workflows/pr_quality_gate.yml` | `pytest tests/` — currently cannot catch this |

## Implementation plan

1. In `trainer.py`, replace `from transformers import TrainingArguments` with `from trl import SFTConfig, SFTTrainer` (or keep both only if needed).
2. Rewrite `_build_training_args` to return `SFTConfig(...)` with existing training fields:
   * Shared: `output_dir`, `per_device_train_batch_size`, `gradient_accumulation_steps`, `learning_rate`, `num_train_epochs`, `bf16`, `logging_steps`, `save_strategy`, `save_steps`, `save_total_limit`, `save_safetensors`, `seed`, `gradient_checkpointing`
   * SFT-specific: `max_length=config.training.max_seq_length`, `dataset_text_field=config.dataset_text_field`
3. Rewrite `_build_sft_trainer` to pass only supported kwargs:
   * `model=…`, `train_dataset=…`, `processing_class=tokenizer`, `args=training_args`
   * Drop `dataset_text_field`, `max_seq_length`, `tokenizer` from the trainer call
4. Confirm `_finalize_training_run` still works: today it uses `trainer.tokenizer` — verify against TRL 1.4 (may need `trainer.processing_class` or equivalent).
5. Keep YAML key names stable; map only at the TRL boundary.
6. Pair with [rmems/agoge-forger#66](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-212/agoge-forger-gh66-regression-test-trainer-construction-vs-installed) regression test so CI fails on future TRL kwargs churn (acceptance also listed on GH#63).
7. Grep docs for old trainer kwarg names; update only if they document `dataset_text_field` / `max_seq_length` as *SFTTrainer* constructor args (config YAML docs stay).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `run_training` builds `SFTTrainer` without `TypeError` on installed `trl` 1.x (verified: current failure is `dataset_text_field`)
- [ ] Sequence length and text field still flow from experiment YAML (`max_seq_length` → `SFTConfig.max_length`, `dataset_text_field` on `SFTConfig`)
- [ ] No remaining uses of removed kwargs: `SFTTrainer(..., tokenizer=)`, `max_seq_length=`, `dataset_text_field=` at the trainer call site
- [ ] Adapter save / tokenizer save path still works after any `trainer.tokenizer` → `processing_class` attribute change
- [ ] Regression test ([rmems/agoge-forger#66](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-212/agoge-forger-gh66-regression-test-trainer-construction-vs-installed) / GH#66) constructs args/trainer entry against **installed** TRL so future upgrades fail CI instead of silent green
- [ ] Docs that name old SFTTrainer kwargs stay accurate if they exist

## Validation

```bash
# API smoke (no GPU weights required if using mocks in tests)
.venv/bin/python -c "from trl import SFTConfig, SFTTrainer; import inspect; print(inspect.signature(SFTTrainer.__init__))"

# Unit suite (must include new trainer construction test once RM-212 lands)
.venv/bin/pytest tests/ -q

# Optional: dry construct args from a real config object
.venv/bin/python -c "
from agoge_forger.train.trainer import _build_training_args
from agoge_forger.config import load_config
# use a local yaml if present; assert type is SFTConfig and max_length is set
"

# Manual GPU path (local only, not required for merge if unit coverage is solid)
# agoge train-qlora configs/smoke_test.yaml
```

## Non-goals

* Unsloth backend (GH#6)
* Full GPU integration train in CI
* Renaming YAML keys (`max_seq_length`, `dataset_text_field`)
* Pinning/changing TRL version beyond making code work with locked 1.4.x
* peft / bitsandbytes / model-load changes outside the trainer construction path

## GitHub

[https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/63](<https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/63>)

Related Linear: [rmems/agoge-forger#66](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-212/agoge-forger-gh66-regression-test-trainer-construction-vs-installed) (GH#66) — CI regression guard for this migration.

P1: CI regression that constructs trainer against installed TRL ([RM-212](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-212/bugci-regression-test-trainer-construction-against-installed-trl) / GH#66). ## Non-goals

title: V1: Define unified wh command and Rust state model
description:
## Summary

Define the complete Rust-only `wh` command surface, lifecycle state machine, JSON output contract, and single authoritative job-state schema.

## Proposed command surface

* `wh doctor`
* `wh discover`
* `wh plan issue owner/repo#123`
* `wh run issue owner/repo#123`
* `wh supervise-pr owner/repo#456`
* `wh watch add|remove|list|check`
* `wh status`
* `wh cleanup <job-id>`

`supervise-pr` is deliberately a runtime primitive, not a duplicate standalone `babysit-pr` skill.

## Acceptance criteria

* Human-readable and `--json` modes for every command.
* Exit code 0 for success, 1 for operational failure, 2 for policy violation.
* One versioned Rust-owned state schema with atomic writes and corruption detection.
* Explicit resumable lifecycle states for issue-to-PR and PR supervision jobs.
* No separate Python watchlist or JSON-envelope implementation required.
* Capability discovery is available for external skills and SDKs.
* Command naming avoids falsely claiming Worktree Hive replaces Codex `babysit-pr`.

title: V1: Record Rust-only architecture and Codex babysit-pr boundary
description:
## Summary

Document the v1 decision to make `wh` the single authoritative Rust runtime and explicitly define the boundary with OpenAI Codex's existing `babysit-pr` skill.

## Context

OpenAI Codex already ships a `babysit-pr` skill for monitoring PRs, CI, flaky retries, review feedback, and continued polling. Worktree Hive should not create a duplicate standalone babysitting skill. It should expose hardened worktree, state, policy, and PR-supervision primitives that existing skills can call.

Reference: [https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/.codex/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md](<https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/.codex/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md>)

## Acceptance criteria

* Add a Rust-only v1 ADR under `docs/adr/`.
* Define `wh` as the only authoritative runtime and mutation boundary.
* Define `SKILL.md` files as thin, platform-facing clients.
* State that Worktree Hive will not publish a separate `pr-babysit` repository for v1.
* Document integration/compatibility expectations for Codex `babysit-pr`.
* Prohibit direct production `git`/`gh` mutation paths outside Rust policy enforcement.
* Define the future Python SDK, if retained, as a thin `wh --json` client only.
* Link the ADR from README and AGENTS.md.

title: Epic: Worktree Hive v1 Rust-only control plane
description:
## Goal

Consolidate Worktree Hive v1 into a single Rust runtime and CLI. Agent skills remain thin clients of `wh`; no production Python orchestrator or second authoritative state machine remains.

## Product boundary

OpenAI Codex already ships a `babysit-pr` skill for persistent PR monitoring, CI diagnosis, flaky retries, and review handling. Worktree Hive will **not** create a competing standalone babysit skill. Instead, `wh` will provide hardened primitives and optional compatibility/integration guidance for existing agent skills, including Codex `babysit-pr`.

Reference: [https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/.codex/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md](<https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/.codex/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md>)

## Target architecture

`Agent skill -> wh CLI -> Rust orchestration -> Rust policy enforcement -> git / gh / OS`

## Acceptance criteria

* All required v1 workflows execute through `wh`.
* One authoritative Rust-owned job/state store.
* Every Git and GitHub mutation passes through Rust policy enforcement.
* Issue-to-draft-PR workflow is implemented in Rust.
* PR supervision primitives are implemented without publishing a duplicate babysit skill.
* Human remains solely responsible for merging.
* Python is removed from the required runtime or reduced to a thin optional SDK that only calls `wh --json`.
* README, AGENTS.md, packaging, and CI describe Rust-only v1.
* Adversarial tests prove unsafe commands, branch mismatch, and path escape are blocked.

## Non-goals

* Reimplementing OpenAI Codex `babysit-pr` as a separate repository.
* Automated PR merging.
* A Python-owned workflow, state store, or direct `git`/`gh` mutation path.

## Child work

1. Record Rust-only ADR and product boundary.
2. Define unified `wh` command/state model.
3. Port discovery and planning to Rust.
4. Port issue-to-draft-PR lifecycle to Rust.
5. Add PR supervision primitives and Codex `babysit-pr` compatibility guidance.
6. Eliminate mutation bypass paths.
7. Retire Python orchestration.
8. Ship Rust-only packaging, docs, and verification.

title: [agoge-forger] GH#66 — Regression-test trainer construction vs installed TRL
description:
## Context

**P1 — CI cannot see the P0 train break.** Workflows `pr_quality_gate.yml` and `security_scan.yml` both run pytest under `.venv` and stay green while training is broken on TRL 1.4.

Root cause: **no test** imports the installed TRL surface or exercises `_build_training_args` / `_build_sft_trainer` used by `run_training`. Existing tests cover checkpoints, artifacts, config load, preflight, datasets, smoke CLI wiring — not SFTTrainer construction.

Companion fix: [rmems/agoge-forger#63](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig) / GH#63 migrates trainer code to `trl.SFTConfig` + `processing_class`. This issue is the **regression net** so the next TRL upgrade fails CI instead of shipping another silent train-path break.

Local facts (2026-08-01 research):

* `uv.lock` resolves `trl==1.4.0`; `SFTTrainer.__init__` rejects `dataset_text_field`, `max_seq_length`, and `tokenizer`
* `SFTConfig` exposes `max_length`, `dataset_text_field`, plus shared TrainingArguments save/bf16 fields
* `tests/` has no `test_trainer*.py`; repo grep for SFTTrainer under tests is empty
* Quality gate installs the editable package into `.venv` then runs `pytest tests/` — a pure unit test with mocks runs there with no GPU and no model download

## Repo / surfaces

| Path | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/trainer.py` | Code under test: `_build_training_args`, `_build_sft_trainer` (private helpers; importable in tests) |
| `src/agoge_forger/config.py` | Build a minimal ExperimentConfig / nested models for the builders |
| `tests/test_trainer_trl_api.py` (proposed) | Regression test home |
| `.github/workflows/pr_quality_gate.yml` | Existing gate — no workflow change needed if test is pure pytest |
| `.github/workflows/security_scan.yml` | Also runs pytest on tests/ |
| `pyproject.toml` | trl dependency already installed in CI venv (`trl>=0.8.0`) |

## Implementation plan

1. Add `tests/test_trainer_trl_api.py` (name flexible) with a module docstring explaining TRL API churn / why the test exists.
2. Construct a minimal in-memory ExperimentConfig (or light stub) with `dataset_text_field`, `training.max_seq_length`, batch/save fields, and `runtime.save_safetensors`.
3. Call `_build_training_args(config, out_dir)` and assert:
   * Result is an instance of `trl.SFTConfig` (or at least has `max_length` / `dataset_text_field` populated from config)
   * `max_length == config.training.max_seq_length`
   * `dataset_text_field == config.dataset_text_field`
4. Call `_build_sft_trainer(...)` with mocks (MagicMock model/tokenizer/dataset) so construction hits real `SFTTrainer.__init__` signature validation — prefer importing real ``` trl.``SFTTrainer ``` so removed kwargs raise TypeError in CI.
5. Optional hardening: fail if source of `trainer.py` still passes removed kwargs into `SFTTrainer(` (string/AST guard) if full construction is too heavy.
6. Keep test GPU-free and HF-download-free; do not call `run_training` end-to-end.
7. Pair with [rmems/agoge-forger#63](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig): test should pass once migration lands; red before that is acceptable (TDD) if landed in the same PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit (or thin integration) test fails if `_build_sft_trainer` / args builder uses removed TRL kwargs (`dataset_text_field`, `max_seq_length`, `tokenizer` on SFTTrainer)
- [ ] Test imports **installed** trl (not a stub of the library) so version drift is real
- [ ] Test runs in existing PR quality gate without GPU or model download (mocks / tiny stubs OK)
- [ ] Module docstring documents why the test exists (TRL API churn / train-path P0 class)
- [ ] No new workflow YAML required unless pytest discovery path changes (it should not)

## Validation

```bash
# Should fail on main before RM-209; pass after migration + this test
.venv/bin/pytest tests/test_trainer_trl_api.py -q

# Full gate surface
.venv/bin/pytest tests/ -q
.venv/bin/ruff check src tests

# Confirm TRL is what CI will see from the lock
.venv/bin/python -c "import trl; print(trl.__version__)"
```

## Non-goals

* Full GPU train smoke in CI
* Replacing or extending reusable uv/pytest workflow bootstrap (GH#32 — orthogonal)
* Config/contract validation on PR (GH#35 — orthogonal)
* Migrating the trainer itself (that is [rmems/agoge-forger#63](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig) / GH#63 — implement together or first)
* Changing trl pin policy beyond what the test asserts about the installed API

## GitHub

[https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/66](<https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/66>)

Related Linear: [rmems/agoge-forger#63](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig) (GH#63) — SFTConfig migration this test guards.

P1: CI regression that constructs trainer against installed TRL ([RM-212](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-212/bugci-regression-test-trainer-construction-against-installed-trl) / GH#66). title: [agoge-forger] GH#64 — Report VRAM in GiB so 16GB risk gates fire on RTX 5080
description:
## Context

Local training is optimized for **16 GiB** cards (RTX 5080 path). Disk preflight already uses binary units (`BYTES_PER_GB = 1024**3`), but GPU VRAM is reported with **decimal** `/ 1e9`. That inflates a true 16 GiB card to ~**17.18** “GB”, so the safety gate `vram <= 16.5` never runs and OOM risk warnings (no 4-bit, batch_size > 1, long sequences) stay silent on target hardware.

| Bytes | `/ 1e9` (today) | `/ 1024**3` (desired) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `16 * 1024**3` | **17.18** | **16.0** |

Priority: **P1** — wrong safety signal on primary local GPU.

## Repo surfaces

| Path | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/preflight.py` | `BYTES_PER_GB` (disk only); `get_gpu_report()` uses `/ 1e9` for `total_vram_gb` / `allocated_vram_gb`; `estimate_training_risk()` gates on `vram <= 16.5` |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/trainer.py` | `run_training` calls `get_gpu_report` + `estimate_training_risk`; `_finalize_training_run` logs/metrics `max_vram_gb` via `/ 1e9` |
| `src/agoge_forger/backends/torch_backend.py` | `check_torch_env` logs Total VRAM with `/ 1e9` |
| `docs/rtx5080_local_training.md` | Documents preflight risk rules; incorrectly claims max_seq warning only for models **>3B** (code has **no** model-size check) |
| `docs/contracts/run_manifest.md`, `docs/contracts/metrics_schema.md` | Field names `*_vram_gb` / `max_vram_gb`; examples assume ~16.0 for full card — unit meaning should stay consistent |
| `tests/test_preflight.py` | Covers disk pressure + LoRA targets only — **no** VRAM unit / risk-gate tests |

### Confirmed bug (local)

```python
# preflight.py
BYTES_PER_GB = 1024**3  # used for disk free/size only

# get_gpu_report()
"total_vram_gb": torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 1e9,
"allocated_vram_gb": torch.cuda.memory_allocated(0) / 1e9,

# estimate_training_risk()
if vram <= 16.5:
    # warn: no 4bit / batch_size > 1 / max_seq_length > 2048
```

Same `/ 1e9` in `trainer.py` (`max_memory_allocated`) and `torch_backend.py`.

## Implementation plan

1. **Single VRAM divisor** — Use `BYTES_PER_GB` (or a shared alias) in `get_gpu_report`, trainer peak VRAM, and torch backend env log so all “GB” VRAM numbers are binary (GiB), matching disk preflight.
2. **Keep field names** — Prefer keeping `*_vram_gb` / `max_vram_gb` keys for manifest compatibility; document that values are binary GiB (optional: log label “GiB” in human strings).
3. **Risk gate** — After unit fix, mocked `total_memory = 16 * 1024**3` must yield ~16.0 and enter `<= 16.5` branch (warnings fire).
4. **Tests** — Extend `tests/test_preflight.py` (or sibling) with monkeypatched CUDA props / no real GPU: assert reported total ~16.0; assert `estimate_training_risk` emits the three warning classes when config is risky on that report.
5. **Docs** — Align `docs/rtx5080_local_training.md` with actual code: no model-size filter on max_seq warning; note binary GiB reporting.
6. **Contracts** — Light touch on metrics/manifest docs if they imply decimal SI GB; clarify unit without renaming fields unless needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All user-facing / metrics VRAM “GB” numbers use the same unit as disk (`1024**3`), or mixed units are explicitly labeled (prefer one unit).
- [ ] Mocked `total_memory = 16 * 1024**3` yields ~`16.0` in `get_gpu_report` and **does** enter the `<=` `16.5` risk branch.
- [ ] Risky config on 16 GiB report warns for: no `load_in_4bit`, `batch_size > 1`, `max_seq_length > 2048`.
- [ ] Tests cover `get_gpu_report` / `estimate_training_risk` unit behavior without a GPU (monkeypatch).
- [ ] `docs/rtx5080_local_training.md` matches real risk rules (drop incorrect “models larger than 3B” claim unless code gains that check).
- [ ] Existing disk preflight / LoRA target tests still pass; train path still starts (no new hard failures from unit change alone).

## Validation (bash)

```bash
cd /home/raulmc/rmems/agoge-forger

# unit: preflight + any new VRAM tests
pytest -q tests/test_preflight.py -k "vram or risk or gpu or disk or lora" --tb=short

# broader smoke if env allows
pytest -q tests/test_preflight.py tests/test_config.py --tb=short

# optional: prove divisor math without GPU
python -c "print(16*1024**3/1e9, 16*1024**3/1024**3)"  # ~17.18 vs 16.0
```

## Non-goals

* Changing risk thresholds themselves (16.5 / batch / seq) beyond making units correct.
* Adding model-parameter-size detection for risk (doc currently claims it; code does not — fix doc, do not expand scope to size heuristics unless product asks).
* Renaming public metric keys (`max_vram_gb`) or breaking run-manifest consumers.
* Full e2e train on real RTX 5080 in CI.
* Parameter count display in `models/inspect.py` (`/ 1e9` for parameter billions is SI-style and out of scope).

## GitHub link

[https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/64](<https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/64>)

Dataset empty-file and messages content validation ([RM-211](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-211/bugdatasets-harden-empty-jsonl-and-non-string-message-content) / GH#65). title: [grok-ozempic] Research: activity-aware / tier-aware τ for spiking-sparse GOZ1
description:
> **Linear SoT:** [RM-201](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-201/grok-ozempic-research-activity-aware-tier-aware-t-for-spiking-sparse)
>
> Body synced from Linear. Prefer Linear for status; this GH issue is the GitHub twin.

## Context

[RM-190](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-190) / [GH#39](<https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/issues/39>) produced the first real GOZ1 from `embedding.slot_00.token_embedding`:

* τ = 0.05 × RMS → **\~4.17% zeros**, ~96% ±1 (**dense / sign-like**)
* Not sparse SNN activity; quantizer behaved correctly
* Result is weight distribution vs default τ, not CPU vs GPU

Algorithm (`src/core/quantizer.rs`):

```text
rms = sqrt(mean(w²))
τ   = gif_threshold × rms
|w| < τ → 0;  w ≥ τ → +1;  w ≤ −τ → −1
```

Default `gif_threshold = 0.05` (`types.rs`). Precedence (`precision.rs`): per-tensor ternary_candidate → manifest defaults → CLI config.

**Trap for sweeps:** stock `baseline.json` bakes `defaults.gif_threshold: 0.05`, so CLI `--gif-threshold` is **ignored** for actual quantize τ. Use a temp manifest without defaults.gif_threshold, or bake τ into defaults per run.

BitNet b1.58 uses absmean + RoundClip (different scale story). GOZ1 is PTQ saliency gate — same alphabet, different control knob.

This issue tracks the **science** so we can *choose* event-driven / spiking-sparse ternary.

## Goal

Make ternary packing policy **activity-aware / tier-aware** so embeddings, MoE experts, and attention land on different sparsity regimes. **Success = measured non-trivial zeros under GIF, not dense-sign packs.**

## Work (research, not kernel work)

- [ ] τ sweeps on embedding (0.0 control, 0.05 default, 0.1 → 0.2 → 0.5 …) with trit histograms / sparsity
- [ ] Same on ≥1 expert projection and ≥1 attention tensor (needs multi-tensor export)
- [ ] Define per-tier defaults (embedding vs MoE vs attn; router = preserve)
- [ ] Document when dense sign-like is OK vs when sparsity is required
- [ ] Optional: per-row / per-group RMS or absmean arm
- [ ] Feed findings into SAAQ 1.5 multi-tensor policy notes
- [ ] Land reports under `reports/grok-1-first-embed-goz1/` (or similar) with commands

### CLI sketch (embedding isolate)

```bash
# STAGE = sole embedding npy dir
# MANI = JSON without defaults.gif_threshold (CLI controls τ)
for TAU in 0.0 0.05 0.1 0.2 0.5; do
  cargo run --release --features cli -- quantize-goz1 \
    --input-dir "$STAGE" --output "goz1-tau-${TAU}.goz1" \
    --manifest "$MANI" --gif-threshold "$TAU" --verify
done
```

## Non-goals

* No CUDA / myelin kernel work (→ [LIM-890](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/LIM-890) / [RM-199](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-199))
* No fake sparsity in the packer — zeros from threshold policy only
* No full-model requant or quality claims
* No brainstem-daemon / runtime integration
* No router ternary

## Acceptance

* Written comparison of sparsity vs τ for ≥2 tensor families (embedding + one other when exportable)
* Recommended default τ (or policy) per tier for next multi-tensor run
* Clear statement of when GOZ1 ternary is event-driven vs dense
* Document baseline-manifest CLI τ trap

## Related

* [RM-190](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-190) (Done) — first embedding GOZ1 + dense finding
* [RM-196](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-196) — parent multi-tensor epic
* [RM-191](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-191) — V2 bridge for correct multi-tensor tiers
* [RM-198](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-198) — SAAQ formula keep (ΔQ law ≠ gif_threshold)
* [LIM-890](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/LIM-890) — packed ternary kernels (execution only)
notes: Research delivered by Claude Fable 5: PR #52 (claude/fable5-51-tau-sweep). Embedding τ→zeros% curve measured (0.05→4.17%, 0.5→39.72%, 1.0→69.71%; 50% sparsity needs τ≈0.65). baseline.json defaults.gif_threshold trap documented + demonstrated. Expert/attn sweeps blocked-by-export: ckpt-0 experts/attn are int8 quant.weight — needs dequant exporter (see goz follow-up). Report: reports/grok-1-tau-sweep/results.md

title: [grok-ozempic] Integrate Limen-Neural/myelin-accelerator for RTX 5080 GOZ1 GEMV/GEMM
description:

>

## Summary

Wire `grok-ozempic` to **existing** Blackwell-first ternary path in `myelin-accelerator` so GOZ1 `TENSOR_TERNARY` payloads drive host bitpacking + device GEMV/GEMM on **RTX 5080 (sm_120)**.

Interop: same trit codes; `pack_ternary_bytes` / LE u32 prefix. Device: `ternary_gemv` / `ternary_gemm` with group scales (default 128) and `skip_zeros` (only helps when GIF sparsity is real).

sm_120: PTX ≥ 9.2, CUDA 13.2+, driver ≥ 570; local goldens with `--features cuda`.

## Non-goals

* No full experiment recipes inside myelin

## Acceptance

- [ ] CPU interop tests green

- [ ] 5080 smoke GEMV and/or GEMM matches host ref
- [ ] skip_zeros path exercised when zeros present

title: [research] Keep SaaqV1_5SqrtRate — external y before any SAAQ 2.0 SR (no circular rediscovery)
description:
> **Linear SoT:** [RM-198](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-198/research-keep-saaqv1-5sqrtrate-external-y-before-any-saaq-20-sr-no)
>
> Body synced from Linear. Prefer Linear for status; this GH issue is the GitHub twin.

## Verdict (Grok Build multi-agent research)

**HYBRID — KEEP SAAQ 1.5 as runtime default.** Do **not** mint SAAQ 2.0 from SymbolicRegression on existing latent CSVs.

| Option | Decision |
| -- | -- |
| KEEP 1.5 | **Yes** — default formula + campaign label |
| PATCH 1.5 | Only for measured defects (cold-start/silence), not prettier SR trees |
| NEW formula (2.0) | **Not yet** — only after an **external** `y` exists |
| HYBRID | Freeze 1.5 hot path; SR = research against external objectives |

**Confidence:** ~0.86

---

## Two meanings of "SAAQ 1.5" (do not conflate)

### A. Formula version — `SaaqV1_5SqrtRate`

```text
saaq_delta_q_target = 0.0573 * sqrt(max(avg_pop_firing_rate_hz, 0.0))
                    + 0.496  * saaq_delta_q_prev
```

* Eng: `corinth-canal/src/latent.rs`, `SAAQ-latent`
* Doc: `corinth-canal/docs/SAAQ_FORMULA_COMPARISON.md`
* Provenance HoF: `Surrogate_Viz.jl/outputs/20260416_232439_RN5oWH/hall_of_fame.csv`

### B. Engineering epic / campaign

Multi-model RE4 lineup, dual calibrator, validation dashboards — product line **around** the formula.

### C. grok-ozempic "SAAQ" (third layer)

GOZ1 ternary packing: `τ = gif_threshold × rms(layer)` (default 0.05). **Not** the latent AR(1) law.

Linear "SAAQ 1.5 multi-tensor GOZ1" ≠ Surrogate_Viz "sqrt-rate formula."

---

## Why 1.5 is good enough *as default ΔQ*

* Simple, hot-path cheap (rate + AR only)
* Dual calibrator + CSV contract already A/B both rules
* Ecosystem frozen: SAAQ-latent tests, MoE campaigns, magere `saaq_v1_5`
* Default in docs (`SAAQ_RULE=saaq_v1_5`)

## Why not create a new formula in Surrogate_Viz *right now*

1. **Circular SR:** targeting `saaq_delta_q_target` rediscovers exact 1.5 — fidelity, not a better law
2. Raw discovery rediscovers synthetic power/400 targets — different problem class
3. **No closed loop into quant:** packing still uses static `gif_threshold`
4. Paired validation often null under some conditions
5. Spikenaut is mining/GPU/HFT telemetry — good for **external** y, not latent SAAQ schema

---

## What a real new Surrogate_Viz formula would need

**Forbidden y for promotion:** `y = saaq_delta_q_target` (circular)

**Allowed external y:** thermal/power, GOZ1 sparsity+quality under τ(ΔQ), router health as features only, closed-loop Δτ

## Work

- [ ] Doc split: formula vs campaign vs GOZ1 gif_threshold
- [ ] Freeze default `SaaqV1_5SqrtRate`; dual emit both rules
- [ ] Ban circular SR for promotion
- [ ] Spec external primary y + success thresholds
- [ ] Optional closed-loop spike: ΔQ → τ on one embedding GOZ1
- [ ] If PATCH: cold-start/silence only + unit tests
- [ ] If 2.0 later: new enum + dual columns; Surrogate_Viz mode targeting external y

## Non-goals

* Do not block GOZ1 / spiking-sparse τ / myelin work
* Do not auto-edit 0.0573/0.496 from a single Spikenaut or MoE Pareto row

## Acceptance

- [ ] Written decision: **KEEP** with optional PATCH path
- [ ] Explicit statement that Linear SAAQ 1.5 GOZ1 epic ≠ formula rediscovery
- [ ] External-y experiment design ready before any SAAQ 2.0 issue
- [ ] No runtime default change without multi-model holdout on external metric

title: [grok-ozempic] GH#38 — CLI for GOZ1 run_quantization (token embedding)
description:
## Context

The documented SAAQ CLI (`smoke-grok1`, `convert-grok1`, `validate-grok1-artifact`) writes **metadata only** (`src/artifact.rs`). Real ternary packing lives in the library path:

* `stream::run_quantization` (`src/core/stream.rs` ~L236)
* `quantizer` + `weight_pack` (GOZ1 container)
* Re-exported from `src/lib.rs` as `run_quantization`

There is **no CLI subcommand** that calls it. First real experiment ([RM-190](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-190/grok-ozempic-gh39-quantize-token-embedding-goz1)) must not require ad-hoc `main` harnesses.

Depends on export format from [RM-189](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-189/grok-ozempic-gh37-picklejax-shard-safetensors-or-npy-export) (pickle → safetensors/npy).

## Repo / surfaces

| Surface | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `src/bin/grok-ozempic.rs` | clap CLI; feature-gated `cli` |
| `src/lib.rs` | `pub use … run_quantization` |
| `src/core/stream.rs` | `run_quantization`, `resolve_manifest` |
| `src/types.rs` | `QuantizationConfig` (`input_dir`, `output_path`, `input_format`, `manifest_path`, …) |
| `src/core/quantizer.rs` | ternary / `pack_trits` |
| `src/core/weight_pack.rs` | GOZ1 writer |
| `Cargo.toml` | `cli` feature + `[[bin]] required-features` |

## Implementation plan

1. Add subcommand e.g. `quantize-goz1` (or `pack-goz1`) under `--features cli`.
2. Map flags → `QuantizationConfig`:
   * `--input-dir` → `input_dir`
   * `--output` → `output_path`
   * `--manifest` → `manifest_path`
   * `--input-format` `safetensors|npy` → `QuantizationInputFormat`
   * Optional: `GROK_OZEMPIC_MANIFEST` already honored by `resolve_manifest`
3. Call `run_quantization(&config)`; print shard stats / summary to stdout.
4. Document recommended first-target invocation (embedding-only export dir + V1-compatible names or post-[RM-191](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-191/grok-ozempic-gh40-v2-structural-name-bridge-for-stream) V2 bridge).
5. Unit/integration tests: clap parse + tiny synthetic npy/safetensors fixture if tests already use that pattern in `stream.rs`.
6. README: section next to SAAQ sprint commands clarifying **metadata path vs GOZ1 path**.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo run --features cli -- quantize-goz1 …` (final name TBD) produces a GOZ1 file from safetensors or npy input
- [ ] Flags cover input/output/manifest/format at minimum
- [ ] At least one automated test for the new subcommand wiring
- [ ] README documents the command and that `convert-grok1` is **not** real quant

## Validation

```bash
cargo build --features cli --locked
# After RM-189 export exists:
cargo run --features cli -- quantize-goz1 \
  --input-dir /path/to/export \
  --output /tmp/embedding.goz1 \
  --manifest dissect/grok-1/baseline.json \
  --input-format npy   # or safetensors
ls -lh /tmp/embedding.goz1
cargo test --features cli --locked
```

## Non-goals

* Implementing pickle load inside the CLI
* Full 770-tensor orchestration
* Myelin CUDA backend (LocalBackend only)
* Changing SAAQ metadata writer behavior

title: [grok-ozempic] GH#37 — pickle/JAX shard → safetensors or .npy export
description:
## Context

Official Grok-1 `ckpt-0` shards are **JAX pickle** frames named `tensorNNNNN_000`. The GOZ1 stream quantizer (`src/core/stream.rs`) explicitly does **not** support pickle — only `*.safetensors` or a flat `.npy` directory (`QuantizationInputFormat::{Safetensors, NpyDir}` in `src/types.rs`). This issue is the **format bridge** that unblocks real weight packing ([RM-193](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-193/grok-ozempic-gh38-cli-for-goz1-run-quantization-token-embedding) / [RM-190](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-190/grok-ozempic-gh39-quantize-token-embedding-goz1)).

Weights are on disk and complete:

* Path: `/home/raulmc/.models/xai-grok-1/ckpt-0`
* **770** shards, ~297 GiB
* First-target shard: `tensor00000_000` (~3.1 GiB) = f32 `(131072, 6144)` token embedding

`xai-dissect` already reads pickle natively; reuse its loaders or a one-off Python script rather than inventing a second parser in-repo if possible.

## Repo / surfaces

| Surface | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `/home/raulmc/.models/xai-grok-1/ckpt-0/tensor00000_000` | Source pickle embedding |
| `src/core/stream.rs` | Docs: “Python pickle is not supported”; scanners for safetensors / npy |
| `src/types.rs` | `QuantizationInputFormat::{Safetensors, NpyDir}`, `QuantizationConfig` |
| `/home/raulmc/rmems/xai-dissect` | Prior pickle inventory tooling |
| Suggested export root | e.g. `/home/raulmc/.models/xai-grok-1/export-npy/` or `/tmp/grok1-embed-npy/` |

## Implementation plan

1. Prefer **embedding-only** export first (not full 770) to save time/disk for the first experiment.
2. Choose format:
   * **Recommended for first target:** single flat `.npy` named so the stream scanner finds it (document exact filename convention stream expects), **or** one small safetensors file with a tensor key matching the manifest rule you will use.
3. Extract f32 payload from pickle `tensor00000_000` → shape `(131072, 6144)`.
4. Write converter script/command under repo `scripts/` or document one-liner if external tool is enough.
5. Smoke-load with a tiny Rust test or `run_quantization` dry path once CLI exists; until then, verify with Python/`numpy.load` + shape/dtype assert.
6. Document output path in a short comment on GH#37 for [RM-190](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-190/grok-ozempic-gh39-quantize-token-embedding-goz1) consumers.
7. Optional follow-up: full 770-tensor export (disk-heavy; out of first-experiment critical path).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least the embedding tensor exists on disk as safetensors or `.npy` with dtype f32 and shape `(131072, 6144)`
- [ ] File(s) are discoverable by `stream` scanners (`*.safetensors` or `.npy` dir layout)
- [ ] Conversion command/script is documented (README snippet or `scripts/` + GH comment)
- [ ] Export path is stable and quoted for [RM-193](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-193/grok-ozempic-gh38-cli-for-goz1-run-quantization-token-embedding) / [RM-190](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-190/grok-ozempic-gh39-quantize-token-embedding-goz1)

## Validation

```bash
# Source present
ls -lh /home/raulmc/.models/xai-grok-1/ckpt-0/tensor00000_000
# After export (example for npy):
python3 - <<'PY'
import numpy as np
# adjust path after export
a = np.load("/tmp/grok1-embed-npy/token_embedding.npy")  # or whatever name you choose
assert a.dtype == np.float32 and a.shape == (131072, 6144), (a.dtype, a.shape)
print("ok", a.nbytes)
PY
```

## Non-goals

* Full 770-shard requantization
* CUDA / myelin kernels
* Inference quality
* Changing GOZ1 on-disk format

## GitHub

* [https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/issues/37](<https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/issues/37>)
* Parent epic: [RM-186](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-186/grok-ozempic-epic-first-real-grok-1-embedding-quant-experiment)

title: [grok-ozempic] GH#39 — Quantize token embedding → GOZ1
description:
## Status: DONE — first real Grok-1 embedding → GOZ1

Closed after successful pack + artifact deep-dive (2026-07-31).

## Results (research)

| Item | Value |
| -- | -- |
| Artifact | `/home/raulmc/.models/xai-grok-1/artifacts/grok1-first-embed.goz1` |
| Format | **GOZ1 v1**, 1 tensor, type **TERNARY** |
| Name | `embedding.slot_00.token_embedding` shape `[131072, 6144]` |
| Elements | 805,306,368 |
| Size | **192.00 MiB** (payload 201,326,592 B + 544 B header) |
| Compression | 3.000 GiB f32 → 192 MiB = **16×** (also **8×** vs FP16) |
| Quant wall / RSS | 4.64 s / ~5.3 GiB (release, CPU) |
| Manifest used | `dissect/grok-1/baseline.json` (V1 default ternary) |
| GIF | `oz.gif_threshold = 0.05` |

### Trit histogram (full payload)

| code | meaning | fraction |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 0b00 | 0 | **4.17%** |
| 0b01 | +1 | **47.65%** |
| 0b10 | −1 | **48.18%** |
| 0b11 | invalid | 0% |

→ Dense/sign-like ternary at default τ — **not** sparse SNN activity for this layer.

### Game change

1. End-to-end path proven: pickle → npy → `quantize-goz1` → verified GOZ1 (not metadata-only).
2. First-target strategy works: one portable tensor, tiny header overhead.
3. GIF sparsity narrative needs τ sweeps for embeddings.
4. Unlocks myelin dequant / multi-tensor (#40) / quality evals.

## Problem

`rmems/gaming-telemetry` should stay a **boring hardware telemetry collector** for neuromorphic / SNN training data from an RTX 5080 workstation under max-settings game load.

The previous agent cycle over-built Cyberpunk 2077 install verification (`verify_cyberpunk`, privacy path, fixtures, CI privacy-and-verify-guard, PT/DLSS/UltraPlus/CET workflow). That complexity does not produce training samples and blocks multi-title capture.

**Owned workloads going forward (operator max settings, not code):** Kingdom Come Deliverance 2, RE2R, RE3R, RE Requiem, and others as purchased — not a CP2077-only verifier pipeline.

## Product intent

| What | How |
| -- | -- |
| Hardware | RTX 5080, NVML + CPU hwmon/RAPL |
| Workloads | Max settings on owned titles |
| Output | Parquet batches → canonical CSV → corinth-canal / SNN |
| Philosophy | Game-agnostic collector. Prefer delete over abstract. |

## Strict review summary (blockers)

1. **Delete** `verify_cyberpunk` — wrong problem; install/mod/PT checks are operator checklist, not code.
2. **Delete/simplify CI + README** built around privacy-safe CP2077 verifier (#7–#15 epic direction).
3. **Do not grow Steam/Proton discovery** — collector already never walks `$HOME`.
4. **Add one simple multi-game field:** `session_label` / `workload_id` via env or single CLI flag (e.g. `SESSION_LABEL=kcd2`). New titles = new string + play session, **zero** new Rust modules.
5. Optional: slim Sentry bootstrap; fix fire-and-forget Parquet writes on shutdown; canonicalize batch filename prefix (`gpu_telemetry_v1_*` vs `system_telemetry_v1_*` drift).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Remove `verify_cyberpunk` binary + fixture-only CI jobs for it
- [ ] Replace CP2077-centric docs with game-agnostic capture runbook
- [ ] Optional `session_label` on every Parquet sample
- [ ] Document recipes for kcd2 / re2r / re3r / re_requiem / cp2077
- [ ] New titles require no new modules
- [ ] Keep: poll → buffer → Parquet → `export_csv` bridge

## Non-goals

* Auto-detect running game
* Parse game configs / saves / mods
* Restore full deleted verify tree from history

title: [SAAQ-DN] Implement Divisive Normalization as alternative to L2 voltage bounding
description:
## Summary

Implement Carandini-Heeger Divisive Normalization as an alternative to the current L2-normalized voltage bounding in SAAQ 1.0. This would improve biological plausibility while preserving the two-layer control structure (normalization + delta-Q adaptation).

**GitHub Issue:** [https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/131](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/131>)

---

## Background

Current SAAQ 1.0 uses L2 normalization:

```
V_norm = V / sqrt(sum(V_i^2) + epsilon)
```

This is a **global** normalization — every component divided by the same scalar. It's computationally cheap and prevents routing collapse, but is not biologically canonical.

Divisive normalization is the **canonical neural computation** observed throughout the visual cortex (Carandini & Heeger, 2012). It operates locally with weighted neighborhood interactions:

```
V_norm_i = max(0, V_i) / (sigma^2 + sum_j w_ij * max(0, V_j)^2)^alpha
```

## Key Differences

| Property | L2 (current) | Divisive Normalization |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Scope | Global (one scalar per vector) | Local (per-neuron, weighted neighbors) |
| Weights | Uniform (all neurons equal) | Gaussian neighborhood (biological) |
| Nonlinearity | None (raw norm) | Half-wave rectification + exponent |
| Semi-saturation | epsilon (tiny floor) | sigma (tunable baseline) |
| Biological fidelity | Low (computational shortcut) | High (canonical cortical computation) |
| Computation cost | O(n) | O(n * k) where k = neighborhood size |

## Compatibility with SAAQ 1.5

The delta-Q adaptation law operates **on top of** voltage normalization and would remain unchanged:

```
delta_q_target = 0.0573 * sqrt(avg_pop_firing_rate_hz) + 0.496 * delta_q_prev
```

Two-layer structure preserved:

1. **Layer 1 (normalization)**: DN replaces L2 for voltage bounding
2. **Layer 2 (adaptation)**: SAAQ 1.5 delta-Q law operates on normalized activity

## Open Design Questions

* **Neighborhood topology**: What defines "neighbors" in the walker/routing context? Same walker range? Same routing basin? Same time step?
* **sigma tuning**: Should sigma adapt with population activity (doubly-adaptive system)?
* **alpha choice**: `alpha=0.5` gives square-root normalization (similar to SAAQ 1.5's sqrt term). `alpha=1.0` is standard Carandini-Heeger.
* **Weight matrix w_ij**: Gaussian kernel with what bandwidth? Learned or fixed?

## Proposed Approach

**Don't replace L2 yet. Implement DN as a parallel path** behind a feature flag. Then run the same SR benchmark (Surrogate_Viz.jl, 9 models, 3 conditions) with DN normalization and compare Pareto fronts.

## References

* Carandini & Heeger, "Normalization as a canonical neural computation," Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 2012
* Survey: `survey/snn-quant-attn-bio/divisive_norm_and_data_analysis.md`
* SAAQ 1.5: `SAAQ 1.5/README.md`

title: [Spikenaut-SNN] Monotonic hidden weight artifact in merged v2 parameters
description:
## Root Cause Identified (2026-07-12)

The monotonic weight pattern is NOT an export bug. It is degenerate training convergence caused by:

1. **Training data too small** — only 8 records, 2 of 6 features effectively constant
2. **No inhibitory connections** — zero negative weights, all neurons fire in lockstep
3. **Identical gradient signals** — E-prop/OTTT produces same updates across all neurons

### Pattern

Formula: `weight[n][i] = 0.75 + n×0.015625 + i×0.00390625`

---

## Fix Applied (2026-07-12)

* ✅ Replaced `fresh_sync_data.jsonl` (8 records) with `qubic_ticks_snn.jsonl` (27,430 records)
* ✅ Created data adapter `tools/transform_qubic_to_snn.py`

## Data Cleanup Complete (2026-07-13)

* ✅ Julia cleanup pipeline: `tools/julia-compute/clean_datasets.jl`
* ✅ node_sync_harvest: 120K records cleaned (9 dead cols removed, 20 synthetic trimmed)

title: Implement packed ternary CUDA kernels for SAAQ experiments
description:
## Goal

Add true ternary weight kernels instead of relying on FP16/FP32 weighted kernels.

## Motivation

Current kernels are useful for SNN routing and telemetry research, but they are not yet real ternary quantization kernels. This repo needs a packed low-bit execution path for binary/ternary experiments.

## Tasks

- [ ] Define ternary encoding layout for {-1, 0, +1}.
- [ ] Implement 2-bit packed weight storage.
- [ ] Add group scaling support.
- [ ] Implement ternary GEMV kernel.
- [ ] Implement ternary GEMM kernel.
- [ ] Add optional sparse zero skipping.
- [ ] Add correctness tests against FP16 reference.
- [ ] Benchmark memory bandwidth and occupancy.

## Benchmark targets

* Compare against FP16.
* Compare against AWQ/GPTQ baselines.
* Measure:
  * latency
  * throughput
  * VRAM usage
  * numerical drift

## Acceptance criteria

* Ternary kernels run end-to-end on RTX 5080.
* Packed representation reduces VRAM traffic.
* Error metrics are logged against FP16 reference outputs.

title: [agoge-forger] GH#65 — Harden empty JSONL and non-string message content
description:
## Context

Dataset loading normalizes JSONL Formats A/B/C in `src/agoge_forger/datasets.py` before training. Two hard edges produce bad failures or silent schema drift:

1. **Empty / all-blank JSONL** — `dataset_stats` builds a numpy length array and calls `arr.max()` / `arr.mean()` with no empty guard → opaque `ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation maximum which has no identity`. Empty generators can also fail awkwardly in `Dataset.from_generator`.
2. **Non-string** `messages[].content` — Only `role` presence/allow-list is validated. Non-string content (e.g. `123`) is f-string joined into `"User: 123"` instead of a clear 1-indexed schema error, diverging from `docs/contracts/dataset_jsonl.md` (content documented as `str`).

Priority: **P2** — data-path correctness and clear errors before long train jobs.

## Repo surfaces

| Path | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `src/agoge_forger/datasets.py` | `normalize_row`, `load_jsonl_dataset`, `dataset_stats` |
| `docs/contracts/dataset_jsonl.md` | Contract: Format A/B/C; `content` is **str**; empty lines skipped; errors 1-indexed |
| `tests/test_dataset_validation.py` | Happy path for text / messages / instruction |
| `tests/test_datasets_strict.py` | Invalid text type, messages not list, bad role, unknown format — **not** empty file or non-string content |

### Confirmed behavior (local)

```python
# normalize_row — messages branch
for m in row["messages"]:
    if "role" not in m or "content" not in m: ...
    if m["role"] not in ["user", "assistant", "system", "tool"]: ...
    # no isinstance(m["content"], str)
# fallback join stringifies non-str content:
text = "\n".join([f"{m['role'].capitalize()}: {m['content']}" for m in row["messages"]])

# dataset_stats — no empty guard
arr = np.asarray(lengths, dtype=np.int64)
logger.info(f"Max Tokens: {arr.max()}")  # blows up when lengths == []
```

`load_jsonl_dataset` skips blank lines (`if not line.strip(): continue`) then yields normalized rows; zero yields → empty dataset / bad stats path.

Already solid: `text` must be `str`; `instruction` must be `str`; invalid roles and unknown formats raise with line index.

## Implementation plan

1. **Validate message content type** — In `normalize_row` messages loop, require `isinstance(m["content"], str)` (and optionally non-empty policy only if contract requires; default: type only). Raise `ValueError` with 1-indexed line number (and ideally message index).
2. **Empty dataset guard** — In `load_jsonl_dataset` and/or `dataset_stats`, if zero rows after parse, raise a clear `ValueError` (e.g. “dataset is empty / no valid rows”) instead of numpy reduction errors or opaque HF generator failures.
3. **Whitespace-only file** — Same path as empty (all lines skipped).
4. **Tests** — Extend `tests/test_datasets_strict.py` (and/or validation tests):
   * empty file
   * whitespace-only / blank lines only
   * `messages` with non-string `content`
   * regression: valid Formats A/B/C still normalize
5. **Contract** — If behavior for empty files is newly explicit, add one line under Validation Rules in `docs/contracts/dataset_jsonl.md` (optional but preferred).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Empty or all-blank JSONL yields a clear `ValueError` (or similar) from load and/or stats — **not** a numpy zero-size reduction error.
- [ ] Non-string `messages[i].content` raises with **1-indexed** line number.
- [ ] Tests cover empty file, whitespace-only, and bad content type.
- [ ] Behavior stays compatible with Formats A/B/C in the dataset contract (happy paths unchanged).

title: [agoge-forger] GH#36 — Azure OIDC dry-run (no deploy)
description:
## Context

Epic [RM-93](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-93/agoge-forger-gh22-docker-azure-cicd-epic-acr-amlaks) / GH#22 assumes GitHub → Azure OIDC (`AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`) for ACR push and deploy. The repo has **no** workflow that proves federated login works in isolation. Failures today would only appear inside a larger docker-push/deploy job.

Azure TF remains a stub (`infra/terraform/environments/azure/`); this issue is **auth-only**, not infra provisioning.

## Repo surfaces

| Path | Role |
| -- | -- |
| *(add)* `.github/workflows/azure_oidc_smoke.yml` | Manual OIDC dry-run |
| `infra/terraform/environments/azure/README.md` | Document Entra app + secrets (expand) |
| `docs/ci_smoke_tests.md` | Document workflow + required secrets |
| `README.md` § Cloud Infrastructure | Point to OIDC setup |
| Existing security patterns | `python_smoke_test.yml` input-via-env; SHA-pinned actions; least privilege |
| No current `azure/login` usage | Greenfield |

## Implementation plan

1. Add `.github/workflows/azure_oidc_smoke.yml`
2. Trigger: `workflow_dispatch` **only**
3. Inputs:
   * `dry_run` (default `true`) — auth + read-only account listing only
4. Permissions:
   * `id-token: write` (OIDC)
   * `contents: read`
5. Steps:
   * Checkout (optional; prefer minimal)
   * `azure/login@v2` **pinned by commit SHA** with OIDC client/tenant/subscription
   * `az account show`
   * `az group list --query "[].name" -o tsv | head` (read-only)
   * Explicitly **no** resource create/update/delete, no ACR push, no TF apply
6. Docs:
   * Entra ID app registration + federated credential (repo + environment subject)
   * GitHub secrets/variables table
   * Failure modes when federation misconfigured
7. Prefer GitHub Environment (e.g. `azure-smoke`) for secret scoping and protection rules

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Manual dispatch succeeds against a configured Azure federated credential
- [ ] `dry_run=true` performs auth + read-only queries only; no mutations
- [ ] Docs list Entra app setup and required GitHub secrets/vars
- [ ] OIDC trust conditions documented (repo and/or environment scoped)
- [ ] Workflow fails clearly when secrets or federation are wrong
- [ ] Action SHAs pinned; no long-lived Azure client secrets in repo

## Validation commands

```bash
# Local parity (developer machine; not the GHA OIDC path)
az login
az account show
az group list --query "[].name" -o tsv | head

# CI: Actions → "Azure OIDC smoke" → Run workflow (dry_run=true)
```

**Required GitHub configuration (document, do not commit values):**

| Name | Purpose |
| -- | -- |
| `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` | Federated credential app (client) ID |
| `AZURE_TENANT_ID` | Entra tenant |
| `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` | Target subscription |

## Non-goals

* `docker push` to ACR (epic [RM-93](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-93/agoge-forger-gh22-docker-azure-cicd-epic-acr-amlaks) after this)
* Azure ML job submission
* Terraform apply / plan against cloud
* Production environment promotion gates (beyond optional Environment protection)
* Creating ACR/AKS resources

## GitHub

[https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/36](<https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/36>)

## Related issues

* **Parent epic:** [RM-93](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-93/agoge-forger-gh22-docker-azure-cicd-epic-acr-amlaks) / GH#22 — de-risks ACR/deploy auth
* **Sibling:** [RM-96](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-96/ciinfra-add-terraform-fmt-and-validate-for-azure-scaffold-on-pr) Terraform fmt/validate (static HCL; no credentials)

title: [agoge-forger] GH#34 — Docker PR smoke (CPU image, no push)
description:
## Context

Epic [RM-93](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-93/agoge-forger-gh22-docker-azure-cicd-epic-acr-amlaks) / GH#22 bundles Dockerfile + ACR push + Azure deploy. There is still **no** root container definition, so nothing proves an image builds and runs a CPU-safe command before OIDC/registry complexity.

This issue is the de-risked first container slice: build + run only, no push.

## Repo surfaces

| Path | Role |
| -- | -- |
| *(missing)* `Dockerfile` | CPU/smoke baseline to add |
| *(missing)* `.dockerignore` | Exclude heavy/local artifacts |
| `pyproject.toml` | Package metadata; entry `agoge = agoge_forger.cli:app` |
| `uv.lock` | Locked deps for reproducible install |
| `src/agoge_forger/` | Installable package |
| `.github/workflows/python_smoke_test.yml` | Host-based smoke pattern to mirror (inputs via `env:`) |
| `.github/workflows/pr_quality_gate.yml` | SHA-pinning / least-privilege pattern |
| `docs/ci_smoke_tests.md` | Document new workflow |
| `docs/dependency_policy.md` | Lockfile / install policy |
| `adapters/`, `runs/`, `merged/`, `rust-tools/target/` | Must be dockerignored |

## Implementation plan

1. Add `Dockerfile` (CPU/smoke):
   * Base: official Python slim (3.12) or uv-friendly base
   * Copy lock + project metadata first for layer cache
   * Install deps from lock; install package (editable OK for smoke image; document if runtime image differs)
   * Default CMD/ENTRYPOINT suitable for `agoge --help`
2. Add `.dockerignore`:
   * At least: `adapters/`, `runs/`, `merged/`, `.venv`, `rust-tools/target/`, `.git`, caches, large local artifacts
3. Add `.github/workflows/docker_build_smoke.yml`:
   * `pull_request` paths: `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `src/**` (or narrower if preferred), workflow file
   * `workflow_dispatch` with optional `dry_run`
   * Steps: BuildKit `docker build` → `docker run` with `agoge --help` **or** `python -c "import agoge_forger"`
   * Optional non-blocking container scan (Docker Scout / Snyk) if secrets present
4. **No** registry push, **no** `azure/login`
5. Document in `docs/ci_smoke_tests.md`

title: [agoge-forger] GH#35 — Config/contract PR validation
description:
## Context

The repo ships training YAMLs and documented artifact contracts, but path filters on existing gates do **not** treat config/contract-only PRs as first-class:

* `pr_quality_gate.yml` paths: `src/**`, `tests/**`, `scripts/**`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` — **not** `configs/**` or `docs/contracts/**`
* Config breakage is often found only at training time

There are already unit tests that should run when those paths change; they need a dedicated, fast PR workflow (or expanded path filters).

## Repo surfaces

| Path | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `configs/smoke_test.yaml` | CI/tiny model baseline |
| `configs/local_rtx5080_16gb.yaml` | Local GPU profile |
| `configs/gka_hqwen3_reasoner_qlora.yaml` | QLoRA profile |
| `configs/nemotron_3_nano_4b_qlora.yaml` | QLoRA profile |
| `src/agoge_forger/config.py` | `ExperimentConfig` + `load_config()` (Pydantic; requires `model_id`, `dataset_path`) |
| `src/agoge_forger/manifests.py` | Run manifest writer |
| `docs/contracts/run_manifest.md` | Manifest contract |
| `docs/contracts/artifact_index.md` | Artifact index contract |
| `docs/contracts/{benchmark_event_jsonl,dataset_jsonl,metrics_schema,polyglot_boundaries}.md` | Other contracts |
| `tests/test_config.py` | Loads smoke config; checkpoint/safetensors fields |
| `tests/test_docs_workflow.py` | README / docs assertions |
| `tests/test_manifest.py` | Manifest JSON shape |
| `docs/model_config_validation.md` | Config validation docs |
| *(add)* `.github/workflows/config_contract_gate.yml` | New gate |

## Implementation plan

1. Add `.github/workflows/config_contract_gate.yml`
2. Triggers (`pull_request` + optional `workflow_dispatch`):
   * `configs/**`
   * `src/agoge_forger/config.py`
   * `src/agoge_forger/manifests.py`
   * `docs/contracts/**`
   * relevant tests + workflow file
3. Job (ubuntu-latest, < 2 min target):
   * Reuse Python bootstrap ([RM-95](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-95/ci-extract-reusable-workflow-for-uv-editable-install-and-pytest) composite if landed; else same `uv venv` + editable install pattern as `pr_quality_gate.yml`)
   * Parse **every** `configs/*.yaml` via `load_config` (script or pytest parametrize)
   * Run: `tests/test_config.py`, `tests/test_docs_workflow.py`, `tests/test_manifest.py`
   * Fail with actionable logs (which file/key)
4. No model download, no GPU, no HF network requirement
5. Optionally extend `pr_quality_gate` path filters later — this issue remains the focused contract gate

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All committed `configs/*.yaml` parse successfully in CI
- [ ] Contract/doc regression tests run on relevant PRs
- [ ] Workflow completes in < 2 minutes on ubuntu-latest
- [ ] No model download or GPU required
- [ ] `permissions: contents: read`; actions SHA-pinned

## Validation commands

```bash
uv venv && uv pip install -e ".[dev]"
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from agoge_forger.config import load_config
for p in sorted(Path("configs").glob("*.yaml")):
    cfg = load_config(str(p))
    print(f"OK {p}: model_id={cfg.model_id}")
PY
.venv/bin/pytest tests/test_config.py tests/test_docs_workflow.py tests/test_manifest.py -q
```

## Non-goals

* Full training execution
* Hugging Face model validation / download (host smoke: `python_smoke_test.yml`; container: [RM-97](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-97/cicontainer-add-pr-docker-build-smoke-workflow-cpu-image-no-registry))
* Replacing the full `pr_quality_gate` pytest suite

title: [agoge-forger] GH#32 — Reusable uv/pytest workflow
description:
## Context

Multiple workflows repeat the same Python bootstrap:

`checkout` → `astral-sh/setup-uv` → `uv venv` → `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"` → run tools from `.venv/bin/`.

Drift already caused install-mode confusion (`uv sync` vs editable `uv pip install`). After [RM-94](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-94/ci-add-pr-quality-gate-for-ruff-mypy-and-full-pytest) shipped `pr_quality_gate.yml`, the duplication is **worse** — four places share the pattern, not two.

## Repo surfaces

| File | Bootstrap today |
| -- | -- |
| `.github/workflows/pr_quality_gate.yml` | uv venv + `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"` → ruff/mypy/pytest |
| `.github/workflows/security_scan.yml` | same → pytest (+ separate rust job) |
| `.github/workflows/python_smoke_test.yml` | same → smoke script (also `setup-python` 3.12) |
| `.github/workflows/snyk_security.yml` | same pattern in SCA job |
| Docs | `docs/ci_smoke_tests.md`, `docs/dependency_policy.md` |
| Project | `pyproject.toml` (`[project.optional-dependencies] dev`), `uv.lock` |

**Pinned actions in use (match these SHAs):**

* `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1` # v7.0.1
* `astral-sh/setup-uv@c771a70e6277c0a99b617c7a806ffedaca235ff9` # v9.0.0

## Implementation plan

1. Add reusable workflow (composite action *or* `workflow_call` — prefer **composite action** under `.github/actions/python-uv-setup/` if callers need to continue in the same job; use `workflow_call` only if a full called-workflow job boundary is acceptable).
   * Suggested composite: `.github/actions/python-uv-setup/action.yml`
   * Inputs: `python-version` (default `3.12`), `install-extras` (default `dev`), `enable-cache` (default `true`)
   * Steps: optional `setup-python`, `setup-uv`, `uv venv`, `uv pip install -e ".[${extras}]"`
   * Document that tools run as `.venv/bin/<tool>` (no `PYTHONPATH` hacks)
2. Refactor callers to use the composite/reusable setup:
   * `pr_quality_gate.yml`
   * `security_scan.yml` (python-tests job only)
   * `python_smoke_test.yml`
   * Optionally `snyk_security.yml` SCA job (same bootstrap)
3. Keep smoke-test-specific `workflow_dispatch` inputs only in `python_smoke_test.yml`.
4. Document in `docs/ci_smoke_tests.md` under a “Shared Python setup” section.
5. Do **not** broaden permissions beyond `contents: read` for these callers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Shared setup path exists and is used by ≥3 Python workflows
- [ ] Install behavior identical to today: editable `.[dev]` into `.venv`; pytest imports `agoge_forger` without `PYTHONPATH`
- [ ] Callers keep `permissions: contents: read` (no expansion)
- [ ] Documented in `docs/ci_smoke_tests.md`
- [ ] `pr_quality_gate` still runs ruff + mypy + full `tests/`

## Validation commands

```bash
# Local parity with CI install
uv venv
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"
.venv/bin/ruff check .
.venv/bin/ruff format --check .
.venv/bin/mypy src/agoge_forger
.venv/bin/pytest tests/

# After change: open a no-op PR touching a workflow and confirm jobs green
```

## Non-goals

* Rust/Julia reusable workflows
* Changing to `uv sync` as the only install path (unless all callers migrate deliberately and docs update)
* Docker image build ([RM-97](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-97/cicontainer-add-pr-docker-build-smoke-workflow-cpu-image-no-registry)) or Azure OIDC ([RM-99](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-99/agoge-forger-gh36-azure-oidc-dry-run-no-deploy))

* **Parent epic:** [RM-93](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-93/agoge-forger-gh22-docker-azure-cicd-epic-acr-amlaks) / GH#22
* **Done precursor:** [RM-94](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-94/ci-add-pr-quality-gate-for-ruff-mypy-and-full-pytest) / GH#31 (PR quality gate — already duplicates this bootstrap)

description:
## Context

Broken HCL is only found during manual `terraform plan`.

Note: `snyk_security.yml` already runs **Snyk IaC** on `infra/terraform/` (medium+), but that is not a substitute for `fmt` + `validate` with the official Terraform CLI.

## Repo surfaces

| Path | Notes |

| `infra/terraform/environments/azure/main.tf` | `azurerm` ~> 3.0; commented `azurerm_linux_virtual_machine` |
| `infra/terraform/environments/azure/variables.tf` | `location` (East US), `vm_size` (Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4) |
| `infra/terraform/environments/azure/README.md` | One-liner: requires `az login` or SP |

| `infra/cloud-init/*.sh` | Placeholders incl. `setup-nvidia-container.sh` |
| `infra/terraform/README.md` | Top-level TF docs |
| `.github/workflows/snyk_security.yml` | Existing IaC scan (complement, not replace) |
| *(add)* `.github/workflows/terraform_validate.yml` | New PR gate |

## Implementation plan

1. Add `.github/workflows/terraform_validate.yml`
2. Triggers:
   * `pull_request` paths: `infra/terraform/**`, `infra/cloud-init/**`, the workflow file itself
   * Optional `workflow_dispatch`
3. Jobs (no cloud credentials):
   * `terraform fmt -check -recursive` on `infra/terraform`
   * For `infra/terraform/environments/azure`: `terraform init -backend=false` + `terraform validate`
   * Optionally matrix other environments later (aws/do/ibm) — Azure first
4. Pin `hashicorp/setup-terraform` by commit SHA; `permissions: contents: read`
5. Expand `infra/terraform/environments/azure/README.md` with CI gate + local commands
6. Fail loudly on fmt or validate errors (no `continue-on-error`)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PRs that break Azure TF fmt/validate fail CI
- [ ] Workflow uses `-backend=false` and needs **no** secrets
- [ ] Azure README documents the CI gate and local validate commands
- [ ] Actions pinned by SHA; least privilege
- [ ] Does not run `terraform plan` or `apply`

## Validation commands

```bash
cd infra/terraform
terraform fmt -check -recursive
cd environments/azure
terraform init -backend=false
terraform validate
```

## Non-goals

* Terraform apply from GitHub
* Remote state bootstrap / backend config
* ACR/AKS resource creation ([RM-93](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-93/agoge-forger-gh22-docker-azure-cicd-epic-acr-amlaks))

title: [grok-ozempic] GH#32 — Model-agnostic MoE/SNN quantization engine
description:
## Objective

`grok-ozempic` is currently tightly coupled to the Grok-1 model. It contains hard-coded assumptions about:

* Tensor inventory (770 tensors in `grok1_inventory.rs`)
* Tensor naming conventions (V1 `blk.{L}.{role}` and V2 `block_{NNN}.slot_{SS}`)
* Classification rules for routers, norms, MoE experts, attention projections, etc.
* Manifest schema expectations from `xai-dissect`
* Dry-run planning, alignment reporting, and coverage logic that all assume Grok-1 structure

While `magere-brug` provides a higher-level model registry, quantization recipes, and experiment tracking layer, it does **not** provide a reusable quantization engine. The two repos together still only solve the Grok-1 case.

## Goal

Extract a reusable core quantization engine that can support multiple open-source MoE models (Llama-3 MoE, Mixtral, DeepSeek-V2, Qwen2-MoE, etc.) while keeping Grok-1 as the primary/reference implementation.

## Lessons from PR #29 (Testing & Alignment)

PR #29 added 29 new tests for `BackendKernel`, `DryRunPlanner`, and alignment verification. During that work, several pain points emerged that directly inform this generalization effort:

### 1\. Massive test duplication (already partially addressed)

* Every `DryRunPlanner` test repeated the same 3-line setup:

  ```rust
  let m = embedded_grok1_structural_manifest();
  let config = QuantizationConfig::default();
  let report = DryRunPlanner::plan(m, &config).expect("plan should succeed");
  ```
* Extracted `plan_structural_manifest()` helper in `dry_run.rs`, but this is still Grok-1-specific.
* **Generalization impact**: A model-agnostic engine will need a generic test harness or fixture system so adding a new model doesn't require duplicating 10+ test blocks.

### 2\. `.codacy.yml` exclusions reveal structural problems

* Had to exclude `src/**/*` from duplication analysis because test patterns were too repetitive.
* Later narrowed to `src/**/*_test.rs` + `src/**/tests.rs` after CodeRabbit feedback.
* **Generalization impact**: The current test structure will not scale. A generic engine should have model-specific test modules that don't pollute the core test suite.

### 3\. Alignment verification is Grok-1 specific

* `check_alignment()`, `classify_full_inventory()`, `Grok1Inventory::full()` all assume the 770-tensor Grok-1 layout.
* The `every_inventory_tensor_matched_by_manifest_rule` test had to be patched to handle `<defaults>` fallback semantics.
* **Generalization impact**: Alignment checking should be a pluggable strategy, not a Grok-1-only module.

### 4\. Structural manifest loading is hardcoded

* `embedded_grok1_structural_manifest()` and `GROK1_STRUCTURAL_MANIFEST_JSON` are compile-time includes.
* V1 vs V2 naming convention handling lives in `manifest.rs` but is still Grok-1 flavored.
* **Generalization impact**: Manifest loading must become model-agnostic with per-model schema plugins.

## Suggested Abstractions

* Introduce a `ModelInventory` trait/plugin instead of the concrete `Grok1Inventory`
* Make tensor name conventions and glob patterns configurable per model
* Allow pluggable classification rules (router, norm, expert, projection, etc.)
* Support multiple manifest schemas (not just xai-dissect V1/V2)
* Per-model default precision tiers and GIF thresholds
* Keep the `BackendKernel` trait and `DryRunPlanner` as model-agnostic

## Non-Goals (keep scope reasonable)

* Do not move CUDA kernels into this repo
* Do not build a full model registry or experiment tracking system (belongs in `magere-brug`)
* Do not change the existing GOZ1 artifact format in v1

## Relationship to `magere-brug`

`magere-brug` would consume the generalized engine. `grok-ozempic` would become one (ideally the reference) implementation of that engine.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Core types (`BackendKernel`, `DryRunPlanner`, `QuantizationConfig`, etc.) have no Grok-1-specific assumptions
* Grok-1 continues to work with 100% of existing tests passing
* At least one additional model (or a minimal mock inventory) can be added without forking the repo
* Documentation updated to explain how to add support for a new model
* Test duplication is addressed at the architectural level (not just via `.codacy.yml` exclusions)

## Related

* `magere-brug` ([https://github.com/rmems/magere-brug](<https://github.com/rmems/magere-brug>)) — higher-level registry/recipes layer
* PR #29 (introduced the new tests that surfaced these duplication and coupling issues)
* Issues #28, #30, #31 (current refactoring and Docker follow-ups)

**Agent:** Kilo agent: xAI / Grok 4.3

title: [agoge-forger] GH#22 — Docker + Azure CI/CD epic (ACR, AML/AKS)
description:
## Context

Agoge Forger is local-first. CI today is Python/Rust/Julia smoke tests, a PR quality gate, and security scans — all host runners, no container image, no Azure publish/deploy path. That blocks reproducible cloud-scale training against the existing Azure Terraform scaffold.

**Current state (2026-08-01):**

* No root `Dockerfile` or `.dockerignore`
* Workflows under `.github/workflows/`: `pr_quality_gate.yml` (Done via [RM-94](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-94/ci-add-pr-quality-gate-for-ruff-mypy-and-full-pytest)/GH#31), `security_scan.yml`, `python_smoke_test.yml`, `rust_smoke_test.yml`, `julia_smoke_test.yml`, `snyk_security.yml`, `aikido_security.yml`
* Azure stub only: `infra/terraform/environments/azure/` (commented VM; minimal `variables.tf`)
* Cloud-init placeholders: `infra/cloud-init/setup-nvidia-container.sh` (stub)
* README Cloud Infrastructure section notes Terraform stubs only

This is the **M5 epic**. Child issues de-risk it: reusable Python bootstrap ([RM-95](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-95/ci-extract-reusable-workflow-for-uv-editable-install-and-pytest)), Terraform validate ([RM-96](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-96/ciinfra-add-terraform-fmt-and-validate-for-azure-scaffold-on-pr)), Docker PR smoke ([RM-97](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-97/cicontainer-add-pr-docker-build-smoke-workflow-cpu-image-no-registry)), config contracts ([RM-98](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-98/ci-validate-training-configs-and-artifact-contracts-on-pull-request)), Azure OIDC dry-run ([RM-99](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-99/ciazure-add-workflow-dispatch-oidc-login-dry-run-for-azure-no-deploy)).

## Repo surfaces

| Area | Paths |

title: [agoge-forger] GH#20 — Add agoge cleanup-run to prune checkpoints after export
description:
## Context

After `agoge export-final-model` (or a successful train that leaves a final adapter at the run root), HF/transformers still leaves full `checkpoint-*` trees under `adapters/<run_name>/`. In-run retention via `save_total_limit` (default **2**, shipped in GH#17 / RM-89 and wired in `trainer.py` → `TrainingArguments`) only caps growth **during** training. There is no post-export operator command to reclaim disk once a final PEFT adapter (and/or merged model) is the durable artifact.

Cleanup must be conservative: never remove the only recoverable weights, never touch merged outputs, final adapter files, `artifact_index.json`, or run manifests.

## Repo surfaces

| Path | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `src/agoge_forger/cli.py` | Add `cleanup_run` → `agoge cleanup-run`; no cleanup command today |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/checkpoints.py` | `list_valid_checkpoints`, `is_valid_checkpoint`, `is_adapter_artifact`, `CHECKPOINT_RE` — **source of truth** for what is a checkpoint |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/preflight.py` | `_directory_size_bytes` for dry-run byte accounting; free-space patterns if logging reclaim |
| `src/agoge_forger/export/merge_adapter.py` | Export leaves merged trees **outside** `run_dir` by default (`--out-dir`); cleanup must not require merge dir under run |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/trainer.py` | Final adapter + `artifact_index.json` written to `output_dir/run_name`; `save_total_limit` already applied mid-train |
| `src/agoge_forger/config.py` | `save_total_limit: int \| None = 2` — semantic alignment for `--keep-latest` default story |
| `src/agoge_forger/manifests.py` | `runs/<run_name>/manifest.json` — **outside** adapter run_dir; still must never be deleted if present under run_dir copies |
| `src/agoge_forger/path_safety.py` | Resolve `run_dir` safely before any `shutil.rmtree` |
| `tests/test_checkpoints.py` | Reuse `_write_checkpoint` / `_write_final_adapter` fixtures |
| `README.md` | Document recommended flow: export → status → cleanup |

**Protected names (do not delete):** anything that is not a `checkpoint-N` directory matching validity rules — especially root `adapter_model.safetensors`, `adapter_config.json`, `artifact_index.json`, `manifest.json`, tokenizer files, and any merged model path outside the checkpoint set.

## Implementation plan

1. **Library helper** — e.g. `plan_checkpoint_cleanup(run_dir, *, keep_latest: int = 0, allow_unsafe: bool = False) -> CleanupPlan` with:
   * candidates: valid (or all matching `checkpoint-*`?) dirs sorted by step
   * keep set: last `N` by step when `--keep-latest N` (`N=0` → delete all checkpoints once final artifact OK)
   * estimated `bytes_reclaimable` via `_directory_size_bytes`
   * `final_artifact_present: bool` — `is_adapter_artifact(run_dir)` **or** documented equivalent “exportable final” signal; refuse otherwise unless `--force`
2. **Safety policy**
   * Default: require final adapter at run root (`is_adapter_artifact(run_dir)`). Checkpoints alone are **not** enough to auto-delete (operator would lose recovery path).
   * `--force`: allow pruning checkpoints without final adapter **only** with loud warning; still never delete non-`checkpoint-*` paths
   * Only delete directories whose names match `^checkpoint-(\d+)$` and that the plan selected; never recursive-delete the run root
3. **CLI** — `agoge cleanup-run <run_dir>`:
   * `--dry-run` (default **true** is safest; or require explicit `--execute` / `--yes` — pick one and document; prefer dry-run default **or** require affirmative flag for destructive path)
   * `--keep-latest N` aligned with retention semantics of `save_total_limit`
   * `--force` for override when no final artifact
   * `--allow-unsafe-serialization` only affects recognition helpers if needed; does not relax path allowlists
4. **Logging** — list each path + size; total bytes; “would delete” vs “deleted”
5. **Tests** — dry-run no filesystem mutation; execute removes only selected checkpoints; keep-latest retains N highest steps; refuse without final artifact; force path; protected files remain
6. **Docs** — README: after `export-final-model`, `run-status` then `cleanup-run --dry-run` then execute

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `agoge cleanup-run <run_dir>` supports dry-run and execute modes with clear logging of candidates and estimated/actual bytes reclaimed
- [ ] Only `checkpoint-*` directories under `run_dir` are ever removed; final adapter, tokenizer files, `artifact_index.json`, manifests, and merged outputs are never deleted
- [ ] Safety guard: refuse destructive cleanup when no final adapter/exportable final artifact is detected, unless `--force` with an explicit warning
- [ ] `--keep-latest N` retains the N highest-step checkpoints (aligned with `save_total_limit` semantics)
- [ ] Tests cover: dry-run byte accounting, keep-latest behavior, refusal without final artifact, force override, and “protected files untouched”
- [ ] README documents recommended cleanup flow after `agoge export-final-model`
- [ ] Labels unchanged; GH#20 attachment retained

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/test_cleanup_run.py tests/test_checkpoints.py -q
# dry-run first
agoge cleanup-run adapters/<run_name> --dry-run
# after export + final adapter present
agoge cleanup-run adapters/<run_name> --keep-latest 0   # or explicit --execute per chosen UX
agoge run-status adapters/<run_name>   # once RM-90 lands: zero checkpoints expected
```

## Non-goals

* Changing mid-train `save_total_limit` behavior (already shipped)
* Deleting merged model directories or HF/Unsloth caches (`preflight` monitors those separately)
* Implementing remote object-store cleanup
* Interactive TUI confirmation beyond CLI flags
* Auto-running cleanup at the end of `export-final-model` (keep export pure; cleanup is opt-in)

## GitHub

* Issue: [https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/20](<https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/20>)
* Builds on export/resume GH#16 and retention GH#17 (RM-89 Done)
* Complements RM-90 (`run-status`) — status before/after cleanup
* Milestone: **M3 — Run lifecycle CLI**
