Retention and disk preflight already shipped on GitHub (#17/#19).

title: [agoge-forger] GH#18 — Add agoge run-status for checkpoint and export readiness
description:
## Context

Operators finishing a Qwen3.5 (or any) PEFT run under `adapters/<run_name>/` currently have no first-class way to answer: *is this resume-ready, export-ready, or already finalized?* Discovery logic already lives in library helpers (`list_valid_checkpoints`, `find_latest_valid_checkpoint`, `resolve_export_source`, `is_adapter_artifact`, `infer_base_model_from_adapter`), and `export-final-model` / resume already consume them — but the CLI has no read-only status command. In-run retention (`save_total_limit`, default `2`) is already shipped (GH#17 / RM-89); this issue is the operator-facing **status** half of M3 run lifecycle.

Typical on-disk layout after train:

```
adapters/<run_name>/
  adapter_config.json              # final adapter at run root (preferred export source)
  adapter_model.safetensors
  artifact_index.json
  checkpoint-50/
  checkpoint-100/
  ...
runs/<run_name>/manifest.json      # reproducibility manifest (outside adapter tree)
merged/<run_name>/                 # optional export target (not under run_dir by default)
```

## Repo surfaces

| Path | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `src/agoge_forger/cli.py` | Typer app; today has `export-final-model`, `merge-adapter`, train, smoke-eval — **no** `run-status` |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/checkpoints.py` | `is_adapter_artifact`, `is_valid_checkpoint`, `list_valid_checkpoints`, `find_latest_valid_checkpoint`, `infer_base_model_from_adapter`, `resolve_resume_checkpoint`, `resolve_export_source` |
| `src/agoge_forger/export/merge_adapter.py` | `export_final_model` / `merge_adapter` — export path selection via `resolve_export_source` |
| `src/agoge_forger/path_safety.py` | `resolve_existing_path` (reject `..`, require existing dir) — reuse at CLI boundary |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/preflight.py` | Disk helpers (`_directory_size_bytes`, free-space report) — optional for size fields |
| `src/agoge_forger/config.py` | `TrainingConfig.save_total_limit` (default `2`) already wired into `TrainingArguments` |
| `tests/test_checkpoints.py` | Fixtures `_write_checkpoint` / `_write_final_adapter`; patterns for incomplete & legacy-bin cases |
| `README.md` | Sections 6–7 document resume + `export-final-model`; needs a short status example |

**Not present today:** any `run_status` / `run-status` command, stable status JSON schema, or CLI tests for status.

## Implementation plan

1. **Library helper (preferred)** — add a pure function e.g. `build_run_status_report(run_dir: PathLike, *, allow_unsafe: bool = False, merged_dir: PathLike | None = None) -> dict` next to checkpoint helpers (either in `checkpoints.py` or a small `train/run_status.py` imported by CLI). Must call existing helpers only; no re-implementation of validity rules.
2. **CLI** — `@app.command()` `run_status` (Typer → `agoge run-status`):
   * Arg: `run_dir` (required directory)
   * Options: `--format json|table` (default `json`), `--allow-unsafe-serialization` (mirror other adapter commands), optional `--merged-dir` for explicit merged-model presence check
   * Path: `resolve_existing_path(run_dir, must_be_dir=True)`; map missing/invalid to non-zero exit (`typer.Exit(1)` / `BadParameter`)
3. **Report fields (stable JSON keys)** — document in tests as the contract:
   * `run_dir` (resolved absolute path)
   * `valid_checkpoint_count`, `valid_checkpoints` (sorted step list or paths), `latest_checkpoint_step`, `latest_checkpoint_path`
   * `resume_checkpoint_path` — same selection as `find_latest_valid_checkpoint` / resume-without-explicit-path
   * `has_final_adapter` — `is_adapter_artifact(run_dir)`
   * `export_source_path` — `resolve_export_source(run_dir=...)` or `null` + reason if none
   * `base_model` — from `infer_base_model_from_adapter` on export source or final adapter when available
   * `has_merged_model` / `merged_dir` — if `--merged-dir` given, or a documented heuristic only if cheap/safe (prefer explicit option over guessing)
   * Optional: `artifact_index_present`, rough size totals via preflight `_directory_size_bytes` (nice-to-have, not blocking)
4. **Table format** — human-readable one-row summary or key/value lines; JSON remains default for scripting.
5. **Tests** — extend `tests/test_checkpoints.py` or add `tests/test_run_status.py`: incomplete checkpoints skipped, final adapter preferred for export, missing dir exits non-zero, schema key set frozen.
6. **Docs** — README example after export section: `agoge run-status adapters/<run_name> | jq .`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `agoge run-status <run_dir>` exits **0** for existing inspectable directories and **non-zero** for missing / non-directory / path-safety failures
- [ ] Default output is **JSON** with a **stable key set** covered by unit tests (table is optional `--format table`)
- [ ] Reuses `checkpoints.py` (and export source resolution) — **no duplicate** checkpoint/adapter discovery logic
- [ ] Report includes: valid checkpoint count + latest step/path, final-adapter-at-root flag, resume selection path, export selection path, inferred base model when available, merged presence when provided/discoverable
- [ ] Honors safetensors-only default; `--allow-unsafe-serialization` only when explicitly opting into legacy `.bin` trees (consistent with resume/export)
- [ ] README includes a short example of interpreting the report
- [ ] Labels unchanged (`enhancement`, `training`, `Migrated`); GH attachment retained

## Validation

```bash
# after implementation
pytest tests/test_checkpoints.py tests/test_run_status.py -q
agoge run-status adapters/<run_name>
agoge run-status adapters/<run_name> --format table
agoge run-status /does/not/exist ; echo exit:$?
```

Fixture cases to cover: (1) only incomplete `checkpoint-*`, (2) mixed valid + broken, (3) final adapter at root + checkpoints, (4) exportable checkpoint-only tree, (5) empty dir.

## Non-goals

* Mutating the run tree (that is RM-92 / `cleanup-run`)
* Changing `save_total_limit` / trainer retention (already shipped)
* Remote/Hugging Face hub status; this is local filesystem only
* Full training metrics dashboard (use `runs/<run_name>/manifest.json` for that)
* Auto-detecting arbitrary merged dirs outside an explicit option without a clear, tested convention

## GitHub

* Issue: [https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/18](<https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/18>)
* Parent epic on GH: #17 (Training Lifecycle); Linear parent: RM-89 (Done — retention)
* Complements: GH#19 / disk preflight (shipped helpers), GH#20 / RM-92 cleanup
* Milestone: **M3 — Run lifecycle CLI**

title: Define accelerator backend scope and public API boundaries
description:
## Goal

Clarify what `myelin-accelerator` owns as a reusable CUDA/SNN accelerator crate/library.

## Why

The repo should become the low-level acceleration layer that other projects such as `corinth-canal`, SAAQ experiments, and future Metis/Spikenaut prototypes can depend on without copying kernels around.

## Tasks

- [ ] Write `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` describing the backend boundary.
- [ ] Define which pieces belong here: CUDA kernels, FFI bindings, memory wrappers, launch config helpers, benchmark harnesses.
- [ ] Define which pieces do **not** belong here: model-specific prompts, dataset evaluation, high-level research orchestration.
- [ ] Document expected consumers: `corinth-canal`, SNN libraries, telemetry experiments, quantization prototypes.
- [ ] Add a short module map to the README.

## Acceptance criteria

* A new contributor can tell whether a proposed CUDA/SNN feature belongs in this repo or in a higher-level repo.
* README links to architecture docs.
* Public API surface is named and separated from internal implementation modules.

title: [agoge-forger] GH#10 — Rust schema JSONL + benchgen
description:
## Context

Rust tooling in `rust-tools/` is the optional high-performance lane for **JSONL validation** and future **workload generation** (benchgen). Python remains source of truth for dataset row normalization and training (`src/agoge_forger/datasets.py`, `docs/contracts/dataset_jsonl.md`).

**Partially shipped (syntax-only validate):**

| Piece | Location |
| -- | -- |
| JSON **syntax** validator | `rust-tools/crates/agoge-jsonl` — `validate_file` (serde_json parse per non-empty line; 1-indexed errors) |
| CLI | `rust-tools/crates/agoge-cli` — `agoge-cli validate <file>` |
| Example | `rust-tools/examples/validate_jsonl.rs` |
| Workspace | members: `agoge-cli`, `agoge-jsonl`, `agoge-gguf` only — no benchgen crate yet |
| Docs | `rust-tools/README.md` minimal; polyglot notes `workload.jsonl` as **planned** |

**Not done:** schema-aware dataset validation (Formats A/B/C) and `agoge-benchgen` deterministic workload generator.

No dependency on TRL train fix ([RM-209](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig)).

## Repo surfaces

| Surface | Notes |
| -- | -- |
| `docs/contracts/dataset_jsonl.md` | Formats A `text`, B `messages`, C `instruction`/`input`/`output` |
| `docs/contracts/polyglot_boundaries.md` | Rust = syntax preflight + future benchgen; Python owns schema for train |
| `docs/contracts/benchmark_event_jsonl.md` | Downstream consumer shape for serving benches |
| `datasets/samples/tiny_sft.jsonl` | Mixed A/B/C — golden accept for schema mode |
| `.github/workflows/rust_smoke_test.yml` | Optional CI smoke for workspace |
| Related Python | [RM-211](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-211/agoge-forger-gh65-harden-empty-jsonl-and-non-string-message-content) / GH#65 dataset hardening |

## Implementation plan

### 1. Schema validation (`--schema dataset` or similar)

* Extend `agoge-jsonl` + CLI flag; default remains syntax-only for backward compatibility.
* Rules: object per line; require `text` (string) **or** `messages` (list of `{role,content}` with valid roles + string content) **or** `instruction` (string); 1-indexed errors.
* Do **not** reimplement full Python normalization — structural preflight only.

### 2. `agoge-benchgen`

* New crate or `agoge-cli` subcommand generating deterministic JSONL workloads under `runs/<run_name>/` (e.g. `workload.jsonl`).
* Seeded, reproducible; useful for [RM-84](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-84/agoge-forger-gh5-vllm-model-compatibility-smoke)/[RM-83](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-83/agoge-forger-gh4-vllm-rust-frontend-benchmark) serving benches.
* Stay out of default Python install.

### 3. Docs + CI

* Expand `rust-tools/README.md` (syntax vs schema, benchgen examples).
* Wire schema tests + sample validate into `rust_smoke_test` if cheap.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Schema mode accepts `datasets/samples/tiny_sft.jsonl` and rejects known-bad fixtures (missing keys, bad roles, non-object lines).
- [ ] Default/syntax mode behavior unchanged for valid JSON lines that are not dataset-shaped (or document if tightened).
- [ ] Benchgen writes deterministic files under `runs/<run_name>/` given fixed seed.
- [ ] `cargo check` / existing rust smoke still green.
- [ ] Docs describe optional install: `cd rust-tools && cargo run -p agoge-cli -- validate ...`.

## Validation

* Unit tests in `agoge-jsonl` for good/bad fixtures.
* CLI integration: validate sample + fixture dir.
* Benchgen: two runs same seed → identical output hash.

## Non-goals

* Replacing Python dataset validation for training.
* FFI into Python training loop.
* Full OpenAI chat API fuzzer (workload gen is prompt/dataset oriented).
* vLLM frontend work ([RM-83](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-83/agoge-forger-gh4-vllm-rust-frontend-benchmark)).

## Dependencies

* None on [RM-209](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig).
* Related: [RM-211](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-211/agoge-forger-gh65-harden-empty-jsonl-and-non-string-message-content) (Python dataset hardening); consumers [RM-84](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-84/agoge-forger-gh5-vllm-model-compatibility-smoke)/[RM-83](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-83/agoge-forger-gh4-vllm-rust-frontend-benchmark) for workloads.

title: [agoge-forger] GH#8 — Julia ML spike (Flux/Lux/MLJ/SciML)
description:
## Context

Add a **Julia ML experiment lane** to learn where Julia fits in `agoge-forger`: classical ML evaluation, differentiable scientific ML, small neural baselines, data transforms, and future model-analysis tooling.

Julia must remain **optional**. The base Python package must not require Julia. Communication is via **file contracts** only (no FFI) — see `docs/contracts/polyglot_boundaries.md`.

**Repo status (2026-08-01):**

* **No** `julia/` **directory** in tree yet.
* `.github/workflows/julia_smoke_test.yml` exists: PR path installs Julia 1.10 and reports version; `workflow_dispatch` runs `Pkg.instantiate` / test / build against configurable `project_dir` (default `.`) and writes `julia_output/*` smoke artifacts.
* Polyglot doc already reserves `runs/<run>/julia/{metrics,predictions,report}` as **planned** ML outputs (not produced by current workflow).

No dependency on TRL train fix ([RM-209](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig)). LLM training stays Python.

## Repo surfaces

| Surface | Notes |
| -- | -- |
| `.github/workflows/julia_smoke_test.yml` | PR + dispatch smoke; expects project when running full check |
| `docs/contracts/polyglot_boundaries.md` | Julia owns scientific ML / metrics aggregation experiments |
| `docs/contracts/metrics_schema.md` | Shared metrics conventions for readers |
| Dataset contracts | JSONL owned by Python; Julia may read CSV/Parquet derivatives |
| Missing | `julia/Project.toml`, scripts, `docs/julia_ml_spike.md` |

## Implementation plan

1. Scaffold `julia/Project.toml` (+ Manifest as appropriate) with Flux, Lux, MLJ, SciML stack at versions that install on CI CPU.
2. Scripts:
   * `julia/scripts/flux_smoke.jl` — tiny MLP class/reg
   * `julia/scripts/lux_smoke.jl` — MLP with explicit params/state
   * `julia/scripts/mlj_smoke.jl` — tabular baseline + model comparison
   * `julia/scripts/sciml_smoke.jl` — small neural ODE or param estimation (or documented skip)
3. I/O contract:
   * Inputs: sample CSV/features under `datasets/samples/` or `runs/<run>/features/*.parquet` (generate tiny fixtures if needed; avoid requiring full LLM JSONL for neural smokes)
   * Outputs: `runs/<run_name>/julia/metrics.json`, `predictions.csv`, `report.md`
4. Docs: `docs/julia_ml_spike.md` — which library fits which agoge role; how CI smoke relates.
5. Point `julia_smoke_test.yml` `project_dir` default at `julia/` once Project.toml exists; optionally run one smoke script on dispatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `julia --project=julia julia/scripts/flux_smoke.jl` runs.
- [ ] `julia --project=julia julia/scripts/lux_smoke.jl` runs.
- [ ] `julia --project=julia julia/scripts/mlj_smoke.jl` runs.
- [ ] SciML smoke runs **or** documents dependency/GPU limitation with non-zero-but-explained skip policy.
- [ ] Scripts write machine-readable metrics (JSON).
- [ ] `docs/julia_ml_spike.md` maps libraries → agoge roles.
- [ ] Default Python package install has zero Julia requirement.
- [ ] PR julia workflow still green (version report and/or project instantiate).

## Validation

* Local CPU: run three primary smokes.
* CI: PR path on `julia/**` changes; dispatch full smoke with artifact upload.
* Confirm outputs under `runs/.../julia/` match polyglot doc conventions.

## Non-goals

* Julia LLM training or replacing PyTorch/TRL.
* GPU optimization beyond smoke-level.
* Binding Julia into the Python CLI as a hard dependency.
* Implementing Rust JSONL work ([RM-88](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-88/rust-tools-schema-aware-jsonl-validate-agoge-benchgen-workload)).

## Dependencies

* None on [RM-209](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig) / Unsloth / vLLM.
* Soft: metrics contract alignment with Python smoke outputs for future cross-language reports.

## GitHub

title: [agoge-forger] GH#7 — Unsloth export validation
description:
## Context

Validate **export and inspection paths** for adapters/models produced by the optional Unsloth backend ([RM-85](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-85>) / GH#6). Ensure Unsloth outputs interoperate with existing PEFT-oriented tooling: merge, artifact index, safetensors inspection, smoke-eval, and (later) vLLM serving smokes.

Parent: [RM-85](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-85/trainingunsloth-add-optional-unsloth-backend-for-fast-lora-and-qlora). No Unsloth code exists in-tree yet — this issue starts after (or tightly stacked with) the backend.

Default train/export path today: `export/merge_adapter.py`, CLI `merge-adapter` / `export-final-model`, GGUF intentionally non-automatic (`export/gguf_notes.py`). Unsloth may emit PEFT-compatible adapters or its own merge/export helpers; validation must document which modes work and fail clearly otherwise.

**Train dependency:** full end-to-end proof needs a working train artifact path. Default TRL train is broken on 1.4 ([RM-209](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209>)); Unsloth export validation should use Unsloth-trained adapters once [RM-85](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-85/trainingunsloth-add-optional-unsloth-backend-for-fast-lora-and-qlora) lands, not assume fixed TRL train.

## Repo surfaces

| Surface | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `src/agoge_forger/export/merge_adapter.py` | Merge PEFT → full model + `write_artifact_index` |
| `src/agoge_forger/export/gguf_notes.py` | Documents why GGUF is manual / architecture-limited |
| `src/agoge_forger/cli.py` | `merge-adapter`, `export-final-model`, `smoke-eval`, `inspect-safetensors` |
| `src/agoge_forger/artifacts/safetensors_io.py` | Index + unsafe `.bin` policy |
| `docs/artifacts_and_safetensors.md` | Safetensors-first policy |
| Unsloth export module | **Missing** — to add under `export/` |
| Serving consumer | [RM-84](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-84>) vLLM compat smoke (can consume merged exports) |

## Implementation plan

1. Add `src/agoge_forger/export/unsloth_export.py` wrapping Unsloth save/merge APIs into agoge layout (`adapters/`, `merged/`).
2. CLI/script: `scripts/export_unsloth.py` and optional `agoge export-unsloth` if thin.
3. Config: `configs/export/unsloth_export.yaml` for adapter vs merged targets.
4. Validation matrix (doc + automated where cheap):
   * Adapter-style export readable by PEFT / smoke-eval when format matches.
   * Merged HF dir loadable and indexed.
   * GGUF: either documented success path via external llama.cpp **or** explicit failure note (align with `gguf_notes.py` — no silent bad GGUF).
5. Confirm `artifact_index.json` hashes include all weight shards + tokenizer files.
6. Wire docs: `docs/unsloth_export_compatibility.md` with known-good model families and serving handoff to [RM-84](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-84/servingvllm-add-model-compatibility-smoke-checks-for-adapters-and).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Export helpers exist and are optional (no hard Unsloth dep on base install).
- [ ] Adapter export validated (files present, safetensors policy, index written).
- [ ] Merged model export validated (index + load smoke without full serve if GPU limited).
- [ ] GGUF path either documented manual steps or structured “unsupported architecture” failure — never a false success.
- [ ] Local inspection commands (`inspect-safetensors`, adapter metadata) work on outputs.
- [ ] Docs state which outputs are valid inputs to vLLM / chat-completions smoke ([RM-84](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-84/servingvllm-add-model-compatibility-smoke-checks-for-adapters-and)).
- [ ] Parent [RM-85](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-85/trainingunsloth-add-optional-unsloth-backend-for-fast-lora-and-qlora) still required for real Unsloth-trained fixtures.

## Validation

* Unit tests with fixture layouts (mock files) for index + path safety.
* Manual: export after Unsloth smoke train; run merge/inspect; optional vLLM load of merged dir.
* Regression: default PEFT merge path unchanged.

## Non-goals

* Making Unsloth the default training backend.
* Supporting every model family Unsloth claims on day one.
* Automating llama.cpp conversion for custom/SSM architectures.
* Implementing the full vLLM matrix ([RM-84](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-84/servingvllm-add-model-compatibility-smoke-checks-for-adapters-and)) or Rust frontend bench ([RM-83](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-83/servingvllm-add-rust-frontend-support-and-python-vs-rust-benchmark)).

## Dependencies

* **Parent / blocked by [RM-85](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-85>)** (Unsloth backend must produce artifacts).
* Soft: [RM-209](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209>) for any dual-path “TRL vs Unsloth export” comparison.
* Related consumer: [RM-84](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-84>) serving smoke.

title: [agoge-forger] GH#6 — Optional Unsloth backend for LoRA/QLoRA
description:
## Context

Add **Unsloth** as an *optional* training backend alongside the existing PyTorch + Transformers + PEFT + TRL path (`src/agoge_forger/train/trainer.py`, `lora.py`, `qlora.py`).

Default install must not require Unsloth. Goal: faster LoRA/QLoRA smoke and local RTX-class experiments while reusing agoge contracts (JSONL datasets, adapter layout, `manifest.json`, `artifact_index.json`).

**Important dependency:** the default train path is **broken on TRL 1.4** ([RM-209](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/bugtraining-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig-training-broken>) / GH#63): `SFTTrainer` still uses pre-1.x kwargs (`dataset_text_field`, `max_seq_length`, `tokenizer=`). Park or implement Unsloth only after [RM-209](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig) lands (or isolate Unsloth so it never calls the broken TRL path). Comparison docs against TRL/PEFT require a working baseline train.

## Repo surfaces

| Surface | Status (2026-08-01) |
| -- | -- |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/trainer.py` | Default SFT path; TRL 1.4 API broken ([RM-209](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig)) |
| `src/agoge_forger/train/{lora,qlora,preflight,checkpoints}.py` | Existing train helpers to mirror for manifests/adapters |
| `src/agoge_forger/cli.py` | Typer CLI: `train-qlora`, `train-lora`, `smoke-eval`, merge/export — no Unsloth commands |
| `pyproject.toml` optional groups | `jax`, `dev`, `infra`, `cuda` only — **no** `unsloth` **group** |
| Unsloth in tree | **None** (only a disk-pressure path hint for `~/.unsloth/...` in preflight) |
| Configs | `configs/smoke_test.yaml`, `local_rtx5080_16gb.yaml`, etc. — no unsloth YAMLs |
| Contracts | `docs/contracts/dataset_jsonl.md`, run manifest via `manifests.write_run_manifest`, artifact index via `artifacts/safetensors_io.py` |
| Sample data | `datasets/samples/tiny_sft.jsonl` (formats A/B/C mixed) |

## Implementation plan

1. **Optional dep** — add `[project.optional-dependencies] unsloth = [...]` with pinned/compatible unsloth + its torch stack notes in docs; `pip install 'agoge-forger[unsloth]'` (or uv equivalent).
2. **Backend module** — `src/agoge_forger/train/unsloth_backend.py`:
   * Lazy import Unsloth; clear `ImportError` pointing at optional extra.
   * Load model/tokenizer via Unsloth FastLanguageModel (or current Unsloth API), apply LoRA/QLoRA, train on normalized JSONL text field.
   * Finalize like `_finalize_training_run`: save adapter under `adapters/<run>`, `write_artifact_index`, `write_run_manifest` with unsloth/torch/CUDA/GPU/dtype/quant/LoRA metadata.
3. **CLI** — `agoge train-unsloth --config ...`, `agoge inspect-unsloth-env` (versions + GPU).
4. **Configs** — `configs/unsloth_smoke.yaml` (tiny steps), `configs/local_rtx5080_unsloth.yaml` (16GB-aware defaults aligned with existing local config philosophy).
5. **Scripts + tests** — `scripts/train_unsloth.py` thin wrapper; `tests/test_unsloth_config.py` for config/import-guard (no GPU required in unit tests).
6. **Docs** — `docs/unsloth_backend.md`: install path, vs TRL/PEFT table, known model family limits, link to [RM-209](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig) status for baseline comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unsloth is optional; base/`[dev]` install and CI Python smoke do not import or require it.
- [ ] Missing Unsloth raises a clear error naming the optional install path.
- [ ] `agoge train-unsloth --config configs/unsloth_smoke.yaml` runs a tiny smoke train on a GPU host.
- [ ] Adapter artifacts land under `adapters/` (safetensors-first; same unsafe-bin policy as default train).
- [ ] Writes `runs/<run_name>/manifest.json` (or equivalent run dir used by existing helpers).
- [ ] Writes `artifact_index.json` on the adapter output dir.
- [ ] Manifest/metrics capture: Unsloth version, torch, CUDA, GPU name, dtype, quantization mode, LoRA config.
- [ ] Doc compares Unsloth backend vs TRL/PEFT path (throughput/VRAM notes allowed to be qualitative on first pass).
- [ ] Does not regress default CLI when Unsloth is absent.

## Validation

* Unit: config parse + import guard without Unsloth installed.
* Manual GPU: smoke train on tiny_sft + inspect adapter with existing `agoge smoke-eval` / `inspect-safetensors` if PEFT-compatible.
* Confirm `make train-smoke` / default TRL path still tracked under [RM-209](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig) separately.

## Non-goals

* Making Unsloth the default backend.
* Multi-GPU / DeepSpeed / FSDP.
* RL (DPO/PPO/GRPO) via Unsloth in this issue.
* Fixing TRL 1.4 default trainer ([RM-209](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig) owns that).

## Dependencies

* **Blocked by [RM-209](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209>)** for fair baseline comparison and any shared finalization that still assumes a working TRL train. Prefer shipping Unsloth only after train path is green, or hard-isolate so Unsloth never imports broken `SFTTrainer` kwargs.
* Child: [RM-86](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-86>) (export validation) depends on this backend existing.

title: [agoge-forger] GH#5 — vLLM model compatibility smoke
description:
## Context

There is no automated or scripted smoke that proves models produced by `agoge-forger` (PEFT adapters or merged safetensors exports) **actually serve** under local vLLM / OpenAI-compatible chat completions.

A thin client already exists (closed GH#3):

* `src/agoge_forger/providers/chat_completions.py` — `ChatCompletionsClient` / `ChatCompletionsConfig`
* Docs: `docs/chat_completions_providers.md`
* Tests: `tests/test_chat_completions_provider.py` (mock HTTP; maps connect/timeout errors)

This issue is the **compatibility matrix + smoke entrypoint**, not another client.

**Train dependency:** full adapter/merged matrix needs real train artifacts. Default train is **broken on TRL 1.4** ([RM-209](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209>)). Client-only tests can ship now; end-to-end “train → merge → serve” remains blocked until train is fixed (or Unsloth path [RM-85](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-85/agoge-forger-gh6-optional-unsloth-backend-for-loraqlora)/86 provides fixtures).

## Repo surfaces

| Surface | Notes |
| -- | -- |
| `providers/chat_completions.py` | `base_url` default `http://localhost:8000/v1`, stream + non-stream, raw dumps under `runs/<run>/raw/` |
| `InferenceResult` | latency_ms, TTFT, tokens, finish_reason, error |
| `docs/contracts/benchmark_event_jsonl.md` | Result/event schema for smoke/bench producers |
| `export/merge_adapter.py` + CLI merge/export | Produce merged HF dirs for vLLM `--model` |
| `eval/smoke_eval.py` | Local generation smoke on adapter (not HTTP serve) |
| No `serve_vllm` / vLLM install in pyproject | Serving remains external process |
| Child | [RM-83](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-83>) Rust frontend benchmark |

## Implementation plan

1. **Docs matrix** — supported serve modes: base HF id, merged safetensors directory, adapter+base if vLLM LoRA supported for that family; known-broken pairs (tiny CI model vs local 0.5B–8B).
2. **Smoke entry** — script and/or `agoge serve-smoke` / `smoke-vllm` that:
   * targets endpoint via config/env (`base_url`, `model`, optional `api_key`)
   * sends minimal chat completion (stream + non-stream optional)
   * writes structured results under `runs/<run_name>/` (align with `InferenceResult` and/or benchmark_event JSONL)
3. **Failure UX** — clear messaging when endpoint down (reuse client error strings: connection refused, timeout, HTTP status).
4. **CI** — client half with mock HTTP (extend existing tests); GPU-backed vLLM via `workflow_dispatch` only if feasible.
5. Link from README and `docs/chat_completions_providers.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Smoke can target `http://localhost:8000/v1` with documented flags/env.
- [ ] Success and failure paths write structured results under `runs/`.
- [ ] README or `docs/chat_completions_providers.md` links the smoke path.
- [ ] Compat matrix documents base / merged / adapter modes.
- [ ] No GPU required for client unit tests; live serve is manual or dispatch.
- [ ] Does not reimplement the chat client.

## Validation

* pytest mock server success + connect failure.
* Manual: start vLLM with a small HF model → smoke; optional merged export after train (post [RM-209](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig)).
* Confirm raw response files still land under `runs/<run>/raw/`.

## Non-goals

* Rust vLLM frontend / Python-vs-Rust bench → [RM-83](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-83/servingvllm-add-rust-frontend-support-and-python-vs-rust-benchmark) / GH#4.
* Unsloth-specific export validation → [RM-86](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-86/agoge-forger-gh7-unsloth-export-validation) / GH#7.
* Vendoring or packaging vLLM inside agoge-forger.
* Fixing TRL train ([RM-209](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig)) — but E2E adapter serve depends on it.

## Dependencies

* **Soft-blocked by [RM-209](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209>)** for adapter/merged artifacts from the default train path.
* Related: Unsloth export compatibility ([RM-86](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-86/agoge-forger-gh7-unsloth-export-validation)) may supply alternate fixtures.
* Child: [RM-83](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-83/servingvllm-add-rust-frontend-support-and-python-vs-rust-benchmark) (Rust frontend bench) should reuse this smoke client/metrics shape.

## GitHub

title: [agoge-forger] GH#4 — vLLM Rust frontend benchmark
description:
## Context

Add a **vLLM serving lane** that compares the default Python frontend against vLLM’s Rust frontend path (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND`), while keeping `agoge-forger` Python-first for training.

Parent: [RM-84](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-84>) (model compatibility smoke / client). Reuse `ChatCompletionsClient` for load generation and metrics rather than a second HTTP stack.

**Note:** meaningful benches need a stable serve path ([RM-84](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-84/agoge-forger-gh5-vllm-model-compatibility-smoke)) and, for adapter/merged scenarios, working train/export artifacts. Default train is broken on TRL 1.4 ([RM-209](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209>)) — base HF model benches can proceed; LoRA-adapter dimensions wait on train/export.

## Repo surfaces

| Surface | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `providers/chat_completions.py` | Load gen + latency/TTFT/tokens |
| `docs/chat_completions_providers.md` | Client config |
| `docs/contracts/benchmark_event_jsonl.md` | Event schema for `results.jsonl` |
| `docs/contracts/polyglot_boundaries.md` | Python owns inference client; Rust optional tooling |
| `rust-tools/` | Separate JSONL/CLI workspace — **not** the vLLM Rust frontend (upstream vLLM) |
| Missing | `scripts/serve_vllm.py`, `bench_vllm_frontend.py`, `configs/serving/*`, `docs/vllm_rust_frontend.md` |

## Implementation plan

1. **Serve wrapper** — `scripts/serve_vllm.py` / `agoge serve-vllm`:
   * `--frontend python` → `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0`
   * `--frontend rust` → `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`
   * Fail with diagnostic if Rust frontend unsupported on installed vLLM version.
2. **Bench harness** — `scripts/bench_vllm_frontend.py` / `agoge bench-vllm-frontend`:
   * prompt set YAML (short/long)
   * concurrency levels, stream vs non-stream
   * emit `results.jsonl`, `summary.md`, `comparison.csv` under `runs/<run_name>/`
3. **Configs** — `configs/serving/vllm_python_frontend.yaml`, `vllm_rust_frontend.yaml`.
4. **Docs** — `docs/vllm_rust_frontend.md`: env vars, version pins, reproduce steps, known limitations.
5. Capture environment: vLLM version, CUDA, GPU name, frontend env vars, CPU util / RSS if cheap (`psutil` optional).

## Benchmark dimensions

- [ ] Python frontend vs Rust frontend
- [ ] Streaming vs non-streaming
- [ ] Short vs long prompts
- [ ] Low vs high concurrency
- [ ] Base model vs LoRA adapter (when artifacts available)
- [ ] CPU utilization, RSS
- [ ] p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, time to first token

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `agoge serve-vllm --frontend rust` launches vLLM with Rust frontend enabled (or documents exact upstream flag if renamed).
- [ ] Unavailable Rust frontend → clear non-zero failure, not hang.
- [ ] Bench emits `results.jsonl`, `summary.md`, `comparison.csv` with Python-vs-Rust table.
- [ ] Report includes vLLM/CUDA/GPU/env fingerprint.
- [ ] Docs explain full reproduce path.
- [ ] Client metrics reuse existing provider types where practical.

## Validation

* Dry-run/config parse without GPU.
* Manual GPU: same model, both frontends, smoke prompt set; compare TTFT/latency.
* Adapter row optional until [RM-209](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig)/[RM-84](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-84/agoge-forger-gh5-vllm-model-compatibility-smoke) fixtures exist.

## Non-goals

* Vendoring the Rust frontend or forking vLLM.
* Replacing Python training with Rust.
* Implementing schema JSONL / benchgen in `rust-tools` (that is [RM-88](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-88/rust-tools-schema-aware-jsonl-validate-agoge-benchgen-workload)).
* Making Rust frontend the default serve path.

## Dependencies

* **Parent:** [RM-84](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-84>) smoke/client conventions.
* **Soft:** [RM-209](<https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209>) for adapter-backed dimensions; base-model bench is independent.
* Related: [RM-88](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-88/rust-tools-schema-aware-jsonl-validate-agoge-benchgen-workload) benchgen can later feed prompt workloads.

## GitHub

* [https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/4](<https://github.com/rmems/agoge-forger/issues/4>)

title: [#118] hotspot 7: run_validation is 369 lines with a 4x copy-pasted epilogue
description:
Sub-task of [#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>).

## Summary

`run_validation` in `examples/saaq_latent_calibration.rs:201-569` is 369 lines, and contains the
same ~35-line failure epilogue **four times** — at `:283`, `:346`, `:486`, and `:525`. Only the
status string and the error value differ:

```rust
write_manifest_and_summary(ctx, &config, &model, &run_dir, &manifest_path,
    &summary_path, &tick_path, &latent_path, <src>, saaq_rule, <STATUS>, <err>,
    &metrics, collect_generated_files(&manifest_path, &summary_path,
        &[&tick_path, &latent_path, &routing_csv_path]))?;
pending.push(pending_row_from_state(ctx, &model, &run_dir, &latent_path,
    &summary_path, &metrics, <STATUS>));
emit_validation_finish(observer, ctx, validation_started, <STATUS>, <err>);
```

## Proposed fix

Extract a `Finalizer<'a>` holding `{ observer, ctx, config, paths, prompt_embedding_source, saaq_rule, started }` with:

```rust
fn finish(&self, model: &Model, metrics: &_, pending: &mut Vec<_>,
          status: &str, error: Option<&str>)
```

Removes ~110 lines and kills the three `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` at `:571`, `:665`,
`:713`.

**Design constraint:** do **not** capture `&model` in the struct. The tick loop holds `&mut model`,
so a `Finalizer` borrowing it immutably will not compile. `model` must stay an explicit parameter of
`finish`.

## Do this LAST, and gate it on evidence rather than on CI

Three reasons this is the riskiest item in the [#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>) set despite looking mechanical:

1. The file is `required-features = ["cuda"]`, so `cargo check --all-targets --no-default-features`
   never compiles it and hosted CI never sees it.
2. It is already Codacy-excluded, so there is no tooling pressure either.
3. `summary.json` **and** `run_manifest.json` **are parsed downstream** by
   `examples/summarize_local_saaq.rs`, `examples/validate_local_saaq.rs`, and `Surrogate_Viz.jl`. A
   silently reordered or dropped field breaks the analysis pipeline, and **nothing tests it**.

### Required extra gate

Run one real calibration before and after, and `diff` the artifacts byte-for-byte:

```bash
just saaq   # before
just saaq   # after
diff artifacts/<run>/summary.json      artifacts/<run>/summary.json
diff artifacts/<run>/run_manifest.json artifacts/<run>/run_manifest.json
```

**If you cannot get GPU time, do not merge this.** The line saving is not worth an unverifiable
change to the artifact schema.

## Lower-risk pieces of the same file, separable

If the epilogue work stalls, these are self-contained and can move independently:

* CSV index writing — `flush_index_csv:838`, `ensure_index_header_compatible:866`,
  `format_index_row:894`, `csv_escape:922`, `PendingIndexRow:25` — ~130 lines →
  `examples/support/index_csv.rs`
* Date math — `format_local_timestamp_compact:1076`, `civil_from_unix_secs:1093` — ~40 lines →
  `examples/support/timefmt.rs`

Note both destinations sit in `examples/support/`, whose tests never run ([#141](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-235/testing-examplessupportmodrs-unit-tests-never-execute)) — so land any
extracted logic with tests somewhere that executes, or accept it is unguarded.

## Note

[#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>)'s body lists five hotspots; this is not among them. [#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>) should be edited to add it as
hotspot 7.

title: gpu: unreachable public accelerator API and stale dead_code allows
description:
Prerequisite for [#145](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-238/myelin-accelerator-upstream-gifsaaq-kernels-shim-before-the-119-swap) / [#119](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/119>) — don't upstream unreachable code into myelin-accelerator.

## Root cause worth stating first

All of `src/gpu/**` is `#[cfg(feature = "cuda")]`, and CI runs `--no-default-features`. **No CI job****
****ever compiles this code.** That is why the rot accumulated invisibly, and it is the reason this
issue is worth doing before any extraction.

## Verified caller counts

An earlier analysis pass reported two of these as dead. **Both are live** — deleting them would
break every GPU tick. Corrected here so the mistake isn't repeated:

| Item | Location | Callers | Action |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `saaq_find_best_walker` | `accelerator.rs:615` | **3** — `:461` inside `gif_step_weighted_tick` (GPU hot path), `:882`, `:914` | **Keep.** Narrow `pub fn` → `fn` |
| `page_size_bytes` | `cuda_register.rs:127,141` | **1** — `:47` | **Keep.** Drop the stale `#[allow(dead_code)]` |
| `temporal_adaptation_to_vec` | `accelerator.rs:263` | **0** (siblings `temporal_spikes_to_vec`/`temporal_membrane_to_vec` have 4 each) | Remove |
| `load_synapse_weights` | `accelerator.rs:299` | **0** — one-line alias for `load_synapse_weights_named`, which every real caller uses. Only named in a doc comment at `model/temporal.rs:14` | Remove |
| `src/tensor/mod.rs` | whole module, 15 lines | **0** anywhere in `src/`, `examples/`, `tests/` | Remove + drop `pub mod tensor;` |
| `satsolver_extract` | `accelerator.rs:548`, 67 lines | **0 Rust callers** | **Decide, don't reflex-delete** — see below |

## Open question: `satsolver_extract`

Not obviously abandoned:

* Its CUDA kernel is a **load-time requirement** (`kernel.rs:111` lists it in the module's function
  table).
* Its sibling `satsolver_aux_reduce_best` **is** live (`src/model/core.rs:193`).
* `tests/gpu_sentry_telemetry.rs:172` references `"satsolver_extract"` as a kernel-name string.

So the SAT path is **half-wired, not dead**: the reducer runs but the read-back wrapper has no
caller. Deleting `satsolver_extract` removes the only way to read a solution back out. Is this
unfinished work or abandoned work? Answer before touching it.

## Note on `src/tensor/mod.rs`

Removing `pub mod tensor;` from `src/lib.rs` is a **public API removal**. Precedent exists ([#97](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/97>) /
`677b9ac`) and the crate is unpublished (`version = "0.1.0"`, not on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>)), so the cost is
zero — but that is why this should be a `chore(gpu):` PR and not a `refactor(...): (GH#118 PR-N)`
one, whose pattern promises zero API change.

`src/tensor/` was also the target of a proposed re-homing into `Limen-Neural/cortex-tensor` (whose
README cites SpikeLMo → corinth-canal lineage). Since nothing consumes it, deletion and re-homing
are the same act — worth a line in the PR body.

## Verification

This is the one area the normal gate cannot check:

```bash
cargo check  --all-targets --features cuda,gpu-stub
cargo clippy --all-targets --features cuda,gpu-stub -- -D warnings   # note: WITHOUT -A dead_code
cargo test --test gpu_sentry_telemetry                                # on hardware
```

Running clippy without `-A dead_code` is the point — it makes the sweep prove what it claims.

## Related

[#145](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-238/myelin-accelerator-upstream-gifsaaq-kernels-shim-before-the-119-swap) (myelin upstreaming, blocked on this), [#119](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/119>), [#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>)

title: [#118] hotspot 6: split src/moe/safetensors.rs (1780 lines, two unrelated jobs)
description:

## Summary

`src/moe/safetensors.rs` is 1780 lines doing **two unrelated jobs**: header-only inspection +
deterministic manifest generation, and mmap'd tensor loading.

## The real argument — this is [#116](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/116>)'s extraction boundary

Line count alone is a weak case in a repo whose `.codacy.yml` already says architectural complexity
is intentional. The actual payoff: [#116](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/116>) **wants the inspection/manifest/MoE-candidate logic copied****
****into a new** `Limen-Neural/safetensors-parser` **crate, with no dependency back on corinth.** The split
below draws exactly that line in code, so the extraction becomes a copy of whole files instead of a
careful dissection of one.

* **Extractable half:** `manifest.rs`, `validate.rs`, `json.rs`, `discovery.rs`
* **corinth-specific half:** `config.rs`, `map.rs` (mmap, HF config, `MappedSafetensorsCheckpoint`)

## Proposed split

The directory `src/moe/safetensors/` already exists (`discovery.rs`, `tests.rs`), and
`safetensors.rs:31` already does `mod discovery; pub use discovery::{...}` — the façade pattern is
in use inside this very file. Same shape as PR-4 ([rmems/corinth-canal#128](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-split-checkpointrs-into-private-gguf-modules-gh118-pr-4-230bc5f503d8)).

| Module | Source range | ~lines | Contents |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `manifest.rs` | `:40-505` | 465 | `SafetensorsManifest`, `inspect_*`, `build_manifest` |
| `validate.rs` | `:506-727` | 220 | `reject_tensor_data_ranges`, `expected_tensor_byte_size`, `dtype_size_bytes` |
| `paths.rs` | `:728-928` | 200 | `paths_refer_to_same_file`, **all Win32 unsafe FFI**, `validate_path_stays_under_root` |
| `json.rs` | `:930-1073` | 145 | `NoDuplicateValue` visitor, `parse_json_rejecting_duplicate_keys` |
| `config.rs` | `:1112-1303` | 190 | `HfConfig`, `HfTextConfig`, scalar-or-singleton deserializer |
| `map.rs` | `:1075-1110`, `:1305-1777` | 510 | `MappedSafetensorsCheckpoint`, shard maps, `bf16_to_f32` |

## Suggested PR order

Four PRs — one 1780-line reshuffle is not reviewable, and the AI reviewers get noisy above ~500
lines.

1. `paths.rs` + `json.rs` (~345) — **first**, because it corrals all 9 `unsafe`
   `GetFileInformationByHandle` blocks (`:754-846`) into one file behind one
   `#[allow(unsafe_code)]`. That is a security-review win independent of everything else, and it is
   the piece most likely to want a Windows reviewer.
2. `manifest.rs` + `validate.rs` (~685)
3. `config.rs` + `map.rs` (~700); `safetensors.rs` becomes a ~45-line façade
4. Decompose `MappedSafetensorsCheckpoint::from_directory` (`:1401`, ~200 lines) into
   `resolve_shard_layout` / `map_and_index_shard` / `finalize`. **Only PR with logic change** —
   verify with a before/after `diff` of a real manifest.

## External surface to preserve

Only five names, so no call-site churn: `MappedSafetensorsCheckpoint`, `SafetensorsMetadata`,
`dtype_size_bytes` (`pub(super)`), `write_safetensors_manifest`, `SafetensorsTensorRecord`.
`examples/safetensors_manifest.rs:10` is the only out-of-crate consumer.

## Two mechanical traps

* `src/moe/safetensors/tests.rs` (1031 lines) opens with `use super::*` and reaches six private
  helpers directly (`merge_shard_metadata` ×5, `build_manifest` ×4,
  `shard_metadata_namespaced_key` ×3, `paths_refer_to_same_file` ×3, `parent_or_current`,
  `canonical_existing_or_parent`). Glob-import them back into the façade (`use manifest::*;`) so
  `use super::*` keeps resolving — child modules see a parent's private `use` items, so this needs
  no visibility widening. **Those 1031 lines are the regression net: if a test body has to change,****
****the extraction wasn't pure.**
* `.codacy.yml` lists `src/moe/safetensors.rs` and `src/moe/safetensors/tests.rs` separately.
  Replace both with `src/moe/safetensors/**` **in PR 1**, before the new files exist, so the Codacy
  gate never sees an unexcluded file.

## Docs (per the [#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>) pattern)

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:114` becomes a submodule table like the `moe/gguf/` row at `:111`;
`docs/MODULE_STATUS.md` gains a `src/moe/safetensors/` row; `manifests/proven_components.toml`
mirrors it — with `target_repo` reading `Limen-Neural/safetensors-parser` per [#116](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/116>), not `rmems-moe`.

## Verification

`cargo test --no-default-features safetensors` must pass with `safetensors/tests.rs` **unmodified****
****except for** `use` **lines**, plus
`cargo check --example safetensors_manifest --no-default-features`.

## Note

[#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>)'s body lists five hotspots and safetensors is not among them (its hotspot 3 was
`checkpoint.rs`, done in [rmems/corinth-canal#128](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-split-checkpointrs-into-private-gguf-modules-gh118-pr-4-230bc5f503d8)). [#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>) should be edited to add this as hotspot 6.

title: process: never base a PR on another feature branch (root cause of the PR-2 loss)
description:
## What happened

PR [rmems/corinth-canal#126](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-priority-ordered-gguf-synapse-source-selection-gh118-pr-2-94fb0e345288) (`GH#118 PR-2`, priority-ordered GGUF synapse selection) shows **MERGED** on GitHub. None of
its code ever reached `main`.

```
$ git grep select_gguf_synapse origin/main -- src/moe/adapter.rs
(no output)
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor ebf8162 origin/main; echo $?
1
```

The nested `if real.is_none() && q8_0.is_none() && ...` chain that PR was written to remove — [#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>)'s
own **hotspot 2** — was still live at `src/moe/adapter.rs:150-229` more than three weeks later.

## Mechanism

1. [rmems/corinth-canal#126](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-priority-ordered-gguf-synapse-source-selection-gh118-pr-2-94fb0e345288) was opened with base `refactor/gh118-unify-infer-family` (the PR-1 branch), not `main`.
2. [rmems/corinth-canal#125](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-unify-ggufsafetensors-family-inference-gh118-pr-1-8cb787b01547) squash-merged PR-1 into `main` and deleted its branch.
3. GitHub saw [rmems/corinth-canal#126](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-priority-ordered-gguf-synapse-source-selection-gh118-pr-2-94fb0e345288)'s head commits reachable from the deleted base and marked [rmems/corinth-canal#126](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-priority-ordered-gguf-synapse-source-selection-gh118-pr-2-94fb0e345288) **merged**.
4. The squash collapsed PR-1's history into one new commit on `main`. [rmems/corinth-canal#126](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-priority-ordered-gguf-synapse-source-selection-gh118-pr-2-94fb0e345288)'s changes were never part
   of that squash — they lived only on the child branch.
5. Result: green checkmark, closed issue link, zero code.

Issue [#134](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/134>) stayed open, which is the only reason this was recoverable — the work survived on an
unpushed local branch and has now been restored in [rmems/corinth-canal#138](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-recover-priority-ordered-gguf-synapse-source-selection-69a98e2563b5).

## Rule

**Always base PRs on** `main`**.** If work genuinely must be stacked, retarget every child PR to `main`
*before* merging the parent.

Added to `AGENTS.md` "Git Workflow" in [rmems/corinth-canal#138](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-recover-priority-ordered-gguf-synapse-source-selection-69a98e2563b5).

## Detection

After squash-merging any stack, verify each child actually landed:

```bash
git grep <new-symbol> origin/main -- <file>     # expect a hit
git merge-base --is-ancestor <child-sha> origin/main && echo landed || echo LOST
```

Worth running once across the other [#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>) PRs to confirm nothing else was dropped the same way —
[rmems/corinth-canal#127](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormodel-extract-config-validation-helpers-gh118-pr-3-5c94da4d8bd1), [rmems/corinth-canal#128](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-split-checkpointrs-into-private-gguf-modules-gh118-pr-4-230bc5f503d8), and [rmems/corinth-canal#129](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-table-drive-modelfamily-architecture-metadata-gh118-pr-5-e113e27356b5) were spot-checked and are present (`FAMILY_ARCHES` is on `main`), but a
systematic pass would be cheap insurance.

## Why it went unnoticed for three weeks

No test failed. The refactor was behaviour-preserving by design, so its absence is invisible to CI —
the old code kept working. Only a `git grep` for the new symbol reveals it. That is a general
property of pure refactors and argues for the post-merge check above being routine rather than
ad hoc.

## Related

* [#134](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/134>) (the sub-issue that stayed open), [rmems/corinth-canal#126](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-priority-ordered-gguf-synapse-source-selection-gh118-pr-2-94fb0e345288) (the phantom merge), [rmems/corinth-canal#138](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-recover-priority-ordered-gguf-synapse-source-selection-69a98e2563b5) (the recovery), [#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>) (epic)

title: myelin-accelerator: upstream GIF/SAAQ kernels + shim before the #119 swap
description:
## Summary

[#119](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/119>) proposes replacing `src/gpu/` with a dependency on `myelin-accelerator`. **That swap would****
****delete working kernels and break the GPU tick path today.** The influence ran corinth → myelin, and
myelin is a *subset* on exactly the paths corinth depends on.

Direction of travel, from myelin's own history:

```
b681c4d [WIP] Update repository with Corinth Canal CUDA and cust codes (#7)
2557ad2 [WIP] Update repository with Corinth Canal CUDA and cust codes (#6)
```

## Capability gap (myelin-accelerator v0.2.0)

|  | corinth-canal | myelin-accelerator |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `spiking_network.cu` | 812 lines | 483 lines |
| `satsolver.cu`, `vector_similarity.cu` | — | **byte-identical** modulo license header |
| `myelin_shim.cu` / `.h` | present | **absent** |
| `TemporalState` | present | absent |
| Accelerator methods `src/model/temporal.rs` calls | 12 | **1** |
| Codegen | fatbin (sm_120 SASS + compute_120 PTX) | PTX-JIT only |
| `sentry_capture.rs` | present | absent |
| `cuda_fp16.h` in `common.cuh` | present | **removed** — no f16 synapse path |

Kernels present in corinth's `spiking_network.cu` and **missing from myelin's**:

* `project_snapshot_current`
* `gif_step_weighted`
* `gif_step_weighted_f16`
* `saaq_find_best_walker`
* `saaq_reduce_partials_f16`

plus the `GIF_*` constant block (`GIF_LEAK 0.92f`, `GIF_ADAPTATION_SCALE 0.22f`, …).

The name is the punchline: the shim is called `myelin_shim` but exists only in corinth-canal.

## What myelin has that corinth lacks

Genuinely useful, and the reason this shouldn't be a one-way merge: `src/bitpacking.rs` (896 lines,
host binary/ternary pack + reference GEMV/GEMM), `cu/ternary_gemm.cu` with `ternary_gemv`/
`ternary_gemm` wrappers, a real `gpu_stub.rs` CPU path (689 lines) that corinth has no equivalent
of, `_async` variants over a persistent `Stream`, `GpuBuffer::zero_prefix`, and nvtx ranges.

## Required sequence

1. **corinth:** dead-code sweep first — don't upstream unreachable API. (separate issue)
2. **corinth:** invert the `sentry_capture` coupling. This is the concrete form of [#119](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/119>)'s vague
   "remove reference repo coupling" blocker, and [#119](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/119>)'s body does not mention it. `sentry_capture`
   is woven into three files — `ffi.rs:11`, `kernel.rs:23`, `accelerator.rs:18`. **A kernel crate****
****must not depend on** `sentry`**.** Invert it: myelin exposes a launch-failure hook, corinth installs
   the Sentry reporter. This is the single most important API decision in the whole promotion and
   should be settled before any code moves.
3. **myelin:** land the 5 kernels + shim pair + `TemporalState` + the 11 accelerator methods, with a
   numerical parity test against corinth fixtures. Cut 0.3.0.
4. **myelin:** fatbin/SASS build with graceful PTX fallback. This is [#119](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/119>)'s "[build.rs](<http://build.rs>) portability"
   blocker and it must be solved **in myelin**, not corinth. PTX-JIT-only also costs first-launch
   latency on every process start and loses corinth's `cuModuleLoadDataEx` JIT-log capture, which is
   what produces actionable `InvalidPtx` diagnostics.
5. **corinth:** delete `src/gpu/`, add the dep, keep `src/gpu/mod.rs` as a ~10-line
   `pub use myelin_accelerator::...` façade — the same trick PR-4 used for `checkpoint.rs`
   ([rmems/corinth-canal#128](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/refactormoe-split-checkpointrs-into-private-gguf-modules-gh118-pr-4-230bc5f503d8)), which makes the swap a zero-public-API-change PR.

Steps 1-2 are corinth code changes. Steps 3-4 belong in myelin's tracker, mirrored as *blocked-by*
on [#119](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/119>). Step 5 should not be opened until step 3's parity test is green.

## Practical note

myelin-accelerator is **not published** (no `cargo publish` step in any workflow, not on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>))
and its `main` currently has a dirty working tree — 6 modified tracked files including
`src/gpu/accelerator.rs`. Any dependency must **pin a commit SHA**, not a version.

No circular-dependency risk: `grep -ri corinth` in myelin hits only prose in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
and a workflow file. Zero code or Cargo.toml references.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `sentry_capture` inverted to a hook; `src/gpu/` has no corinth-specific dependency
- [ ] Mirror issue filed in `Limen-Neural/myelin-accelerator` for steps 3-4
- [ ] Parity test: myelin's GIF/SAAQ kernels numerically match corinth's on shared fixtures
- [ ] fatbin build with PTX fallback in myelin
- [ ] Only then: [#119](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/119>)'s swap PR

## Related

Blocks [#119](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/119>). Same "upstream first" conclusion as [#143](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-236/decision-do-not-adopt-axon-encoder-or-neuromod-as-dependencies) and [#144](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-237/engram-parser-mmap-reader-k-quant-dequant-required-before-115-is).

title: engram-parser: mmap reader + K-quant dequant required before #115 is viable
description:
## Summary

[#115](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/115>) **as written cannot be implemented.** `engram-parser` v0.2.0 is architecturally incompatible
with what corinth's GGUF layer does, in two independent ways. Blocking [#115](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/115>) on this.

## Blocker 1 — engram-parser reads the whole file into RAM

`engram-parser/src/gguf/mod.rs:38-45`:

```rust
/// The full file contents are read into memory (no mmap; zero-dep by design)
...
let bytes = fs::read(path_ref)...
```

`GgufLayout` owns a `Vec<u8>` of the entire checkpoint.

corinth does the opposite, and has to: `src/moe/gguf/map.rs` mmaps the file, and
`src/moe/gguf/cuda_register.rs` CUDA-host-registers page-aligned tensor ranges so the GPU can DMA
from them. These are multi-GB MoE checkpoints. Reading them into an owned `Vec<u8>` is not a
performance detail — it defeats the entire point of the mapping layer.

`engram-parser`'s `[dependencies]` section is empty. Adding `memmap2` contradicts its stated
zero-dep design, so this is a real fork in the road, not an oversight to patch.

## Blocker 2 — only F16 dequantization

```
$ grep -rn "pub fn dequantize" engram-parser/src/
src/gguf/tensor.rs:504:    pub fn dequantize_f16(...)
```

corinth needs Q8_0, Q5_K, Q6_K, and IQ3_M (`src/moe/gguf/map.rs`), which is the entire point of the
synapse-source selection ladder.

## Why the header-only compromise isn't worth it

Adopting engram-parser for just header/KV/tensor-directory parsing would replace
`src/moe/gguf/metadata.rs` — about 335 lines — with a new dependency **that reads the entire****
****checkpoint into RAM in order to parse a header**. Net negative.

## Recommendation

Re-scope [#115](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/115>) to the same shape as [#119](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/119>): **upstream first, adopt second.**

* Land corinth's mmap-backed reader and K-quant dequant in engram-parser behind an optional `mmap`
  feature, with the zero-dep path preserved as the default.
* Revisit the corinth-side dependency only after that ships and passes a parity test on real
  checkpoints.

If the answer is "engram-parser is zero-dep by design and will never take `memmap2`", then [#115](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/115>)
should be **closed as won't-do**, and sharing happens the [#116](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/116>) way: one-way copy, no dependency.
That is a legitimate outcome — it just needs deciding rather than sitting open.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Decide: upstream into engram-parser, or close [#115](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/115>) won't-do and copy per [#116](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/116>)
- [ ] If upstreaming: issue filed in `Limen-Neural/engram-parser` for the `mmap` feature + K-quants
- [ ] [#115](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/115>) re-scoped or closed with the rationale recorded
- [ ] `docs/MODULE_STATUS.md` GGUF row updated to reflect the outcome

## Related

Blocks [#115](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/115>). Same "upstream first" conclusion as [#119](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/119>) and [#143](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-236/decision-do-not-adopt-axon-encoder-or-neuromod-as-dependencies).

title: decision: do not adopt axon-encoder or neuromod as dependencies (upstream first)
description:
## Decision

**Do not add** `Limen-Neural/axon-encoder` **or** `Limen-Neural/neuromod` **as dependencies of****
****corinth-canal.** Recorded so this stops being re-litigated.

This contradicts the 2026-07-20 "Limen-Neural shave-map" analysis (ogham `3407b677`, chroma
`limen-neural-shave-map-20260720`), which proposed `src/telemetry.rs -> axon-encoder` and
`src/funnel.rs -> neuromod`. That memo was written from crate descriptions. Direct source
comparison does not support it.

## Evidence

### axon-encoder v0.4.0 vs `src/telemetry.rs` — divergent, not a superset

`TelemetryEncoder::encode` and axon-encoder's closest analogues disagree on every axis that
matters:

| Semantic | corinth `TelemetryEncoder` | `DerivativeEncoder` | `DeltaEncoder` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Per-channel thresholds | yes `[f32; 4]` | yes `Vec<f32>` | no, one scalar |
| Comparison | `>= t` / `<= -t` | `> t` / `< -t` | `abs(d) > t` |
| Baseline update | **only on crossing** | every step | only on spike |
| First sample | **seeds baseline, emits** `[0;4]` | baseline starts `0.0` → cold-start spike | same cold-start |
| Output | dense `[i8; 4]` | sparse `Vec<SpikeEvent>` | sparse `Vec<SpikeEvent>` |

`subthreshold_change_emits_zero_and_preserves_baseline` fails against `DerivativeEncoder`.
Net deletion after writing a compatibility shim: **\~20 lines**.

### axon-encoder vs `src/funnel.rs` and `src/projector.rs` — zero overlap

* `SignedSplitBankBridge` is a sign→bank fan-out topology, not an encoder. axon-encoder's README
  explicitly disclaims layers, topologies, and SNN simulation.
* `Projector` runs the **opposite direction**: spikes → dense embedding. axon-encoder's only
  embedding-shaped API (`EmbeddingRateEncoder::forward`) goes embeddings → spikes, and
  `EncodedOutput.embeddings` is a passthrough field no encoder ever populates.

### neuromod v0.5.0 vs `src/funnel.rs` — subset, and a regression

`neuromod::GifNeuron`'s dynamics are bit-identical to `SparseGifHiddenLayer`'s core, same operation
order, same constants (`leak 0.92`, `drive_scale 0.75`, `threshold 0.65`, `adaptation_scale 0.22`,
`adaptation_decay 0.94`, `coupling 0.05`, `reset_ratio 0.35`). neuromod's own docs say so:

> `neuromod/src/gif.rs:29` — *"The default parameters mirror the production configuration extracted**
**from the author's* `corinth-canal` *spike-to-embedding pipeline (see* `SparseGifHiddenLayer`*)."*

But it ships a **single neuron**, not a layer. Missing: the deterministic sparse-topology generator,
the batched `run()` over a spike train, and the SoA storage. `GifNeuron` carries 12 fields including
a dense `Vec<f32>` of weights — 2048 of those is a memory and cache-locality regression against
corinth's two flat arrays. `SpikingNetwork` can't substitute either; it wires LIF + Izhikevich only,
never GIF.

Net: **\~25-30 lines, likely net-negative.**

### neuromod vs `src/latent.rs` and `src/moe/routing.rs` — zero overlap

No calibrator, no CSV exporter, no SAAQ concept. `routing.rs` is GGUF/safetensors tensor-orientation
arithmetic and is entirely `pub(super)` — not even public API.

## Disqualifier

`NeuroModulators` is defined in **both** crates with incompatible fields:

* `neuromod`: `{ dopamine, serotonin, acetylcholine, norepinephrine }`
* `axon-encoder`: `{ dopamine, cortisol, acetylcholine, tempo }`

neuromod 0.5.0's CHANGELOG records removing `cortisol`/`tempo` as a breaking change. Depending on
both puts two same-named, non-convertible types in scope. The org has not reconciled this.

`PoissonEncoder` is also duplicated across the two (`neuromod/src/lif.rs:5`,
`axon-encoder/src/poisson.rs:31`).

## The general principle

**The influence gradient runs corinth → siblings, not the reverse.** Every "adopt now" path reduces
to deleting working code and re-adding it. Where sharing is worthwhile, upstream first and adopt
second — the same conclusion reached separately for engram-parser and myelin-accelerator.

## Not covered by this decision

This says nothing about `synaptic-mesh`, `hybrid-fusion`, or `cortex-tensor`, which were not
compared. If someone wants those evaluated, open a separate issue.

## Related

* [#115](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/115>) (engram-parser), [#116](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/116>) (safetensors extraction), [#119](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/119>) (myelin-accelerator)
* `docs/PROMOTION_RULES.md`, `docs/MODULE_STATUS.md`

title: testing: examples/support/mod.rs unit tests never execute
description:
## Summary

`examples/support/mod.rs` has a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block with ~10 tests. **None of them run,****
****in any configuration.** They are compiled-but-never-executed dead weight, and they give false
confidence that the helpers they cover are guarded.

Discovered while adding a regression test for [#140](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-234/examples-routing-modedense-sim-and-stub-uniform-are-silently-dropped) — the new test reported `0 passed; ... filtered out` no matter how it was invoked.

## Why

Two things stack:

1. `examples/support/` is reachable only via `mod support;`, declared by exactly five files —
   `csv_replay.rs`, `gpu_smoke_test.rs`, `saaq_latent_calibration.rs`, `synapse_diagnostic.rs`,
   `telemetry_bridge.rs`. All five declare `required-features = ["cuda"]`, so under
   `--no-default-features` the module is not compiled at all.
2. Even with `cuda` on, `cargo test` does not run the test harness of an **example** target.

Confirmed — the only targets that produce results:

```
$ cargo test --no-default-features --locked 2>&1 | grep -E "Running|Doc-tests"
     Running unittests src/lib.rs
     Running tests/examples_support_lineup.rs
     Running tests/gpu_sentry_telemetry.rs
   Doc-tests corinth_canal
```

The four non-cuda examples (`validate_matrix`, `validate_local_saaq`, `summarize_local_saaq`,
`safetensors_manifest`) do **not** declare `mod support`, so they don't rescue it either.

## Affected tests

The ~10 tests in `examples/support/mod.rs`, covering `load_csv_telemetry_rows`,
`resolve_prompt_embedding_provider`, `parse_family_slug`, and others.

## Precedent for the fix

`tests/examples_support_lineup.rs` already solves this for a sibling file:

```rust
#[path = "../examples/support/lineup.rs"]
mod lineup;
```

That pulls `lineup.rs` into a real integration-test target, and its 7 tests do run.

## Options

1. `#[path]`**-include the testable helpers** the way `lineup.rs` is included. Complication:
   `mod.rs` imports `corinth_canal::model::ModelConfig` and `projector::ProjectionMode` under
   `#[cfg(feature = "cuda")]`, so a naive include won't compile under `--no-default-features`
   without splitting the cuda-gated parts out first.
2. **Move pure helpers into the library** where they are testable in the `--lib` target that
   hosted CI actually runs. This is what [#140](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-234/examples-routing-modedense-sim-and-stub-uniform-are-silently-dropped)'s fix did for the routing-mode table
   (`RoutingMode::from_alias` in `src/types.rs`).
3. **Split** `examples/support/mod.rs` (940 lines) into `telemetry_csv.rs` / `embedding.rs` /
   `discovery.rs` / `env.rs`, then `#[path]`-include the CPU-safe ones. Overlaps the [#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>) work.

Option 2 is the cheapest per-helper and puts the guard in the job that runs on every PR; option 3
is the durable fix.

## Related

* [#140](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-234/examples-routing-modedense-sim-and-stub-uniform-are-silently-dropped) — the bug whose regression test surfaced this
* [#118](<https://github.com/rmems/corinth-canal/issues/118>) — `examples/support/mod.rs` is a listed complexity hotspot

title: examples: ROUTING_MODE=dense_sim and stub_uniform are silently dropped
description:
## Summary

`ROUTING_MODE` and lineup-config `routing_mode` entries had **two separate hand-rolled spelling****
****tables**, and they drifted. The env path silently ignored valid values.

## The two paths

`examples/support/mod.rs`:

```rust
// :137 — used for lineup-config `routing_mode = "..."` entries
pub fn parse_routing_mode(value: &str) -> Option<RoutingMode> {
    match value.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
        "dense" | "dense_sim"     => Some(RoutingMode::DenseSim),
        "stub"  | "stub_uniform"  => Some(RoutingMode::StubUniform),
        "spiking" | "spiking_sim" => Some(RoutingMode::SpikingSim),
        _ => None,
    }
}

// :656 — used for the ROUTING_MODE env var
pub fn routing_mode_override_from_env() -> Option<RoutingMode> {
    let raw = std::env::var("ROUTING_MODE").ok()?;
    match raw.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {      // note: no .trim()
        "dense"   => Some(RoutingMode::DenseSim),  // no "dense_sim"
        "stub"    => Some(RoutingMode::StubUniform), // no "stub_uniform"
        "spiking" | "spiking_sim" => Some(RoutingMode::SpikingSim),
        _ => None,
    }
}
```

`parse_routing_mode`'s doc comment claimed *"Same precedence rules as*
`routing_mode_override_from_env`*"*. It was not.

## Impact

`ROUTING_MODE=dense_sim` returns `None`, and callers treat `None` as "keep the configured
default" — so the run proceeds in `SpikingSim` (the `RoutingMode` default) while the operator
believes they selected dense. Same for `stub_uniform`. `ROUTING_MODE=" dense"` also fails, since
the env path never trimmed.

**Data-integrity angle:** any archived run whose `run_manifest.json` recorded a routing mode set
via the env var is suspect — it may have run in a different mode than it reports.

## Repro

```bash
ROUTING_MODE=dense_sim just saaq   # runs SpikingSim, reports the config default
ROUTING_MODE=dense     just saaq   # runs DenseSim
```

## Fix

Give the table a single owner. `RoutingMode::from_alias` in `src/types.rs`, next to the enum it
parses; both example entry points delegate to it.

## Note on test placement

The regression test is in `src/types.rs`, not next to the changed code, because
`examples/support/mod.rs`**'s** `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` **never executes** — see the companion issue.

title: [agoge-forger] merge_adapter passes removed save_pretrained kwarg on transformers 5
description:
## Context

Spun out of [#63](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-209/agoge-forger-gh63-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-14-sftconfig) / PR [rmems/agoge-forger#67](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/fixtrain-migrate-sfttrainer-to-trl-1x-sftconfig-regression-test-d33c98f1819b) (TRL 1.x migration), where this was found but deliberately left out of scope.

`export/merge_adapter.py:49-51` calls:

```python
merged_model.save_pretrained(
    str(safe_out_dir), safe_serialization=save_safetensors, max_shard_size=max_shard_size
)
```

After `merge_and_unload()`, `merged_model` is a plain `PreTrainedModel`, not a `PeftModel`. In transformers 5 the signature is:

```
save_directory, is_main_process, state_dict, push_to_hub, max_shard_size,
variant, token, save_peft_format, save_original_format, kwargs
```

`safe_serialization` is gone. It is absorbed by `**kwargs` and **silently ignored** rather than raising.

## Impact

Low / cosmetic today. Transformers 5 always writes safetensors, so the resulting artifact is what the caller wanted anyway, and the `assert_no_unsafe_weight_bins` gate downstream still holds. The problem is that the argument reads as if it controls something it no longer controls — and a future caller passing `save_safetensors=False` with `allow_unsafe=True` would get safetensors regardless, with no error.

Note the distinction: `PeftModel.save_pretrained` (peft 0.19.1) **does** still accept `safe_serialization`, so the adapter-save path in `train/trainer.py` is correct as written. Only the merged-model path is affected.

## Suggested fix

Drop `safe_serialization=` from the merged-model `save_pretrained` call and leave a comment explaining that transformers 5 made safetensors unconditional; keep the `save_safetensors` parameter on `merge_adapter` for the PEFT path and the assertion gate.

Worth a small unit test in the same spirit as `tests/test_trainer_trl_api.py`: assert the kwargs `merge_adapter` passes are accepted by the installed `PreTrainedModel.save_pretrained` signature.

title: card: support language_by_pr override in normalize.language_for
description:
## Problem

`language_for` (`scripts/lib/normalize.py:~772`) returns `card["language"]` unconditionally:

```python
def language_for(card, raw):
    if card.get("language"):
        return str(card["language"])
    # ...extension sniffing only reached when the card omits language
```

There is a per-PR escape hatch for domain (`domain_by_pr`, used by `datasets/cards/limen-axon-encoder-v0.json`) but none for language. A mixed-language repo must therefore either mislabel records or drop `language` from the card entirely, which throws away the curated value for every other PR.

## Concrete case

[rmems/grok-ozempic#42](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-export-grok-1-embedding-pickle-npy-37-rm-189-30ca8c22a3ad) is Python (`scripts/export_grok1_embedding_npy.py`, +620, plus a test file) in a repo whose card declares `"language": "Rust"`. Extracting it today labels a Python trajectory as Rust.

The same applies to the Limen-Neural org, which is Rust + Julia + SystemVerilog across repos and will hit this on any repo with tooling scripts.

## Proposal

Mirror `domain_for`: check `card["language_by_pr"]` (string or int keys, as `domain_by_pr` already tolerates) before falling back to `card["language"]`, then to extension sniffing.

## Acceptance

* `language_by_pr: {"42": "Python"}` overrides the card default for that PR only.
* Existing cards without the field behave identically.
* Test alongside the `domain_by_pr` coverage in `tests/test_collect_and_normalize.py`.

Blocks extraction of grok-ozempic#42 (together with the review-signal dedupe issue). Found while working [#11](<https://github.com/rmems/operation-prometheus/issues/11>) / [rmems/operation-prometheus#17](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-grok-ozempic-v0-trajectories-revised-7-pr-shortlist-8917529e7019).

title: normalize: dedupe review_signals and deprioritize 'Addressed in <sha>' acks
description:
## Problem

`extract_review_signals` (`scripts/lib/normalize.py`) can fill all 8 slots with byte-identical text, producing a record with no usable review signal.

Concrete case — [rmems/grok-ozempic#42](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-export-grok-1-embedding-pickle-npy-37-rm-189-30ca8c22a3ad) (`export Grok-1 embedding pickle → .npy`): 51 signals survive the bot filter, but the emitted record is **8 copies of one body**:

> `Addressed in 5ecbe0855124d24533a1cc365274ea2dcb9400c1: portable ~/.models paths in docs/help (no hard-coded username), dtype KeyError guard, NPY header uses space-pad then trailing newline …`

The maintainer posted the same ack across every thread. [rmems/grok-ozempic#43](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-quantize-goz1-cli-for-goz1-run-quantization-38-rm-193-946bde990911) has a milder version (7 unique of 8).

## Cause

Two gaps:

1. **No dedupe.** Nothing compares signal bodies; identical text posted to N threads yields N signals.
2. `_BARE_FIXED_IN_REPLY` **is too narrow** (`normalize.py:~279`). It matches only *bare* `Fixed in <sha>.` / `**Addressed in `abc1234`**`. An ack with trailing content — `Addressed in <sha>: <what changed>` — passes straight through.

Ack-shaped replies are not worthless (they carry the fix rationale), but they are the *answer*, not the *problem statement*. When they crowd out the reviewer comments that prompted them, the trajectory loses its review→patch shape.

## Proposal

* Dedupe on a normalized body key (collapse whitespace, strip the leading `Addressed in <sha>:` / `Fixed in commit <sha>:` prefix) before appending.
* Rank problem statements ahead of acks when the cap forces a choice, so a PR with 6 Codex findings and 20 acks emits the findings.
* Keep at least one ack when it carries rationale — the goal is deduplication, not suppression.

## Acceptance

* [rmems/grok-ozempic#42](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-export-grok-1-embedding-pickle-npy-37-rm-189-30ca8c22a3ad) emits ≥5 unique bodies.
* Existing `corinth-canal-v0` / `limen-axon-encoder-v0` records do not regress (all currently emit 8 unique).
* Covered by a test in `tests/test_collect_and_normalize.py`.

description:

**Not** PR [#52](<https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/pull/52>) / issue [#51](<https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/issues/51>) (embedding τ research only).

Prefer [RM-222](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-222/grok-ozempic-gh53-consume-xai-dissect-run3-planning-surface-pilot) for Linear status.

## Context

xai-dissect **run3** re-cartography (Aug 2026) vs May **run2** shows:

| Finding | Detail |
| -- | -- |
| Structure + stats | **Bit-stable** — 770 tensors, coverage checksum `fnv1a64:de5a1c978121c62c`, same RMS/var aggregates |
| Product surface | run3 adds conversion / quant-plan / pilot-selection / route-preservation + SAAQ readiness schema v2 |

**Preferred handoff path:**

```text
~/rmems/xai-dissect/out/LATEST_CORRECT_GROK1_RUN/manifests/xai-grok-1-ckpt-0/
```

(resolves to `out/grok1_run3_20260802T023050Z`)

Key artifacts:

* `conversion-manifest.json`
* `quant-plan.json` / `.md`
* `pilot-selection-plan.json` / `.md`
* `route-preservation-report.json` / `.md`

## Goal
