title: [Spikenaut-SNN] Integrate Limen-Neural crates as dependencies
description:
## Goal

Gradually integrate 14 Limen-Neural Rust crates as dependencies into Spikenaut-SNN, repo-by-repo as each stabilizes.

## Current State

* Spikenaut-SNN has **ZERO code dependencies** on any Limen-Neural crate
* 14 Rust crates, each standalone with its own Cargo.toml (no workspace)
* Internal deps use a mix of [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) and git-pinned revisions
* 11 of 14 crates are leaves (no internal deps) — clean DAG, no cycles

## 3-Phase Approach

### Phase 1 (now, 0–3 crates)

Use `path` + `version` hybrids for local dev, `git rev` for unstable crates:

```toml
[dependencies]
neuromod = { path = "../../Limen-Neural/neuromod", version = "0.5" }
axon-encoder = { git = "https://github.com/Limen-Neural/axon-encoder", rev = "abc123" }
```

### Phase 2 (3–5 crates)

Introduce Cargo workspace with `[workspace.dependencies]`

### Phase 3 (5+ crates)

Use `[patch.crates-io]` pattern (tokio-style)

## Integration Priority

| Priority | Crate | Why |
| -- | -- | -- |
| HIGH | `neuromod` | Core SNN engine — LIF, STDP, learning rules |
| HIGH | `axon-encoder` | Input quality — fixes telemetry encoding bugs |
| HIGH | `silicon-bridge` | Q8.8 export fidelity — fixes weight artifacts |
| MEDIUM | `limbic-critic` | Reward signal correctness |
| MEDIUM | `synaptic-mesh` | Enables scaling beyond 16 neurons |
| MEDIUM | `plasticity-lab` | Reproducible training loops |

## Version Pinning Strategy

* Pre-adoption: `git rev` (full SHA)
* Adopted: Caret range (`"0.5"`)
* Tightly-coupled pairs: Exact pin (`"=0.5.0"`, rare)

## Key Findings (43 sources, deep-research)

* Embassy (closest match, no_std, 40+ crates) deliberately avoids a workspace
* `GITHUB_TOKEN` can't trigger cross-repo workflows — need GitHub App token
* Use `#[non_exhaustive]` on all shared types from day one
* Semver trick for managing 0.x breaking transitions
* Batch releases: single maintainer can prepare all affected crates in one session

## Shared Types

Create `spikenaut-types` crate with domain primitives:

* `SpikeEvent` struct (#[non_exhaustive])
* `NeuronParams` struct (#[non_exhaustive])
* `TelemetryFormat` enum (#[non_exhaustive])
* `SnnError` enum (#[non_exhaustive])

## Related Issues

* RM-43: Monotonic weight artifact (root cause identified)
* RM-44: Add inhibitory connections (data pipeline steps added)
* RM-45: Export pipeline validation (confirmed NOT broken)
* LIM-772-778: NIR integration pipeline

## Artifacts

* `REPORT.md` — Full deep-research report (373 lines, 43 sources)
* `REVIEW.md` — Citation audit

---

title: [Spikenaut-SNN] Validate Q8.8 export pipeline: GPU float to FPGA roundtrip fidelity
description:
## Problem

The training pipeline has multiple stages where weight precision can be lost:

1. GPU training loop produces float32 weights
2. Export function converts float to Q8.8 hex (4-digit hex per value)
3. FPGA loads via $readmemh into [WeightRam.sv](<http://WeightRam.sv>)
4. FPGA performs Q8.8 arithmetic in hardware

The monotonic weight artifact (see #2) could originate at step 2 if the export function has a rounding bias.

## Investigation Results (2026-07-12)

**Export pipeline is confirmed NOT broken.** The .mem files faithfully encode the float weights with no rounding-induced pattern.

### Evidence

1. **Cross-validation**: All 256 weights in `weights/v2/merged/parameters_weights.mem` match exactly with `weights/v2/merged/snn_model.json` floats
2. **Pattern origin**: The monotonic pattern exists natively in the float weights — it is NOT a Q8.8 quantization artifact
3. **Root cause**: The pattern is caused by degenerate training convergence (8 uniform samples + no inhibitory connections), not by export bugs

### Conclusion

This issue can remain open for future validation but the export pipeline is confirmed working correctly. The root cause of the monotonic weights is in the training data and architecture (see RM-43).

title: [worktrees-hives] GH#18 — Packaging: install script / symlink docs
description:
## Problem

Operators need a **one-command or short copy-paste install** that places **worktrees-hives** into agent skill directories. Today the repo is a scaffold (README + LICENSE); without packaging docs, each platform (`Cline`, shared `~/.agents/skills`, Claude, Cursor, and others) gets a different broken path and the skill never loads.

We already have a working multi-root pattern on this machine for `pr-babysit` (canonical dir + **symlinks** into other skill roots). **worktrees-hives** should document the same approach, optionally with a small install script.

## Goals

* Document **clone + symlink** install for at least one primary skill root.
* Provide an **optional install script** that creates/updates symlinks safely.
* Cover **cross-agent roots** used in this environment: shared agents, Cline, and Claude-compatible roots.
* Keep a single source tree (no forked copies per agent).

## Non-goals

* Publishing to a public skills marketplace as a hard requirement (optional later via `npx skills` / [skills.sh](<http://skills.sh>)).
* Auto-updating every agent on the machine without user consent.
* Bundling as a marketplace plugin in v1 (symlink/user skills first).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Documented install** in README (and/or `docs/install.md`) covering:
  - Clone location recommendation
  - Symlink (or copy) into a skill root so `<root>/worktrees-hives/SKILL.md` resolves
  - How to verify discovery (`/skills`, agent restart, list dir)
- [ ] Works for **at least one** agent skill root path end-to-end (recommended primary: `~/.agents/skills/worktrees-hives` **or** `~/.grok/skills/worktrees-hives` given Grok-first epic).
- [ ] **Optional install script** (e.g. `scripts/install-skill.sh`) that:
  - Is idempotent
  - Creates parent dirs if needed
  - Symlinks the skill directory (not a bare file) into selected roots
  - Refuses to clobber a non-symlink conflicting path without `--force`
  - Prints next steps (restart agent / `/skills worktrees-hives`)
- [ ] Docs list **cross-agent paths** (see design table) so humans can extend install without reverse-engineering.
- [ ] Uninstall notes: remove symlink(s); clone dir optional keep.
- [ ] Does not require Graphite; plain git + `gh` only.

## Design

### Canonical layout after #2

```text
worktrees-hives/                 # git clone
  SKILL.md                       # required entrypoint
  README.md
  scripts/
    install-skill.sh             # optional
  docs/                          # optional
  LICENSE
```

Skill directory name must match frontmatter `name` when agents require that convention: `worktrees-hives`.

### Cross-agent skill roots

| Root | Path | Priority for this skill |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Shared agents / skills CLI | `~/.agents/skills/worktrees-hives` | **Primary shared** — good hub for multi-agent |
| Cline | `~/.cline/skills/worktrees-hives` | High (existing `pr-babysit` pattern) |
| Grok user | `~/.grok/skills/worktrees-hives` | High (Grok Build first) |
| Grok project | `<repo>/.grok/skills/worktrees-hives` | Optional per-repo |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/worktrees-hives` | Medium (also scanned by Grok) |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/skills/worktrees-hives` | Medium if used |
| Codex / others | `~/.codex/skills/…`, OpenCode, Gemini, Kilo, … | Document as optional targets |

**Recommended topology:**

1. Clone once, e.g. `~/src/worktrees-hives` or keep under `~/rmems/worktrees-hives`.
2. Symlink **from** clone **into** `~/.agents/skills/worktrees-hives`.
3. Optionally fan-out more symlinks:

```bash
# Example (illustrative — final script owns flags)
ln -sfn "$CLONE" "$HOME/.agents/skills/worktrees-hives"
ln -sfn "$CLONE" "$HOME/.cline/skills/worktrees-hives"
ln -sfn "$CLONE" "$HOME/.grok/skills/worktrees-hives"
ln -sfn "$CLONE" "$HOME/.claude/skills/worktrees-hives"
```

Observed precedent: `~/.agents/skills/pr-babysit` → `~/.cline/skills/pr-babysit` (and reverse fan-out across opencode/kilo/gemini/etc.). Prefer **one real directory** + many symlinks.

### Manual install (docs minimum)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rmems/worktrees-hives.git ~/rmems/worktrees-hives
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills ~/.grok/skills ~/.cline/skills
ln -sfn ~/rmems/worktrees-hives ~/.agents/skills/worktrees-hives
ln -sfn ~/rmems/worktrees-hives ~/.grok/skills/worktrees-hives
# verify
test -f ~/.agents/skills/worktrees-hives/SKILL.md && echo OK
```

### Optional `scripts/install-skill.sh` behavior

```text
Usage: install-skill.sh [--root agents|grok|cline|claude|all] [--force] [--clone-dir PATH]

Default: --root agents (or all if we prefer multi-root for this project)
- Resolve CLONE_DIR = repo root containing this script
- For each selected root: mkdir -p; if target exists and is not symlink to CLONE, error unless --force
- ln -sfn CLONE_DIR TARGET
- Print verification + restart instructions
```

Support `WORKTREES_HIVES_CLONE` override for non-standard locations.

### Optional ecosystem install

Document as secondary:

```bash
# If/when published to skills registry
npx skills add rmems/worktrees-hives
```

Do not block acceptance on registry publication. Local symlink is enough.

### Verification matrix (docs)

| Check | Command / action |
| -- | -- |
| File present | `test -f ~/.agents/skills/worktrees-hives/SKILL.md` |
| Symlink healthy | `readlink -f …` points at clone |
| Grok | `/skills worktrees-hives` or list skills |
| Cline | skill picker / skills list |
| Claude | restart session; confirm skill listed |

### Relationship to #17

#18 makes install **repeatable**; #17 **runs** smoke tests on a second platform using that install. Ship docs/script before or with #17.

## Dependencies

| Dep | Why |
| -- | -- |
| #2 SKILL.md | Install target must exist |
| #3 README expand | Primary home for install docs |
| Soft: #17 | Consumer of install paths |

Epic milestone **D2**.

## Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
| -- | -- |
| Symlink to nested `worktrees-hives/worktrees-hives` clone path | Script uses `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` / script dir carefully; docs show real path |
| Clobbering existing skill name | Refuse non-symlink targets without `--force` |
| Agent ignores `~/.agents/skills` | Always document Grok/Cline-specific roots; offer `--root all` |
| Relative symlinks break when clone moves | Prefer absolute `ln -sfn` targets |
| Windows/WSL path issues | Document Linux/macOS first; WSL note optional |
| Skills CLI vs manual drift | Keep manual symlink as source of truth in v1 |

## Implementation plan

1. Land #2 (`SKILL.md`) if not already present.
2. Write README **Install** section: manual clone + symlink for `~/.agents/skills` and `~/.grok/skills`; table of other roots.
3. Add `scripts/install-skill.sh` with `--root` / `--force` / idempotent behavior.
4. Dry-run install on this machine into a temp or real root; confirm `SKILL.md` resolves.
5. Cross-link #17 smoke checklist to install section.
6. Optional: note `npx skills` future path.

## Test / verification plan

* Run install script twice (idempotent).
* Create dummy conflict file; ensure script errors without `--force`.
* After install, agent lists skill (at least Grok Build).
* `readlink` shows single clone for multi-root symlinks.

## References

* Epic #1 (milestone **D** — D2)
* #2 SKILL.md, #3 README, #17 second-platform validation
* Local precedents: `~/.agents/skills/*`, `~/.cline/skills/pr-babysit`, `~/.grok/skills/*`
* Grok discovery: `./.grok/skills` → repo `.grok/skills` → `~/.grok/skills` → `~/.claude/skills` (+ config `[skills].paths`)
* Skills CLI: `npx skills add|find|check|update` ([skills.sh](<http://skills.sh>) ecosystem)

## Hybrid layer

**Primary implementation layer:** hybrid packaging; see #41 H2

This issue remains valid under the **Python/Rust hybrid** architecture (epic #21). Rust owns worktrees, state, process supervision, and hard safety; Python owns orchestration/policy; agent skills document how Grok drives both.

title: [worktrees-hives] GH#17 — Validate skill on second agent platform
description:
## Problem

**worktrees-hives** is intended to be platform-neutral. Skill packages that only work in one agent’s tool surface become tribal knowledge and silently break safety rules when ported. This issue tracks deliberate **second-platform validation** so install paths, subagent spawning, `gh`/git workflows, and hard rules (never merge, worktree isolation, fix cap) remain correct across platforms.

## Goals

* Prove the skill is **loadable and operable** on at least one second agent platform.
* Publish a **smoke checklist** operators can re-run after skill changes.
* Record **platform-specific tool differences** (subagents, shell, MCP, skill discovery).
* Confirm **no regression** on never-merge / worktree isolation / force-with-lease / fix-cap rules.

## Non-goals

* Full feature parity automation tests on every agent forever.
* Rewriting the skill into platform-specific forks.
* Validating Graphite or non-allowlisted owners.

## Target platforms

| Priority | Platform | Skill root (typical) | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| First validated platform | Current primary platform | documented in repo | baseline |
| Second (this issue) | Pick one of Claude Code, Cursor, or Cline | see table below | document which was chosen |
| Stretch | OpenCode, Gemini, Codex, Kilo | various | optional note only |

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Written **smoke checklist** for a named second platform checked into skill docs.
- [ ] Checklist covers skill discovery, discovery command, worktree isolation, PR inspect/open without merge, thread/CI read, and final status language.
- [ ] **Platform-specific tool differences** documented.
- [ ] Explicit pass/fail on safety invariants.
- [ ] One real or sandboxed run log attached.
- [ ] Known limitations listed explicitly.

## Design

### Smoke checklist template

```markdown
## Platform smoke: <Platform> (<date>)

### Environment
- Agent version:
- Skill path:
- `gh auth status`: ok?
- Allowed owners under test:

### Steps
| # | Step | Expected | Result |
|---|------|----------|--------|
| 1 | Invoke skill | Skill body loaded | |
| 2 | discover | Only allowlisted owners | |
| 3 | add / claim issue (or dry-run) | Branch + worktree path shown | |
| 4 | Confirm cwd for edits | Worktree path, not main clone | |
| 5 | PR open or babysit check | No merge commands | |
| 6 | Threads + CI read | Taxonomy-aware | |
| 7 | Status report | healthy vs blocked; no merge claim | |
```

## Dependencies

| Dep | Why |
| -- | -- |
| #2 SKILL.md layout | Something loadable to validate |
| #3 README install notes | Operators know how to install on platform |
| #13 Safety guardrails | Invariants under test |
| #18 Packaging / symlink docs | Repeatable install into second platform roots |

## Hybrid layer

**Primary implementation layer:** platform/docs

This issue remains valid under the **Python/Rust hybrid** architecture (epic #21). Rust owns worktrees, state, process supervision, and hard safety; Python owns orchestration/policy; agent skills document how agents drive both.

title: [worktrees-hives] GH#16 — Final status report table
description:
## Problem

Hive cycles leave humans without a single, trustworthy end-of-cycle snapshot. Status is scattered across subagent logs, watchlist state, `gh pr view` output, and chat. Operators need a **human-readable final report** that:

* Summarizes every job the orchestrator touched this cycle
* Separates **healthy / merge-ready** items from **blocked on external gates**
* **Never claims a merge occurred** (hard safety rule: worktrees-hives never merges)

Without a standard table, agents overclaim progress, omit residual blockers, or invent merge outcomes.

## Goals

* Emit a **final status report table** at the end of every orchestrator cycle (`check` / `check-all` / full hive run).
* Make residual work and external gates obvious to a human in under 30 seconds.
* Align report columns with babysit success criteria and CI taxonomy (#9, #10).
* Keep language honest: **merge-ready ≠ merged**.

## Non-goals

* Auto-merge, queue-for-merge, or any merge API/UI action.
* Replacing full PR pages or CI dashboards.
* Historical analytics beyond the current cycle (watchlist can hold timestamps; report is point-in-time).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Report includes a **markdown table** with at least these columns:

  | Column | Meaning |
  | -- | -- |
  | wner/repo` | g. `Limen-Neural/hybrid-fusion` |
  | ssue/PR #` | sue and/or PR number (both when issue→PR) |
  | hreads left` | resolved review threads (0 = clean) |
  | I class` | llup using taxonomy A/B/C (+ pass/fail/pending) |
  | ergeable` | tHub `mergeable` / `mergeStateStatus` (or N/A for issue-only) |
  | esidual blockers` | ort human-readable blockers (or `none`) |
- [ ] Clear visual or textual split of **healthy** vs **blocked on external gates** (e.g. section headers, status emoji, or `status` column with `healthy` / `blocked-external` / `in-progress` / `failed-agent`).
- [ ] Report **never** states that a merge happened, was performed, or is queued by the skill.
- [ ] “Healthy” requires: CI green (or only non-blocking pending third-party), 0 unresolved threads, `mergeable=MERGEABLE` + clean merge state when applicable, no residual fix-cap exhaustion.
- [ ] External-gate examples called out when present: Codacy human gate (Class B), third-party review bots (Class C), `CHANGES_REQUESTED` from humans, missing reviews, branch protection waiting on approvals.
- [ ] Report is written to **stdout / chat** and optionally mirrored into cycle logs; document location if persisted.
- [ ] Multi-repo / multi-owner cycles produce **one consolidated table** (not one silent log per worker).

## Design

### When produced

* After orchestrator join (#7): all workers finished, timed out, or marked residual (#15).
* Also after single-repo `check` cycles that babysit existing PRs.

### Row identity

* One row per watched job (issue and/or PR). If an issue opened a PR this cycle, prefer a single row with both numbers (e.g. `I#42 → PR#17`).
* Source of truth order: live `gh`/`GraphQL` → watchlist state (#12) → worker result payload.

### Suggested status vocabulary

| Status | Use when |
| -- | -- |
| `healthy` | Merge-ready per success criteria; human may merge |
| `blocked-external` | Waiting on human review, branch protection, Codacy gate, or Class C bots |
| `in-progress` | Agent still has fix budget / actionable threads or Class A CI |
| `failed-agent` | Fix cap hit, timeout, worktree error, or unrecoverable agent failure |
| `issue-only` | Issue claimed/worked but PR not opened yet (or intentionally deferred) |

### CI class cell

Reuse #10 taxonomy in compact form, e.g.:

* `A:pass B:n/a C:pending`
* `A:fail(clippy) B:gate C:idle`

Do not spam re-trigger commits for Class C in order to “improve” the report.

### Example table (illustrative)

```markdown
## Final status report (cycle 2026-07-09T21:00Z)

| owner/repo | issue/PR # | threads left | CI class | mergeable | residual blockers | status |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Limen-Neural/hybrid-fusion | I#10 → PR#17 | 0 | A:pass B:n/a C:idle | MERGEABLE/CLEAN | none | healthy |
| rmems/worktrees-hives | PR#3 | 2 | A:fail(test) | CONFLICTING | review threads; rebase needed | in-progress |
| Limen-Neural/silicon-hdl | PR#9 | 0 | A:pass B:gate | MERGEABLE/BLOCKED | Codacy quality gate (human) | blocked-external |

**Healthy:** 1 · **Blocked external:** 1 · **In progress:** 1  
**Note:** No merges performed by worktrees-hives. Humans merge when ready.
```

### Copy rules

* Prefer “ready for human merge” over “done” or “shipped”.
* Prefer “blocked on …” over “failed” when the agent did its job and a human/gate remains.
* Include attribution-friendly footer if replies were made (#14), but report is not a PR comment by default (optional later).

## Dependencies

| Dep | Why |
| -- | -- |
| #7 Multi-subagent orchestrator | Aggregate worker results into one report |
| #9 PR babysit cycle | Thread counts, fix outcomes |
| #10 CI taxonomy | `CI class` column semantics |
| #12 Watchlist / state file | Persistent job list, fix_count, residual_blockers |
| #13 Safety guardrails | Never-merge wording enforcement |
| #15 Timeouts / hang recovery | Failed-agent / residual rows |

Soft dependency on #8 (issue→PR) so issue/PR pairing is accurate.

## Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
| -- | -- |
| Stale mergeable/CI at report time | Re-query GitHub at report generation, not only from worker start |
| Overclaiming “healthy” | Checklist-gated definition; any unresolved thread or Class A fail → not healthy |
| False merge language from model | Explicit prompt ban + acceptance test on sample output |
| Huge multi-repo tables | Cap detail in residual blockers (~120 chars); full logs elsewhere |
| Missing GraphQL pagination for threads | Same pagination rules as #9 |

## Implementation plan

1. Define a `JobStatusRow` schema (fields matching table columns + status enum).
2. After cycle join, for each watchlist/worker job: refresh PR/issue via `gh` + GraphQL threads.
3. Map CI checks → Class A/B/C rollup (#10).
4. Classify status (`healthy` / `blocked-external` / …).
5. Render markdown table + summary counts + never-merge note.
6. Add SKILL.md section: “Final status report” with example and column definitions.
7. Manual dry-run against 2–3 live PRs (healthy + blocked + failing) without merging.

## Test / verification plan

* Fixture or recorded `gh` JSON → golden markdown table.
* Prompt/skill review: sample agent output contains zero merge claims.
* Manual: run check on a green PR and a Codacy-gated PR; confirm status split.

## References

* Epic #1 (milestone **C** Safety & ops — C4)
* Related: #9, #10, #12, #13, #15
* Precedent skill: `pr-babysit` success criteria (CI + mergeable + threads)

## Hybrid layer

**Primary implementation layer:** python renderer + Rust status JSON; see #29 R6, #39 P4

This issue remains valid under the **Python/Rust hybrid** architecture (epic #21). Rust owns worktrees, state, process supervision, and hard safety; Python owns orchestration/policy; agent skills document how Grok drives both.

---

Linear: [RM-16](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-16/worktrees-hives-gh16-final-status-report-table) (`RM-16`)

---

GitHub: [https://github.com/rmems/worktrees-hives/issues/16](<https://github.com/rmems/worktrees-hives/issues/16>)

title: [worktrees-hives] GH#15 — Subagent timeouts and hang recovery
description:
## Summary

**Subagent timeouts and hang recovery** for the worktrees-hives orchestrator. Long-running builds and tests (`cargo`, `julia`, CUDA compiles, large test suites across Limen-Neural stacks) can hang or run far past useful wall-clock. The orchestrator must **detect stuck workers**, **recover the hive** (kill / re-dispatch / mark residual), and **report progress** while waiting — without violating safety guardrails (#13).

This issue is **Milestone C3** (Safety & ops) under epic #1. It extends multi-subagent orchestration (#7) with production-grade ops behavior.

## Problem statement

Parallel workers (#7) each run in isolated worktrees (#6).

## Goals

1. **Per-worker timeout policy** (defaults + overrides)
2. **Stuck detection** beyond naive wall-clock when possible (no progress)
3. **Recovery actions:** graceful cancel → kill → re-dispatch **or** mark residual and free the slot
4. **Progress reporting** while the orchestrator waits on the pool
5. **Safe cleanup** of worktrees/processes (no merge, no bare force-push)

## Non-goals

* Replacing GitHub Actions timeouts (remote CI is separate; see #10)
* Perfect global deadlock detection across all tools
* Unlimited automatic re-dispatch loops
* Graphite-specific job control

## Stuck detection

A worker is **stuck** if any of:

1. **Hard timeout:** elapsed ≥ worker/step limit
2. **Idle timeout:** process alive but no heartbeat/output for `idle_seconds`
3. **Orchestrator lost child:** PID/subagent handle gone without terminal status
4. **Repeated identical failure** after re-dispatch budget exhausted

**Heartbeat mechanisms** (platform-dependent):

* Periodic status file write in worktree or state dir
* Last log timestamp from worker stdout/stderr capture
* Explicit “step started / step finished” events in orchestrator channel

## Platform notes

* Define how the parent waits, cancels, and detects hang with the platform's available tools.
* Document fallback if subagent APIs lack kill: mark residual + stop waiting + warn human.
* Multi-platform (#17): each host maps this policy to its native cancellation primitives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Documented **timeout policy** with named defaults and config keys (worker, step, idle, orchestrator, grace)
- [ ] Documented **stuck detection** criteria (hard, idle, lost child, redispatch exhausted)
- [ ] Documented **recovery playbook**: soft cancel → kill → state update → re-dispatch or residual
- [ ] **max_redispatch_per_item** (default 1) prevents infinite retry loops
- [ ] **Progress reporting** while waiting: pool summary + per-job elapsed/step
- [ ] Safety cross-checks: recovery never merges; never bare force-push; no fake SHA replies
- [ ] Watchlist/report fields for timeout residuals specified (#12 / #16)
- [ ] Platform-neutral implementation notes; multi-platform hook for #17
- [ ] Fix-cap interaction defined (timeout does not corrupt fix_count semantics)

## Hybrid layer

**Primary implementation layer:** rust supervisor; see #27 R4

This issue remains valid under the **Python/Rust hybrid** architecture (epic #21). Rust owns worktrees, state, process supervision, and hard safety; Python owns orchestration/policy; agent skills document how agents drive both.

title: [worktrees-hives] GH#14 — Reply attribution config
description:
## Summary

Configurable **reply attribution** for PR review thread replies and summary comments produced by worktrees-hives workers. Humans and other bots must be able to see **which automation stack** responded and, when code changed, **which commit** landed the fix.

**Default identity:**

```text
worktrees-hives agent
```

This issue is **Milestone C2** (Safety & ops) under epic #1. It pairs with babysit reply rules (#9) and safety (#13): attribution is required for transparency; it must not become empty noise.

## Goals

1. **Default attribution string** suitable out of the box
2. **Configurable agent id** so different platforms can set their own label without forking the skill
3. **Commit SHA inclusion** whenever a code fix was pushed before the reply
4. **Consistent templates** for thread replies vs PR-level summary comments

## Non-goals

* Impersonating GitHub Apps or forging another bot’s identity
* Changing Git `user.name` / `user.email` for commits (optional separate config; not required here)
* Auto-resolving threads without a substantive body (#9)
* Merging or approving PRs as a side effect of replying (#13)

## Default behavior

### Attribution line

Every automated reply body should include a clear attribution, typically as a footer or header line:

```markdown
— worktrees-hives agent
```

Pick one style in `SKILL.md` and use it consistently.

### When a code fix landed

After push, reply **must** include the commit SHA:

```text
Addressed in <sha>: <one-line what changed>

— worktrees-hives agent
```

**Ordering rule:** never reply “fixed” before the push succeeds. If push fails, do not claim a SHA.

### When no code change (question / residual / cap)

Still attribute; do **not** invent a SHA:

```text
<substantive technical answer or residual blocker description>

— worktrees-hives agent
```

## Configuration

Support a primary string such as:

| Key | Type | Default | Purpose |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `agent_id` / `attribution` | string | `worktrees-hives agent` | Identity line on replies |
| `include_sha_on_fix` | bool | `true` | Attach SHA after code fixes |
| `attribution_placement` | `footer` | `header` | `footer` | Where the line goes |

Config sources can include:

1. Explicit session flag
2. Env var such as `WORKTREES_HIVES_AGENT_ID`
3. File under `~/.local/share/worktrees-hives/config.json`
4. Built-in default: `worktrees-hives agent`

## Multi-platform examples

| Platform | Example `agent_id` |
| -- | -- |
| Generic default | `worktrees-hives agent` |
| Claude Code | `Claude Code agent: worktrees-hives` |
| Codex | `Codex agent: worktrees-hives` |
| OpenClaw | `OpenClaw agent: worktrees-hives` |

## Reply quality rules

* **No empty acknowledgments**
* **No reply-before-push** for code fixes
* **Actionable fix:** what changed + SHA + attribution
* **Question / design:** answer the technical question; attribution footer
* **Out of scope / Class C CI (#10):** explain residual; do not spam empty commits to re-trigger bots

## Templates

### Thread reply — code fix

```markdown
Addressed in {{sha}}: {{summary}}

— {{agent_id}}
```

### Thread reply — residual / cap

```markdown
{{technical_status}}

Residual: {{blocker}}
Next: {{next_step}}

— {{agent_id}}
```

## Interaction with other issues

| Issue | Interaction |
| -- | -- |
| #9 Babysit | Reply path, GraphQL resolve-after-reply, no empty acks |
| #10 CI taxonomy | Class-specific messaging; avoid spam |
| #12 Watchlist | Config file co-located; optional last reply metadata |
| #13 Safety | Never claim merge; SHA only after successful push |
| #15 Timeouts | If worker killed mid-fix, do not post SHA for unpushed work |
| #16 Report | Attribution string may appear in human report footer |
| #17 Multi-platform | Alternate `agent_id` required for validation |

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Default attribution is configurable and platform-neutral
- [ ] `SKILL.md` documents how to override agent id
- [ ] Reply templates include attribution on all automated thread replies and optional PR comments
- [ ] When a code fix was pushed, reply body includes commit SHA **and** attribution
- [ ] When no code fix, reply includes attribution **without** a fake SHA
- [ ] Ordering: push success → then reply with SHA
- [ ] Multi-platform note: other agents set `agent_id` without forking reply logic

## Hybrid layer

**Primary implementation layer:** python/skill; see #38 P3

This issue remains valid under the **Python/Rust hybrid** architecture (epic #21). Rust owns worktrees, state, process supervision, and hard safety; Python owns orchestration/policy; agent skills document how agents drive both.

title: [worktrees-hives] GH#13 — Safety guardrails (never merge, force-with-lease, fix cap)
description:
## Summary

Hard **safety guardrails** for the worktrees-hives skill: rules that live in `SKILL.md`, orchestrator prompts, and every worker subagent prompt. These are non-negotiable. Agents implement, open/babysit PRs, and report — they **never** merge, never hard-force-push, and never thrash a branch with unbounded fix commits.

This issue is **Milestone C1** (Safety & ops) under epic #1. It codifies the same guardrails proven in the existing `pr-babysit` skill so multi-worker hives cannot escalate risk.

**Scope of enforcement**

* Skill package docs (`SKILL.md` safety section)
* Orchestrator system/worker prompts (platform-neutral, portable wording)
* Optional runtime checks (branch identity, deny-list of commands) if the platform allows
* State/reporting so humans can see when a cap or residual blocked further fixes

## Why this matters

With **multiple parallel subagents** (#7) each holding a worktree (#6), a single mistaken merge or bare `--force` can destroy stacked work or land unreviewed code. A high fix-commit rate also:

* Triggers flaky CI noise and review-bot spam (see CI taxonomy #10)
* Pollutes `git blame` / review history
* Masks real residual blockers that need a human (Codacy gates, third-party reviews)
* Burns API quota and wall-clock without converging

Guardrails make the hive **safe by default** even when a worker is confused or stuck.

## Hard rules (MUST)

### 1. Never merge PRs

Workers and the orchestrator **must not**:

* Call `gh pr merge` (any flags: `--merge`, `--squash`, `--rebase`, `--admin`, `--auto`)
* Call GraphQL/REST merge mutations (`mergePullRequest`, `PUT .../merge`)
* Click/drive UI merge flows
* Enable auto-merge (`gh pr merge --auto`, GraphQL `enablePullRequestAutoMerge`)
* Merge via local `git merge` into the default branch and push to main/master as a substitute for PR merge

**Allowed:** open PR, push commits to the PR head branch, reply to reviews, resolve threads, re-run failed Actions when appropriate, report “merge-ready” status for a **human**.

**Status language:** Final reports (#16) may say `mergeable: MERGEABLE` / `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN` but **must never** claim a merge happened or that the agent merged.

### 2. Force push only with `--force-with-lease`

| Forbidden | Required |
| -- | -- |
| `git push --force` | `git push --force-with-lease` |
| `git push -f` | `git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<expect>` when available |
| `+refs/heads/...` force refspecs without lease | lease-protected push only |

**When force-with-lease is appropriate**

* After `git rebase` onto updated base (plain git stacks, #11)
* After conflict resolution that rewrote local commits
* After intentional history rewrite **on the job’s own PR branch only**

**When not to force-push at all**

* Default branch (`main` / `master` / repo default)
* Someone else’s branch without explicit user override
* Shared long-lived release branches unless the user explicitly requests it

**On lease failure:** do not fall back to bare `--force`. Fetch, inspect, rebase/retry, or mark residual blocker and report.

### 3. Cap 3 code-fix commits per PR per cycle

* **Code-fix commit:** any commit that changes product/test/CI files to address review threads or CI failures during a babysit/check cycle (#9).
* **Cap:** ≤ **3** such commits **per PR per cycle** (one invocation of `check` / `check-all` worker job for that PR).
* **Not counted toward cap:** pure reply comments; GraphQL `resolveReviewThread`; `gh run rerun` without a new commit; documentation-only replies explaining residual blockers; state-file updates.
* **Replies are unlimited** (subject to quality rules: no empty “ack”, no reply-before-push for code fixes — see #9 / #14).
* When the cap is hit and more code work remains: post a **substantive residual** (what’s left, why blocked, suggested human next step), update watchlist `fix_count` / `residual_blockers` (#12), and stop further code commits for that PR in this cycle.

Orchestrator should surface `fix_count` in the final status table (#16).

### 4. Verify correct branch (and worktree) before edits

Before any edit, commit, or push, the worker must confirm:

1. **CWD** is the job’s isolated worktree (#6), not the main checkout of another job
2. `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` matches the expected PR/issue branch
3. `git status -sb` shows the expected upstream (or documents first push)
4. Repo identity is in scope: `rmems/*` or `Limen-Neural/*` unless user override (#1, #5)

**On mismatch:** stop, do not write files, report error to orchestrator. Never “fix” by editing the wrong tree.

### 5. Additional safety (inherit / document in SKILL.md)

Align with proven `pr-babysit` practices:

* Prefer `git add` of intentional paths; avoid blindly staging secrets (`.env`, keys, large artifacts)
* Set `NO_COLOR=1` for `gh api` / GraphQL used in automation
* Do not modify files outside the PR/issue branch worktree
* Do not delete remote branches or close issues/PRs unless the user explicitly asks
* Do not rotate or print credentials; use existing `gh auth`
* Scope: refuse jobs outside allowed owners unless user overrides
* Stacks: push children only after parent handling; force-with-lease only when rewrite needed (#11)

## SKILL.md / prompt placement

Document a dedicated **Safety Guardrails** section that workers see before tool use. Recommended bullets (copy-adapted):

```text
- Never merge PRs (no gh pr merge, no merge API, no auto-merge).
- Never git push --force; only --force-with-lease on the job branch.
- Cap 3 code-fix commits per PR per check cycle; replies unlimited.
- Verify worktree + branch + repo owner before any edit.
- No empty review acks; never reply-before-push for code fixes.
- On fix-cap or unfixable CI class: residual blocker, do not spam commits.
```

Orchestrator must inject the same rules into every subagent brief (not only top-level SKILL.md).

## Interaction with other issues

| Issue | Interaction |
| -- | -- |
| #6 Worktree isolation | Branch verification is meaningless without per-job worktrees |
| #7 Orchestrator | Cap + hang recovery must be enforced across workers |
| #8 Issue→PR | Opens PR only; never merge |
| #9 Babysit | Fix cap and reply-after-push live in the check cycle |
| #10 CI taxonomy | Class B/C failures must not burn the fix cap on noise |
| #11 Stacks | force-with-lease after rebase; ordered processing |
| #12 Watchlist | Persist `fix_count`, residuals |
| #14 Attribution | Safe reply identity; SHA after real push |
| #15 Timeouts | Hung cargo/julia must not lead to panic merges or bare force |
| #16 Report | Never claim merge; show caps/residuals |

## Out of scope

* Implementing merge queues or protected-branch admin bypasses
* Graphite (`gt`) workflows — plain git / optional `gh-stack` only (#1)
* Changing product repos’ branch protection settings
* Softening the never-merge rule via config (if a “allow merge” flag is ever added, it must default off and require explicit user opt-in — not part of this issue’s default behavior)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SKILL.md` (or equivalent skill entry) has an explicit **Safety Guardrails** section covering: never merge, force-with-lease only, 3-fix-commit cap, branch/worktree verification
- [ ] Worker/orchestrator prompt templates include the same rules in platform-neutral form
- [ ] Documented deny-list: `gh pr merge`, bare `git push --force` / `-f`, merge REST/GraphQL, enable auto-merge
- [ ] Documented allow-list for force-with-lease use cases (rebase, conflict rewrite on job branch)
- [ ] Fix-cap semantics defined: what counts, what does not, residual behavior when cap hit
- [ ] Branch/worktree pre-edit checklist documented and referenced by check/issue workflows
- [ ] Cross-links to #9, #10, #11, #12, #16 so implementers do not re-litigate rules
- [ ] Final status guidance: never claim agent merged; surface fix_count / residuals

## Implementation notes (for later coding issues — not this ticket’s code)

When implementing (separate from this description-only work):

1. Prefer **prompt + docs** enforcement first (portable across agents).
2. Where the host allows, add cheap **preflight checks** (branch name, `nameWithOwner`).
3. Optionally wrap git push in a small helper that rejects missing `--force-with-lease` when force is requested — only if packaging (#18) wants a CLI; not required for pure skill docs.
4. Track `fix_count` in watchlist state (#12) so the cap is durable within a cycle and visible to `list` / report.

## Test / verification plan

- [ ] Dry-run checklist: agent refuses merge instruction in a simulated prompt evaluation (manual)
- [ ] Docs review: every “push after rebase” example uses `--force-with-lease`
- [ ] Cap examples: 4th code fix in one cycle → residual reply, no 4th commit
- [ ] Wrong-branch scenario documented: stop and report
- [ ] Report table does not include a “merged by agent” path (#16)

## Definition of done

Safety rules are **written, cross-linked, and implementer-ready** for SKILL.md and worker prompts. No product skill code is required to close this issue if the deliverable is expanded specification + acceptance (implementation may track under #2 / #9); if implementation is in-scope for the same PR as SKILL scaffolding, checklist items above must be satisfied in-repo.

## Hybrid layer

**Primary implementation layer:** rust hard-stops; see #28 R5

This issue remains valid under the **Python/Rust hybrid** architecture (epic #21). Rust owns worktrees, state, process supervision, and hard safety; Python owns orchestration/policy; agent skills document how Grok drives both.

---

---

title: [worktrees-hives] GH#12 — Watchlist / persistent state file
description:
## Summary

Persist **multi-job hive state** across check cycles so operators and agents can `add` / `remove` / `list` / `check-all` without rediscovering the world every session. State lives under `~/.local/share/worktrees-hives/` (XDG data home), supports **multi-owner** repos (`rmems/*` and `Limen-Neural/*`), and records status, stack membership, fix counts, and residual blockers. Milestone **B8**.

## Problem

`pr-babysit` already proves the pattern:

* Path: `~/.local/share/pr-babysit/watched-prs.json`
* Shape: `{ "prs": [ ... ], "groups": { "<stack_id>": [pr_numbers...] } }`
* Fields in the wild: `number`, `repo`, `branch`, `stack_id`, `stack_type`, `stack_position`, `base`, `title`, `added_at`, `last_checked`, `last_status`, `check_count`, `fix_count`

**Limitations to fix in worktrees-hives:**

1. **Single-repo filter** — pr-babysit only processes PRs matching the current checkout’s `nameWithOwner`. The hive is explicitly multi-owner (#5, #7).
2. **No first-class residual blockers** — operators need structured leftovers (CI Class B/C gates from #10, human review, stuck checks).
3. **No** `check-all` **across owners** — need one command to walk the whole watchlist with orchestrator caps (#7) and stack order (#11).
4. **Path namespace** — new skill should not clobber `pr-babysit` state; use `~/.local/share/worktrees-hives/`.

Without durable state, multi-agent cycles lose fix_count budgets, re-add closed PRs, forget stack groups, and cannot produce a trustworthy end-of-cycle report (#16).

## Goals

* Canonical state directory: `~/.local/share/worktrees-hives/` (honor `XDG_DATA_HOME` if set → `$XDG_DATA_HOME/worktrees-hives/`).
* Primary file (recommended): `watched.json` (or `watched-prs.json` — pick one, document it).
* Entry fields at least: `repo`, `number`, `branch`, `stack_id`, `status`, `last_checked`, `fix_count`, `residual_blockers`.
* Multi-owner: store and process `rmems/...` and `Limen-Neural/...` in one file; do not require “current repo only.”
* Commands: `add`, `remove`, `list`, `check-all` (plus optional `check` for a subset).
* Safe concurrent access story (single-writer assumption or file lock); atomic write (temp + rename).
* Compatible with stack groups (#11) and CI residual codes (#10).

## Non-goals

* Cloud sync / multi-machine CRDT state.
* Replacing GitHub Projects or Linear as the system of record for product work.
* Storing git objects or full worktree contents in the state file.
* Migrating every historical `pr-babysit` entry automatically (optional one-shot import is nice-to-have, not required).
* Secrets in the state file (tokens stay in `gh auth` / env).
* Implementing full babysit logic here — state is persistence + command surface; behavior is #7/#9.

## Detailed acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Location & layout**

title: [worktrees-hives] GH#11 — Stack-aware PR ordering
description:
## Summary

When open PRs form a **stack** (a PR’s `baseRefName` is another open PR’s `headRefName`), the hive must **detect the chain** and process **bottom-up**: fix/rebase the parent before the child, and only **force-with-lease** push children after a needed rebase. This is milestone **B7** for worktrees-hives — stack-aware ordering for the orchestrator (#7) and babysit workers (#9). **No Graphite (**`gt`**)**; plain git + optional `gh-stack` only.

## Problem

Stacked PRs are already common on Limen-Neural. Live example on `Limen-Neural/axon-encoder` (open as of research):

| PR | baseRefName | headRefName | Role |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| #36 | `main` | `feat/24-latency-encoder` | stack bottom (latency) |
| #41 | `feat/24-latency-encoder` | `fix-codacy-integration-…` | child of #36 |
| #38 | `main` | `bench/31-scaling-allocations` | stack bottom (bench) |
| #42 | `bench/31-scaling-allocations` | `fix-codacy-benches-…` | child of #38 |

Existing `pr-babysit` state already groups these as `ae-latency: [36, 41]` and `ae-bench: [38, 42]`.

If an agent “babysits” #41 before #36 is healthy and rebased:

* child CI and review SHAs are invalidated by later parent pushes,
* rebases thrash, conflict loops multiply,
* `--force` without lease (or force when unnecessary) risks clobbering remote work,
* parallel workers (#7) can fight over the same stack.

`pr-babysit` documents detection via **API chain walk** on `baseRefName`/`headRefName` and optional `gh stack`, but worktrees-hives needs this as a **first-class scheduling primitive** across multi-owner watchlists — not an optional footnote.

## Goals

* **Detect stacks** with a plain-git/GitHub API chain walk (no Graphite).
* Optionally use `gh-stack` **/** `gh stack` when installed (`stack_type: github`); otherwise `stack_type: null` with the same ordering semantics.
* **Order work bottom-up** (base → tip): parent fix/rebase/CI attention before child.
* After parent history changes, **rebase children** onto updated parent head and push with `--force-with-lease` **only when the rebase rewrote commits that need publishing**.
* Assign stable `stack_id`, `stack_position` (0 = bottom), and group membership for state (#12) and orchestrator (#7).
* Dedupe by `repo + number`; never register half a stack without documenting orphans.

## Non-goals

* Graphite (`gt`) workflows or Graphite-specific metadata.
* Auto-merging the bottom of the stack (never merge — #13).
* Inventing a new stacking product; GitHub PR base/head is the source of truth.
* Cross-repo stacks (out of scope; stacks are per `owner/repo`).
* Replacing operator judgment on intentional non-stack “base is another branch” one-offs — detection should still flag the chain; operator can ungroup if needed.
* Full conflict-resolution UX (shared with #9); this issue owns **order + rebase push policy**.

## Detailed acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Detection (API chain walk)**
  - [ ] Load default branch: `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef`.
  - [ ] Load open PRs: `gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName,baseRefName --limit 200` (paginate if needed).
  - [ ] **Downstack:** while `baseRefName` matches some open PR’s `headRefName`, walk to that parent; stop at default branch or unknown base.
  - [ ] **Upstack:** find PRs whose `baseRefName` equals this PR’s `headRefName`; recurse.
  - [ ] Full connected chain → one `stack_id`; singleton PRs targeting default branch → `stack_id: null`.
  - [ ] Document algorithm in SKILL.md (port from pr-babysit “Stack detection (API chain)”).
- [ ] **Optional gh-stack**
  - [ ] If `gh stack` / gh-stack extension available: may set `stack_type: github` and use `gh stack checkout|rebase|push` for conflict cycles.
  - [ ] If unavailable or exit 8 (locked): retry once after short sleep; fall back to plain git (`stack_type: null`).
  - [ ] Never require Graphite.
- [ ] **Ordering**
  - [ ] Orchestrator / `check-all` processes stack members **ascending** `stack_position` (bottom first).
  - [ ] Child babysit jobs are **blocked or deferred** until parent is not `CONFLICTING` / not mid-rebase, and parent HEAD is the intended merge base (or parent marked residual with explicit operator continue).
  - [ ] Independent stacks and non-stacked PRs remain parallelizable under the global worker cap (#7).
- [ ] **Rebase & push policy**
  - [ ] Plain git path: `git fetch`; `git rebase origin/<parent head or baseRefName>`; resolve; verify build when feasible; `git push --force-with-lease` **only if** history diverged and remote needs update.
  - [ ] Never `git push --force` without `--force-with-lease` (#13).
  - [ ] Do not force-push when a simple fast-forward or no-op would suffice.
  - [ ] After child rebase, refresh any commit SHAs used in review replies (#9).
- [ ] **State integration**
  - [ ] On `add`, auto-detect and register **all** chain members bottom-up; dedupe `number`+`repo`.
  - [ ] Persist `stack_id`, `stack_type`, `stack_position` (and optional `groups` map like pr-babysit).
  - [ ] `list` / report show stack membership clearly.

## Design notes

### Chain walk (reference)

```bash
DEFAULT_BRANCH=$(gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq '.defaultBranchRef.name')
ALL_PRS=$(gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName,baseRefName --limit 200)
```

Pseudocode:

```
parent(pr) = open PR whose headRefName == pr.baseRefName
children(pr) = open PRs whose baseRefName == pr.headRefName

def chain(pr):
  bottom = pr
  while parent(bottom): bottom = parent(bottom)
  # BFS/DFS from bottom via children to collect full set
  return topological_order(bottom → tips)
```

`stack_position`: 0 at bottom (base is default branch or external), increment toward tips.

### Plain git vs gh-stack

| Mode | Checkout | Rebase | Push |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `stack_type: null` | worktree on PR branch (#6) | `git rebase origin/<baseRefName>` | `git push --force-with-lease` if needed |
| `stack_type: github` | `gh stack checkout <n>` | `gh stack rebase` (+ continue) | `gh stack push` |

### Conflict priority

Decision order remains (#9): **MERGED/CLOSED → conflicts → CI → review → threads**. For stacks, **conflict/rebase on parent runs before child’s conflict/CI**, because child merge base depends on parent tip.

### Mapping from pr-babysit

Port sections:

* Commands `add` (auto-detect stack membership),
* State fields `stack_id`, `stack_type`, `stack_position`,
* “Stack detection (API chain)”,
* Conflict resolution GitHub stack vs plain git.

**Difference:** worktrees-hives must not stop at “filter to current repo only” for discovery of chains — detection is still per-repo, but multi-repo orchestrator runs detection **per repo partition**.

### Lessons

* Parent push **invalidates child SHAs** — reply-after-push must re-read `HEAD` post-rebase.
* Parallel workers on parent and child without ordering = thrash; orchestrator partition key should include stack edges (#7).
* `gh stack` exit 8 locked → retry; don’t wedge the hive.

## Dependencies

| Issue | Relationship |
| -- | -- |
| #1 Epic | Parent epic |
| #2 SKILL.md | Document stack detect + order |
| #6 Worktrees | Rebase/fix happens in job worktree |
| #7 Orchestrator | **Scheduler consumer** of stack edges |
| #9 Babysit | Conflict/CI cycle respects order |
| #12 Watchlist | Persists stack_id/position/groups |
| #13 Safety | force-with-lease only; never merge |
| #16 Report | Show stack column / ordering |

**Hard prerequisites:** #6 (safe branch ops), #7 or #9 as execution context. **State:** #12. **Safety:** #13.

## Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
| -- | -- |
| Base branch name collision (two PRs same head name) | Dedupe by repo; head names unique per repo in practice; if not, prefer open PR match + warn |
| Closed parent mid-stack | Treat as broken chain; residual; do not infinite-walk |
| Deep stacks + fix cap | Cap still per-PR; process bottom first so cap is spent usefully |
| Unnecessary force-with-lease | Compare `@{u}` before push; skip if up to date |
| gh-stack lock (exit 8) | Retry once; fall back to plain git |
| Agent rebases child onto wrong remote ref | Always `git fetch origin`; rebase onto `origin/<baseRefName>` |
| Parallel multi-repo OK, parallel same-stack bad | Orchestrator serializes stack members (#7) |

## Planning order (implementation sequence)

1. Spec chain-walk + field schema in SKILL.md (copy/adapt pr-babysit).
2. Implement detect + assign `stack_id`/`position` on `add` / discover.
3. Enforce bottom-up order in orchestrator queue (#7).
4. Implement plain-git rebase path with force-with-lease gating.
5. Optional gh-stack path + exit 8 retry.
6. Surface stacks in `list` and #16 report.

**Milestone:** B7 (stack-aware PR ordering; pairs with orchestrator B3 and watchlist B8).

## Hybrid layer

**Primary implementation layer:** python (or hybrid); see #37 P2

title: Stack-aware PR ordering
description:
## Summary

When open PRs form a **stack** (a PR’s `baseRefName` is another open PR’s `headRefName`), the hive must **detect the chain** and process **bottom-up**: fix/rebase the parent before the child, and only **force-with-lease** push children after a needed rebase. This is milestone **B7** for worktrees-hives — stack-aware ordering for the orchestrator (#7) and babysit workers (#9). **No Graphite (**`gt`**)**; plain git + optional `gh-stack` only.

## Problem

Stacked PRs are already common on Limen-Neural. Live example on `Limen-Neural/axon-encoder` (open as of research):

| PR | baseRefName | headRefName | Role |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| #36 | `main` | `feat/24-latency-encoder` | stack bottom (latency) |
| #41 | `feat/24-latency-encoder` | `fix-codacy-integration-…` | child of #36 |
| #38 | `main` | `bench/31-scaling-allocations` | stack bottom (bench) |
| #42 | `bench/31-scaling-allocations` | `fix-codacy-benches-…` | child of #38 |

Existing `pr-babysit` state already groups these as `ae-latency: [36, 41]` and `ae-bench: [38, 42]`.

If an agent “babysits” #41 before #36 is healthy and rebased:

* child CI and review SHAs are invalidated by later parent pushes,
* rebases thrash, conflict loops multiply,
* `--force` without lease (or force when unnecessary) risks clobbering remote work,
* parallel workers (#7) can fight over the same stack.

`pr-babysit` documents detection via **API chain walk** on `baseRefName`/`headRefName` and optional `gh stack`, but worktrees-hives needs this as a **first-class scheduling primitive** across multi-owner watchlists — not an optional footnote.

## Goals

* **Detect stacks** with a plain-git/GitHub API chain walk (no Graphite).
* Optionally use `gh-stack` **/** `gh stack` when installed (`stack_type: github`); otherwise `stack_type: null` with the same ordering semantics.
* **Order work bottom-up** (base → tip): parent fix/rebase/CI attention before child.
* After parent history changes, **rebase children** onto updated parent head and push with `--force-with-lease` **only when the rebase rewrote commits that need publishing**.
* Assign stable `stack_id`, `stack_position` (0 = bottom), and group membership for state (#12) and orchestrator (#7).
* Dedupe by `repo + number`; never register half a stack without documenting orphans.

## Non-goals

* Graphite (`gt`) workflows or Graphite-specific metadata.
* Auto-merging the bottom of the stack (never merge — #13).
* Inventing a new stacking product; GitHub PR base/head is the source of truth.
* Cross-repo stacks (out of scope; stacks are per `owner/repo`).
* Replacing operator judgment on intentional non-stack “base is another branch” one-offs — detection should still flag the chain; operator can ungroup if needed.
* Full conflict-resolution UX (shared with #9); this issue owns **order + rebase push policy**.

## Detailed acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Detection (API chain walk)**
  - [ ] Load default branch: `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef`.
  - [ ] Load open PRs: `gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName,baseRefName --limit 200` (paginate if needed).
  - [ ] **Downstack:** while `baseRefName` matches some open PR’s `headRefName`, walk to that parent; stop at default branch or unknown base.
  - [ ] **Upstack:** find PRs whose `baseRefName` equals this PR’s `headRefName`; recurse.
  - [ ] Full connected chain → one `stack_id`; singleton PRs targeting default branch → `stack_id: null`.
  - [ ] Document algorithm in SKILL.md (port from pr-babysit “Stack detection (API chain)”).
- [ ] **Optional gh-stack**
  - [ ] If `gh stack` / gh-stack extension available: may set `stack_type: github` and use `gh stack checkout|rebase|push` for conflict cycles.
  - [ ] If unavailable or exit 8 (locked): retry once after short sleep; fall back to plain git (`stack_type: null`).
  - [ ] Never require Graphite.
- [ ] **Ordering**
  - [ ] Orchestrator / `check-all` processes stack members **ascending** `stack_position` (bottom first).
  - [ ] Child babysit jobs are **blocked or deferred** until parent is not `CONFLICTING` / not mid-rebase, and parent HEAD is the intended merge base (or parent marked residual with explicit operator continue).
  - [ ] Independent stacks and non-stacked PRs remain parallelizable under the global worker cap (#7).
- [ ] **Rebase & push policy**
  - [ ] Plain git path: `git fetch`; `git rebase origin/<parent head or baseRefName>`; resolve; verify build when feasible; `git push --force-with-lease` **only if** history diverged and remote needs update.
  - [ ] Never `git push --force` without `--force-with-lease` (#13).
  - [ ] Do not force-push when a simple fast-forward or no-op would suffice.
  - [ ] After child rebase, refresh any commit SHAs used in review replies (#9).
- [ ] **State integration**
  - [ ] On `add`, auto-detect and register **all** chain members bottom-up; dedupe `number`+`repo`.
  - [ ] Persist `stack_id`, `stack_type`, `stack_position` (and optional `groups` map like pr-babysit).
  - [ ] `list` / report show stack membership clearly.

## Design notes

### Chain walk (reference)

```bash
DEFAULT_BRANCH=$(gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq '.defaultBranchRef.name')
ALL_PRS=$(gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName,baseRefName --limit 200)
```

Pseudocode:

```
parent(pr) = open PR whose headRefName == pr.baseRefName
children(pr) = open PRs whose baseRefName == pr.headRefName

def chain(pr):
  bottom = pr
  while parent(bottom): bottom = parent(bottom)
  # BFS/DFS from bottom via children to collect full set
  return topological_order(bottom → tips)
```

`stack_position`: 0 at bottom (base is default branch or external), increment toward tips.

### Plain git vs gh-stack

| Mode | Checkout | Rebase | Push |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `stack_type: null` | worktree on PR branch (#6) | `git rebase origin/<baseRefName>` | `git push --force-with-lease` if needed |
| `stack_type: github` | `gh stack checkout <n>` | `gh stack rebase` (+ continue) | `gh stack push` |

### Conflict priority

Decision order remains (#9): **MERGED/CLOSED → conflicts → CI → review → threads**. For stacks, **conflict/rebase on parent runs before child’s conflict/CI**, because child merge base depends on parent tip.

### Mapping from pr-babysit

Port sections:

* Commands `add` (auto-detect stack membership),
* State fields `stack_id`, `stack_type`, `stack_position`,
* “Stack detection (API chain)”,
* Conflict resolution GitHub stack vs plain git.

**Difference:** worktrees-hives must not stop at “filter to current repo only” for discovery of chains — detection is still per-repo, but multi-repo orchestrator runs detection **per repo partition**.

### Lessons

* Parent push **invalidates child SHAs** — reply-after-push must re-read `HEAD` post-rebase.
* Parallel workers on parent and child without ordering = thrash; orchestrator partition key should include stack edges (#7).
* `gh stack` exit 8 locked → retry; don’t wedge the hive.

## Dependencies

| Issue | Relationship |
| -- | -- |
| #1 Epic | Parent epic |
| #2 SKILL.md | Document stack detect + order |
| #6 Worktrees | Rebase/fix happens in job worktree |
| #7 Orchestrator | **Scheduler consumer** of stack edges |
| #9 Babysit | Conflict/CI cycle respects order |
| #12 Watchlist | Persists stack_id/position/groups |
| #13 Safety | force-with-lease only; never merge |
| #16 Report | Show stack column / ordering |

**Hard prerequisites:** #6 (safe branch ops), #7 or #9 as execution context. **State:** #12. **Safety:** #13.

## Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
| -- | -- |
| Base branch name collision (two PRs same head name) | Dedupe by repo; head names unique per repo in practice; if not, prefer open PR match + warn |
| Closed parent mid-stack | Treat as broken chain; residual; do not infinite-walk |
| Deep stacks + fix cap | Cap still per-PR; process bottom first so cap is spent usefully |
| Unnecessary force-with-lease | Compare `@{u}` before push; skip if up to date |
| gh-stack lock (exit 8) | Retry once; fall back to plain git |
| Agent rebases child onto wrong remote ref | Always `git fetch origin`; rebase onto `origin/<baseRefName>` |
| Parallel multi-repo OK, parallel same-stack bad | Orchestrator serializes stack members (#7) |

## Planning order (implementation sequence)

1. Spec chain-walk + field schema in SKILL.md (copy/adapt pr-babysit).
2. Implement detect + assign `stack_id`/`position` on `add` / discover.
3. Enforce bottom-up order in orchestrator queue (#7).
4. Implement plain-git rebase path with force-with-lease gating.
5. Optional gh-stack path + exit 8 retry.
6. Surface stacks in `list` and #16 report.

**Milestone:** B7 (stack-aware PR ordering; pairs with orchestrator B3 and watchlist B8).

## Hybrid layer

**Primary implementation layer:** python (or hybrid); see #37 P2

This issue remains valid under the **Python/Rust hybrid** architecture (epic #21). Rust owns worktrees, state, process supervision, and hard safety; Python owns orchestration/policy; agent skills document how Grok drives both.

title: [worktrees-hives] GH#10 — CI taxonomy (Actions vs Codacy vs third-party)
description:
## Summary

Classify CI and status-check failures so babysit workers **fix what is fixable**, **rerun flaky Actions when appropriate**, and **never spam empty commits** to “kick” third-party review bots. This is the **check-decision brain** for worktrees-hives (milestone **B6**): it turns `gh pr checks` / `statusCheckRollup` into actionable classes used by the PR babysit cycle (#9) and final status reporting (#16).

## Problem

Limen-Neural and rmems PRs report a **heterogeneous rollup** of:

* **GitHub Actions** jobs (workflow set: `CI`, `Audit`, `Coverage`, `CodeQL`, `Docker`, `reviewdog`, …),
* **Azure Pipelines** multi-OS builds (e.g. `Limen-Neural.neuromod (BuildTest linux|mac|windows)`),
* **Codacy** GitHub App checks (`Codacy Static Code Analysis` → `app.codacy.com`),
* **Third-party review apps** with little or no fixable log surface: **Kilo Code Review** (`app.kilo.ai`), **CodeRabbit** (often a `StatusContext`), **Gitar**, plus review-thread bots (Devin, Macroscope, Codex, Qodo, Semgrep).

Today `pr-babysit` treats “not green” roughly uniformly: dig into logs, fix, push, or comment. That causes bad agent behavior:

1. **Noise commits** that only exist to re-trigger Kilo/CodeRabbit/Codacy.
2. **Burning the 3-fix/cycle cap** on gates the agent cannot close (human quality gate, external bot still running, stuck `Expected` check).
3. **Missing real fixes** when Class A Actions failures (`clippy`, `fmt`, tests, `rustsec`) are mixed with Class C residual noise.
4. Confusion around GitHub conclusions such as `ACTION_REQUIRED` (documented check conclusion = “required actions upon completion”) — common for quality/security apps that want human or in-app action, not another empty push.

`gh pr checks <n> --json name,state,bucket,workflow,link` already buckets state into `pass | fail | pending | skipping | cancel`. Taxonomy must sit **on top of** that: map each row (and each `statusCheckRollup` entry) into Class A/B/C (+ pending/skip) and a **policy**.

### Empirical fixtures (live org patterns)

| Source | Example names | Signals |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Class A (Actions) | `Build & Test`, `Validate, Test & Doc`, `rustsec`, `trivy`, `reviewdog`, `Codecov`, `Analyze (rust)`, `docker`, `Code Coverage` | `workflow` non-empty; `detailsUrl` under `github.com/.../actions/runs/...` |
| Class A (Azure) | `Limen-Neural.<repo> (BuildTest linux\|mac\|windows)` | `dev.azure.com/...` links; treat like fixable build/test when logs accessible |
| Class B | `Codacy Static Code Analysis` | App **Codacy Production**; link `https://app.codacy.com/gh/<owner>/<repo>/pull-requests/<n>` |
| Class C | `Kilo Code Review`, `CodeRabbit`, `Gitar` | Apps/links on `kilo.ai` / empty `StatusContext` / `gitar.ai`; no useful Actions log |
| Skip / non-blocking | `Supabase Preview` (`SKIPPED`) | `bucket: skipping` — do not fail the cycle |

Success criteria inherited from pr-babysit: all checks whose conclusion is not `FAILURE` / `ERROR` / `ACTION_REQUIRED` (plus mergeable/review/thread rules owned by #9).

## Goals

* Define **Class A / B / C** (and how **pending** / **skipping** / **cancel** interact).
* Document **classification rules** agents can apply from `gh pr checks` JSON + optional GraphQL/`statusCheckRollup` (CheckRun vs StatusContext).
* For each class: **allowed actions**, **forbidden actions**, when to use `gh run rerun`, when to mark **residual human gate**.
* Prefer **real code fixes** or **official reruns** over empty “chore: retrigger CI” commits.
* Feed residual blockers into watchlist state (#12) and final report (#16).
* Stay compatible with fix cap (#13: ≤3 code-fix commits per PR per cycle).

## Non-goals

* Implementing the full babysit thread GraphQL loop (owned by #9) — this issue owns **CI classification policy**, not thread replies.
* Auto-bypassing branch protection or dismissing required checks.
* Replacing Codacy/Kilo product UIs; no API key harvest for third-party dashboards unless already available to the operator.
* Inventing Graphite-style CI orchestration.
* Perfect flaky-test ML; simple rerun budget is enough.
* Changing product CI configs across all Limen-Neural repos (may *suggest* workflow fixes as Class A patches when the failure is in-repo YAML).

## Detailed acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Class A — fixable first-party CI (Actions / Azure build-test)**
  - [ ] Recognizes common names/workflows: test, fmt/format, clippy/lint, rustsec/audit, build, coverage upload failures caused by compile/test, docker build when Dockerfile is in-repo.
  - [ ] On `bucket: fail`: fetch logs (`gh run view <id> --log-failed` when Actions; best-effort for Azure), diagnose, fix in worktree, commit, push (counts toward fix cap).
  - [ ] On likely **flake** (same job passed on prior SHA / intermittent timeout, no code signal): prefer `gh run rerun <run-id>` (or rerun-failed) **once** before writing a code change.
  - [ ] Does **not** open empty commits solely to retrigger Class A.
- [ ] **Class B — Codacy quality gates**
  - [ ] Identifies `Codacy Static Code Analysis` (and related Codacy coverage gates if present) via name and/or `app.codacy.com` link.
  - [ ] When Codacy surfaces **actionable annotations** / review threads with concrete file+line issues: fix real findings (same path as review threads in #9); then push + reply with SHA.
  - [ ] When conclusion is `ACTION_REQUIRED`, fail with only dashboard-level gate, or issues are style/threshold policy the agent cannot change: **document residual human gate** (do not loop empty pushes).
  - [ ] Never “fix” Codacy solely by force-pushing the same tree.
- [ ] **Class C — third-party review status (Kilo, CodeRabbit, Gitar, …)**
  - [ ] Identifies by name/link/app (`Kilo Code Review`, `CodeRabbit`, `Gitar`, similar).
  - [ ] **No empty re-trigger commits** to wake these bots.
  - [ ] If the bot left **inline review threads**, handle via #9 thread workflow (substantive fix or reply); status check itself may remain pending/fail as residual.
  - [ ] Pending Class C does not block fixing Class A in the same cycle.
- [ ] **Cross-cutting policy**
  - [ ] Taxonomy table lives in SKILL.md (or linked design doc in skill package) with examples from Limen-Neural check names.
  - [ ] Classifier inputs documented: at minimum `gh pr checks --json name,state,bucket,workflow,link` plus rollup `conclusion` when needed for `ACTION_REQUIRED`.
  - [ ] `skipping` / `SKIPPED` checks are non-blocking.
  - [ ] `pending` checks: status `pending`; continue other work; do not spam reruns.
  - [ ] Residual blockers recorded as structured strings suitable for #12 / #16 (e.g. `class_b:codacy_action_required`, `class_c:kilo_pending`).
  - [ ] Explicit rule: **prefer real fixes or** `gh run rerun` **over noise commits**.

## Design notes

### Classification algorithm (recommended)

```text
for each check in gh pr checks --json ...:
  if bucket in (pass, skipping): ignore (non-actionable success/skip)
  if bucket == pending: mark pending; continue
  if bucket == cancel: optional single rerun if Actions; else residual
  if name/link matches Codacy → Class B
  else if name/link matches Kilo|CodeRabbit|Gitar|similar review SaaS → Class C
  else if workflow non-empty OR link contains github.com/.../actions OR dev.azure.com buildtest → Class A
  else → Class C (unknown third-party; conservative: no empty push)
```

Refine with `statusCheckRollup`: `__typename` `CheckRun` vs `StatusContext`; `conclusion` for `ACTION_REQUIRED`.

## Hybrid layer

**Primary implementation layer:** python policy; see #38 P3

This issue remains valid under the **Python/Rust hybrid** architecture (epic #21). Rust owns worktrees, state, process supervision, and hard safety; Python owns orchestration/policy; agent skills document how agents drive both.

title: [worktrees-hives] GH#9 — PR babysit cycle (threads + CI)
description:
## Summary

Babysit open PRs until they are **merge-ready for a human**: resolve **inline review threads** and **CI failures**, push fixes, **reply with commit SHAs**, resolve threads — and **never merge**. This is milestone **B5**, the direct generalization of `~/.agents/skills/pr-babysit/SKILL.md` into the multi-repo worktrees-hives worker (`pr_babysit`), usually running under the capped orchestrator (#7) inside an isolated worktree (#6).

## Problem

Review bots and CI leave PRs half-done: unresolved threads, red checks, conflicts. `pr-babysit` already encodes a solid single-repo loop, but worktrees-hives must:

* run that loop **across many repos in parallel**,
* enforce the same **safety caps** (3 code-fix commits/PR/cycle, never merge),
* avoid known failure modes from production babysit runs:
  * **hangs** on long `cargo` / Julia verification,
  * **empty CI re-trigger commits** that add noise and anger reviewers,
  * **stale SHAs in replies** after force-with-lease / rebase.

Without a codified babysit worker, issue→PR (#8) dumps unfinished PRs with no consistent follow-through.

## Goals

* One **check cycle** per PR (repeatable until healthy or residual-blocked).
* **Decision order** aligned with pr-babysit:
  1. MERGED/CLOSED → drop / report
  2. Conflicts → resolve first
  3. CI failed → fix from logs (within fix cap)
  4. Changes requested → address if actionable
  5. Unresolved review threads → **always** process
  6. Pending CI → status `pending`, do not block other thread work unnecessarily
  7. All green → `healthy`
* **GraphQL** fetch of review threads with **pagination**, `NO_COLOR=1`, ANSI strip.
* Actionable threads: **fix → push → reply with SHA → resolve** (never reply-before-push for code fixes).
* Cap **3 code-fix commits per PR per cycle**; thread **replies unlimited**.
* Substantive replies only (no “ack” / “will fix”).
* Never merge; force push only with `--force-with-lease`.
* Integrate with CI taxonomy (#10) when available; until then, prefer real fixes or `gh run rerun` over noop commits.

## Non-goals

* Merging PRs or enabling auto-merge.
* Unlimited fix commits in one cycle (cap = 3 code fixes).
* Graphite (`gt`).
* Pretending Class C third-party gates are green via empty commits (#10).
* Final operator table polish (#16) — emit fields the table will need.
* Inventing new review bots’ slash commands beyond what pr-babysit already documents (Semgrep `/fp`, `/ar`, `/other`, etc.).

## Detailed acceptance criteria

### Cycle & queries

- [ ] Load PR: `gh pr view` with `state`, `mergeable`, `mergeStateStatus`, `statusCheckRollup`, `reviewDecision`, `headRefName`, `baseRefName`.
- [ ] Load checks: `gh pr checks` (name, state, link).
- [ ] Operate in the PR branch worktree (#6); verify branch before edits.
- [ ] `git fetch origin` at cycle start.

### Conflicts

- [ ] If `CONFLICTING` / `DIRTY`, rebase onto base (plain git or `gh stack` when `stack_type: github`).
- [ ] Resolve markers fully; verify build within time budget; push `--force-with-lease` when history rewrote.
- [ ] Stack-aware: prefer parent health first (#11).

### CI failures

- [ ] For each failed check, pull logs (`gh run view <id> --log-failed`) and diagnose.
- [ ] Apply real fixes; commit; push; optional PR comment summarizing the fix.
- [ ] Count toward **3 code-fix commits / PR / cycle**.
- [ ] **Do not** push empty or whitespace-only “re-trigger CI” commits.
- [ ] Prefer `gh run rerun` (or waiting) when failure is flake/infra and no code change is justified (#10).
- [ ] When Class B/C gates need humans, record residual blockers instead of thrashing.

### Review threads (mandatory)

- [ ] Fetch **all** threads via GraphQL pagination (pattern from pr-babysit; `NO_COLOR=1`; strip ANSI).
- [ ] For every `isResolved == false`:
  - [ ] **Actionable + under fix cap:** code fix → push → reply including **post-push** `git rev-parse HEAD` SHA → resolve thread.
  - [ ] **Fix cap reached:** substantive technical reply describing the needed change; do not skip the thread.
  - [ ] **Question / out of scope:** substantive explanation (not empty ack).
  - [ ] **Semgrep FP:** use documented slash commands when applicable.
- [ ] **Never reply before pushing** a claimed code fix.
- [ ] Resolve via `resolveReviewThread` mutation after replying when policy says resolve.

### Success / residual

- [ ] Healthy when: CI not failing, mergeable clean (or residual noted if only external gates), no unresolved threads left that the worker should have handled, `reviewDecision` not stuck on unaddressed `CHANGES_REQUESTED`.
- [ ] Residual blockers listed explicitly (Codacy human gate, pending CI, cap exhausted, hang timeout, etc.).
- [ ] **Never** report success as “merged.”

### Safety (also #13)

- [ ] No merge commands/APIs.
- [ ] Force only with `--force-with-lease`.
- [ ] Fix cap 3 code commits / PR / cycle; replies uncapped.
- [ ] Correct branch check before edits.

### Documentation

- [ ] SKILL.md embeds or links the babysit cycle, GraphQL snippets, fix cap, reply-after-push rule.
- [ ] Cross-links #7, #8, #10, #11, #13, #14 (attribution), #15 (timeouts).

## Design notes

### Grounding: pr-babysit patterns (must preserve)

| Pattern | Rule |
| -- | -- |
| Thread GraphQL | Paginate `reviewThreads`; include `isResolved`, thread `id`, comment `databaseId`, path, body |
| Fix commits / cycle | **Max 3** code-fix commits per PR per cycle |
| Never merge | Babysit only; human merges |
| Reply after push | Push first; reply with **current** SHA; then resolve |
| `NO_COLOR=1` | All `gh api` / GraphQL for stable parsing |
| Force push | `--force-with-lease` only |
| Bots seen in rmems / Limen-Neural | Codacy, Devin, Kilo, CodeRabbit, Macroscope, Codex, Qodo, Semgrep |

### Decision order (reference)

Same as pr-babysit SKILL.md “Decision order” — conflicts before CI before threads is preferred for fewer wasted fixes; still process threads every cycle when present.

### Lessons learned (must encode)

1. **Hang on cargo / Julia**
   Local verify and long test suites can stall the worker. Use wall-clock budgets; on hang, kill/mark residual (#15) rather than blocking the orchestrator slot forever. Do not treat “still compiling” as healthy.
2. **Empty CI re-triggers are bad**
   Noop commits pollute history, retrigger expensive matrices, and look like spam. If CI needs a kick without code changes, use `gh run rerun` or wait for the provider. Taxonomy in #10 (Class A fixable Actions vs B Codacy vs C third-party).
3. **Force-push invalidates SHAs**
   After `rebase` + `--force-with-lease`, any SHA captured earlier is wrong. Always:

   ```bash
   git push --force-with-lease
   COMMIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
   # then reply with $COMMIT_SHA
   ```

   Never reply with a pre-rebase SHA. Orchestrator must not cache handoff SHAs across babysit pushes.

### Reply shape (suggested)

```text
Addressed in <full_or_short_sha>: <one-line technical summary of the change>
```

With attribution when #14 lands (default e.g. `worktrees-hives agent`).

### GraphQL thread fetch (canonical sketch)

Reuse the paginated query from pr-babysit (owner, name, number, cursor; `reviewThreads(first: 50)`; comments with `databaseId`). Write threads to a temp JSON file; iterate unresolved only.

### Reply + resolve

```bash
# after push
COMMIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
NO_COLOR=1 gh api repos/{OWNER}/{REPO}/pulls/{number}/comments/{databaseId}/replies \
  -X POST -f body="Addressed in ${COMMIT_SHA}: <what changed>"

NO_COLOR=1 gh api graphql -f query='
mutation($threadId: ID!) {
  resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: $threadId}) {
    thread { isResolved }
  }
}' -f threadId="<thread_id>"
```

### State fields (for #12)

## Dependencies

| Issue | Relationship |
| -- | -- |
| #1 Epic | Parent |
| #6 Worktree | **Hard** isolation for fixes |
| #7 Orchestrator | Dispatches `pr_babysit` jobs; join/report |
| #8 Issue → PR | Upstream producer of PRs to babysit |
| #10 CI taxonomy | Classifies fix vs residual vs rerun |
| #11 Stack ordering | Parent before child when stacked |
| #12 Watchlist | Persist multi-PR multi-owner state |
| #13 Safety | Caps, never-merge, force-with-lease |
| #14 Reply attribution | Configurable identity on replies |
| #15 Timeouts | Hang recovery during verify/CI fix loops |
| #16 Status report | Consumes cycle outcomes |

| Risk | Mitigation |
| -- | -- |

| Empty re-trigger commit spam | Ban noop commits; #10 + `gh run rerun` |
| Exceeding fix cap silently | Track `fix_count`; switch to reply-only |
| Resolving threads without substance | Require technical reply body |
| Merging by habit from other skills | Explicit never-merge; no merge in success criteria |
| Stack child thrash | #11 bottom-up schedule |
| ANSI/color breaking JSON parse | `NO_COLOR=1` + sed strip |

2. Worktree checkout of PR branch (#6).
3. Implement one full cycle on a pilot PR (single repo).
4. Wire as orchestrator worker type (#7) with result aggregation.
5. Add CI taxonomy hooks (#10) and stack ordering (#11).

* CI conclusions not `FAILURE` / `ERROR` / `ACTION_REQUIRED` (pending may be `pending` status)

* Every bot/human thread fixed in code or answered substantively
